entries.content:
# When saves get large

Hundreds of items in a backpack, thousands of log entries and events, a whole map: this exceeds the 16 KB that `ctx.state` holds. The platform already provides what you need, so do not build your own storage. Split the data by kind into private files (128 MB per app), and use `ctx.state` only as an index that records which file currently holds each kind. The problems to solve are not space but the time SD card writes take, and keeping several files consistent with each other. This page provides a `store.lua` module you can copy as is.

## First estimate whether to split

For the basics, see "Saving and loading". First, estimate the size of the save as JSON for the player who plays longest:

| Save size | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Always under 8 KB | Keep everything in `ctx.state`; you do not need this page |
| Only one thing grows, such as history | Put that one thing in a file and cap its count ("Large data goes in private files" in "Saving and loading") |
| Several things grow: backpack, quests, logs, map, several save slots | Split the data into files as this page describes |

When estimating: a Chinese character takes 3 bytes; one entry `{ t = 123, msg = "Defeated a slime" }` is about 40 bytes as JSON; a thousand entries is 40 KB.

Limits and speeds (contract sections 9 and 10, reference values measured on Gancao firmware):

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.state` | 16 KB |
| One private file | 256 KB, up to 512 files, 128 MB in total |
| Writing a 4 KB file | about 120 ms on X4 Pro, about 30 ms on X4 Classic |
| Deleting a file | about 70 ms on X4 Pro |
| JSON encode or decode | about 1.6 µs per byte on X4 Pro, about 100 ms for 64 KB |
| One callback | 1000 ms, 2000 ms for `on_load` |

Space is rarely the limit; time is. Keep each file between a few KB and a dozen or so KB, write only what changed, and write one or two files per callback.

## How to split: ctx.state as the index, one file per kind

- Data that changes together belongs in the same kind. When a purchase changes both gold and items, put the gold in the backpack file too, rather than half in `ctx.state` and half in a file.
- Data that only grows (logs, events, chat, match records) is split into chunks by count, one file per chunk; see below.
- Large, sparse data such as a map is split by area, for example one chunk per 16×16 cells, and only visited areas are stored.
- For several save slots, use one set of kind names per slot, such as `s1bag` and `s2bag`.
- Small data such as the current level, settings, and the slot in use stays in `ctx.state`.

File names use only lowercase letters, digits and `._-`, 1 to 64 bytes (section 9). The module below names files "kind.generation.json", such as `bag.3.json`, so kind names use only lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, and must not be all digits (a key `"12"` in `ctx.state` comes back as the integer 12). Do not give other private files this "name.number.json" form, or `cleanup` deletes them as stale. The index itself is stored in `ctx.state`, so keep the number of kinds to a few dozen; the index then takes only a few KB.

## store.lua: write only what changed, a few files at a time

```lua
-- store.lua: one file per kind of large data; ctx.state.files records which file each kind uses now
local M = {}
local PER_FLUSH = 2          -- at most this many files per callback; use 1 for large files
local DELAY = 300            -- how long after a change to start writing (ms)

local data = {}              -- loaded into memory: data[kind] = table
local dirty = {}             -- changed, not yet written: dirty[kind] = true
local timer
M.error = nil                -- error name of the last failed write

local function index(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.files = s.files or {}    -- s.files.bag = { name = "bag.3.json", gen = 3 }
  return s.files
end

-- get one kind; read the file on first use, fall back to fresh() when missing or damaged
function M.get(ctx, kind, fresh)
  if data[kind] then return data[kind] end
  local f = index(ctx)[kind]
  local t
  if f then
    local raw = ctx.storage:read(f.name)
    t = raw and ctx.json:decode(raw)
  end
  if type(t) ~= "table" then t = fresh() end
  data[kind] = t
  return t
end

-- call after changing a kind: note it, write it a little later
function M.touch(ctx, kind)
  dirty[kind] = true
  if not timer then timer = ctx:after(DELAY, function(ctx) M.flush(ctx) end) end
end

-- write to a new file name, never over the old one; returns true and the old name
local function write(ctx, kind)
  local files = index(ctx)
  local old = files[kind]
  local gen = (old and old.gen or 0) + 1
  local name = kind .. "." .. gen .. ".json"
  local text, err = ctx.json:encode(data[kind])
  if not text then return nil, err end
  local ok, werr = ctx.storage:write(name, text)
  if not ok then return nil, werr end
  files[kind] = { name = name, gen = gen }
  return true, old and old.name
end

-- write up to limit changed kinds, then switch to the new names with one save_state
function M.flush(ctx, limit)
  if timer then timer:cancel(); timer = nil end
  limit = limit or PER_FLUSH
  local olds, n = {}, 0
  for kind in pairs(dirty) do
    if n == limit then break end
    local ok, r = write(ctx, kind)
    if not ok then M.error = r; break end
    dirty[kind] = nil
    olds[#olds + 1] = r
    n = n + 1
  end
  if n > 0 then
    local ok, err = ctx:save_state()
    if ok then
      for _, name in ipairs(olds) do ctx.storage:remove(name) end
      M.error = nil
    else
      M.error = err
    end
  end
  if next(dirty) then timer = ctx:after(DELAY, function(ctx) M.flush(ctx) end) end
end

-- a kind no longer needed: remove it from the index; cleanup deletes the file
function M.drop(ctx, kind)
  index(ctx)[kind] = nil
  data[kind], dirty[kind] = nil, nil
end

-- release a kind that was read but not changed
function M.forget(kind)
  if not dirty[kind] then data[kind] = nil end
end

-- call in on_load: delete old files the index no longer names, at most max each time
function M.cleanup(ctx, max)
  local keep = {}
  for _, f in pairs(index(ctx)) do keep[f.name] = true end
  local n = 0
  for _, name in ipairs(ctx.storage:list()) do
    if n == (max or 3) then break end
    if name:match("^[a-z0-9_-]+%.%d+%.json$") and not keep[name] then
      ctx.storage:remove(name)
      n = n + 1
    end
  end
end

return M
```

Usage:

```lua
local store = require("store")
local function new_bag() return { v = 1, gold = 0, items = {} } end

local function bag(ctx)
  local b = store.get(ctx, "bag", new_bag)
  b.gold = b.gold + 0.0                  -- numbers read from JSON may be integers: back to float
  return b
end

function on_load(ctx)
  store.cleanup(ctx)                     -- not on the lock screen
end

local function buy(ctx, id, price)
  local b = bag(ctx)
  if b.gold < price then return false end
  b.gold = b.gold - price
  b.items[id] = (b.items[id] or 0) + 1
  store.touch(ctx, "bag")
  store.flush(ctx)                       -- money was spent: write now
  return true
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  store.flush(ctx)                       -- write one more batch of what is left
end
```

- After a change, you normally call only `touch`. The module writes 300 ms later, at most two files at a time, and schedules the rest for the next timer. Hundreds of consecutive changes result in only a few writes.
- Call `flush` immediately after actions that must not be lost (spending money, clearing a level, collecting a reward).
- `on_leave` also has only 1000 ms, and `ctx.budget:extend()` does not work there, so it can write only one or two more files. Do not defer a large number of changes until exit. Kinds that are not written in time load as their last written version next time; the data is not corrupted.
- Keep a format version `v` in each table read from a file, and migrate each kind on its own ("Loading" in "Saving and loading"). When a kind has a newer version than yours, do not `touch` it.
- When `store.error` is not nil, show "save failed" in a corner of the screen.

## Why new file names: several files never get out of step

`ctx.storage:write` is complete for a single file: after a power loss, you read either all of the old content or all of the new content. Several files, however, cannot be switched together: if power fails after the first file is written and before the second, the two files reflect two different moments.

The module never overwrites an old file. It writes to a new name (generation plus one). Only after all of them are written does it change the names in `ctx.state.files` and save them with a single `ctx:save_state()`. `save_state` is also complete, so it acts as the commit:

| Where the failure occurs | What the next session reads |
| --- | --- |
| Power loss or error while writing the new files | The index still names the old files: everything is old |
| New files written, power loss or error before `save_state` | Same as above; `cleanup` deletes the extra new files |
| After `save_state`, before the old files are deleted | Everything is new; `cleanup` deletes the old files |

Therefore:

- Delete old files only after `save_state` succeeds.
- The kinds written in one `flush` always reflect the same moment. Data that must always stay consistent belongs in one kind, or is flushed together after the change.
- Call `cleanup` in `on_load`. It deletes only a few files each time, so it does not slow down opening. Lock screen sessions do not save automatically, so the lock screen script must not call `touch`, `flush` or `cleanup`; it reads only with `get`.

## Logs, events and other data that only grows: chunks

A log only grows at the end. If you keep it in a single file, every new entry rewrites the whole file, and writes take longer the longer the game is played. Split it into chunks of 100 entries: only the last chunk changes, a new chunk starts when the current one is full, and when there are too many chunks the oldest one is dropped.

```lua
-- log.lua: 100 entries per chunk, only the last chunk changes; keep at most 20 chunks
local store = require("store")
local M = {}
local PER_CHUNK, MAX_CHUNKS = 100, 20
local function empty() return {} end

local function range(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.log = s.log or { first = 1, last = 1 }
  return s.log
end

function M.push(ctx, entry)
  local r = range(ctx)
  local chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. r.last, empty)
  if #chunk >= PER_CHUNK then              -- this chunk is full, start a new one
    store.forget("log" .. r.last)
    r.last = r.last + 1
    chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. r.last, empty)
    if r.last - r.first >= MAX_CHUNKS then  -- too many, drop the oldest chunk
      store.drop(ctx, "log" .. r.first)
      r.first = r.first + 1
    end
  end
  chunk[#chunk + 1] = entry
  store.touch(ctx, "log" .. r.last)
end

-- the latest n entries, newest first
function M.recent(ctx, n)
  local r, out = range(ctx), {}
  for i = r.last, r.first, -1 do
    local chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. i, empty)
    for j = #chunk, 1, -1 do
      if #out == n then break end
      out[#out + 1] = chunk[j]
    end
    if i < r.last then store.forget("log" .. i) end  -- release older chunks once read
    if #out == n then break end
  end
  return out
end

return M
```

- 100 small entries per chunk take about 4 KB, and one write takes about 120 ms on X4 Pro. For larger entries, use fewer entries per chunk.
- When many entries are added in a row, the changes are held and written together 300 ms later, so adding hundreds at once results in only a few writes. A full chunk is not changed again after it is written.
- At most 20 chunks are kept, which is the latest 2000 entries. To keep everything, remove the cap, but check the file count: the 512 files must leave room for the other kinds.
- When browsing older entries, read them one chunk at a time and release each chunk with `store.forget` afterwards. Do not load them all into memory at once.

## Reading: load on use, release when done

- In `on_load`, read only the kinds needed for the first screen. Read the backpack, the bestiary, and similar kinds with `store.get` when their page opens.
- Decoding a 64 KB file takes about 100 ms on X4 Pro, plus the time to read the file. Keep the total read at open to a few dozen KB, or `on_load` exceeds its 2000 ms.
- For kinds you only read, call `store.forget` when you are done so they do not hold memory. Kinds that have changed and are not yet written are not released.
- When a file is missing or damaged, `store.get` returns the defaults and the game still runs. Whether to notify the player is up to you.

## Checklist before release

- The save size is estimated for the player who plays longest, and `ctx.state` holds only the index and small state.
- Nothing called every frame (`on_tick`, `on_draw`) calls `flush` or `ctx.storage:write`.
- `flush` is called after spending money, clearing levels, and similar actions, and failures are shown on screen.
- Every kind has a format version `v`, and a kind whose version is newer than yours is not written.
- Logs and events have a cap on entries or chunks.
- The lock screen script only reads.
- On X4 Pro, the duration of one `flush` has been measured with `ctx.clock:millis()` and leaves headroom below 1000 ms.

# 存档变大以后

背包中的几百件物品、几千条日志和事件、整张地图，超出了 `ctx.state` 的 16 KB 上限。平台提供的能力已能满足需求，无需自行实现存储：将数据按种类分别存入私有文件（每个应用 128 MB），`ctx.state` 只作为目录，记录每种数据当前所在的文件。需要处理的不是空间，而是写入存储卡的耗时，以及多个文件之间的一致性。本页提供一个可直接复制使用的 `store.lua` 模块。

## 先估一下要不要分文件

基本的保存方法见「存档与读档」。先按游玩时间最长的玩家，估算存档编码为 JSON 后的大小：

| 存档大小 | 做法 |
| --- | --- |
| 始终在 8 KB 以内 | 全部放入 `ctx.state`，无需本页 |
| 只有一项会增长，例如历史记录 | 将这一项放入一个文件，并设置条数上限（「存档与读档」的「大块数据放私有文件」） |
| 多项会增长：背包、任务、日志、地图、多个存档位 | 按本页的方法分文件 |

估算时：一个中文字符占 3 字节；一条 `{ t = 123, msg = "打败了史莱姆" }` 编码为 JSON 约 40 字节；一千条即 40 KB。

可用的额度和速度（契约第 9、10 节，甘草固件实测参考值）：

| 项 | 数值 |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.state` | 16 KB |
| 单个私有文件 | 256 KB，最多 512 个，合计 128 MB |
| 写入一个 4 KB 文件 | X4 Pro 约 120 ms，X4 Classic 约 30 ms |
| 删除一个文件 | X4 Pro 约 70 ms |
| JSON 编码或解码 | X4 Pro 每字节约 1.6 µs，64 KB 约 100 ms |
| 一次回调 | 1000 ms，`on_load` 2000 ms |

空间通常不会用尽，需要节省的是时间：每个文件控制在几 KB 到十几 KB，只写入修改过的数据，一次回调只写入一两个文件。

## 怎么分：ctx.state 当目录，数据按种类分文件

- 同时变化的数据归为同一种。购买时金币和物品同时变化，就把金币也放入背包文件，不要一半在 `ctx.state`、一半在文件中。
- 只增不减的数据（日志、事件、聊天、对局记录）按条数分块，每块一个文件，见下文。
- 地图这类大而稀疏的数据按区域分块，例如每 16×16 格一块，只保存去过的区域。
- 多个存档位时，每个存档位使用一套种类名，例如 `s1bag`、`s2bag`。
- 当前关卡、设置、当前使用的存档位这类小数据仍放在 `ctx.state` 中。

文件名只能使用小写字母、数字和 `._-`，长度为 1 到 64 字节（第 9 节）。下面的模块使用「种类名.代号.json」格式，例如 `bag.3.json`，因此种类名只使用小写字母、数字、`_` 和 `-`，并且不要全为数字（`ctx.state` 中的键 `"12"` 读回后会变成整数 12）。其他私有文件不要使用「名字.数字.json」格式，否则会被 `cleanup` 当作过期的旧文件删除。目录本身也存放在 `ctx.state` 中，因此种类数应控制在几十种以内，这样目录只占几 KB。

## store.lua：只写改过的，分几次写

```lua
-- store.lua：大块数据按种类各存一个文件，ctx.state.files 记每种现在用哪个文件
local M = {}
local PER_FLUSH = 2          -- 一次回调最多写几个文件；文件大时改成 1
local DELAY = 300            -- 改完多久开始写（毫秒）

local data = {}              -- 读进内存的：data[kind] = 表
local dirty = {}             -- 改过还没写的：dirty[kind] = true
local timer
M.error = nil                -- 最近一次写失败的错误名

local function index(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.files = s.files or {}    -- s.files.bag = { name = "bag.3.json", gen = 3 }
  return s.files
end

-- 取一种数据；第一次用时读文件，读不到或坏了用 fresh() 的默认值
function M.get(ctx, kind, fresh)
  if data[kind] then return data[kind] end
  local f = index(ctx)[kind]
  local t
  if f then
    local raw = ctx.storage:read(f.name)
    t = raw and ctx.json:decode(raw)
  end
  if type(t) ~= "table" then t = fresh() end
  data[kind] = t
  return t
end

-- 改完一种数据后调用：记下来，稍后再写
function M.touch(ctx, kind)
  dirty[kind] = true
  if not timer then timer = ctx:after(DELAY, function(ctx) M.flush(ctx) end) end
end

-- 写到新名字的文件，不覆盖旧的；成功返回 true 和旧文件名
local function write(ctx, kind)
  local files = index(ctx)
  local old = files[kind]
  local gen = (old and old.gen or 0) + 1
  local name = kind .. "." .. gen .. ".json"
  local text, err = ctx.json:encode(data[kind])
  if not text then return nil, err end
  local ok, werr = ctx.storage:write(name, text)
  if not ok then return nil, werr end
  files[kind] = { name = name, gen = gen }
  return true, old and old.name
end

-- 写最多 limit 个改过的种类，再用 save_state 一次换上新文件名
function M.flush(ctx, limit)
  if timer then timer:cancel(); timer = nil end
  limit = limit or PER_FLUSH
  local olds, n = {}, 0
  for kind in pairs(dirty) do
    if n == limit then break end
    local ok, r = write(ctx, kind)
    if not ok then M.error = r; break end
    dirty[kind] = nil
    olds[#olds + 1] = r
    n = n + 1
  end
  if n > 0 then
    local ok, err = ctx:save_state()
    if ok then
      for _, name in ipairs(olds) do ctx.storage:remove(name) end
      M.error = nil
    else
      M.error = err
    end
  end
  if next(dirty) then timer = ctx:after(DELAY, function(ctx) M.flush(ctx) end) end
end

-- 不再需要的种类：从目录里去掉，文件留给 cleanup 删
function M.drop(ctx, kind)
  index(ctx)[kind] = nil
  data[kind], dirty[kind] = nil, nil
end

-- 读过、没改的种类从内存里放掉
function M.forget(kind)
  if not dirty[kind] then data[kind] = nil end
end

-- on_load 里调用：删掉目录里没有的旧文件，每次最多删 max 个
function M.cleanup(ctx, max)
  local keep = {}
  for _, f in pairs(index(ctx)) do keep[f.name] = true end
  local n = 0
  for _, name in ipairs(ctx.storage:list()) do
    if n == (max or 3) then break end
    if name:match("^[a-z0-9_-]+%.%d+%.json$") and not keep[name] then
      ctx.storage:remove(name)
      n = n + 1
    end
  end
end

return M
```

用法：

```lua
local store = require("store")
local function new_bag() return { v = 1, gold = 0, items = {} } end

local function bag(ctx)
  local b = store.get(ctx, "bag", new_bag)
  b.gold = b.gold + 0.0                  -- JSON 读回的数可能是整数：换回浮点
  return b
end

function on_load(ctx)
  store.cleanup(ctx)                     -- 锁屏里不要调用
end

local function buy(ctx, id, price)
  local b = bag(ctx)
  if b.gold < price then return false end
  b.gold = b.gold - price
  b.items[id] = (b.items[id] or 0) + 1
  store.touch(ctx, "bag")
  store.flush(ctx)                       -- 花了钱，马上写
  return true
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  store.flush(ctx)                       -- 还没写的写一批
end
```

- 修改数据后通常只调用 `touch`。模块在 300 ms 后写入，一次最多写入两个文件，其余的排到下一次定时中。连续几百次修改只会产生几次写入。
- 不能丢失的操作（花钱、过关、领取奖励）之后立即调用 `flush`。
- `on_leave` 同样只有 1000 ms，并且其中不能使用 `ctx.budget:extend()`，只够再写入一两个文件。因此不要把大量修改留到退出时再写入。来不及写入的种类，下次打开时读到的是上次写入完成的版本，数据不会损坏。
- 读出的表中同样保存格式版本号 `v`，每种数据各自迁移（「存档与读档」的「读档」）。读到比当前程序更新的版本时，不要对这一种调用 `touch`。
- `store.error` 不为 nil 时，在画面角落提示「存档失败」。

## 为什么写新文件名：好几个文件也不会对不上

`ctx.storage:write` 对单个文件的写入是完整的：断电后读到的要么全部是旧内容，要么全部是新内容。但多个文件无法同时切换：如果第一个文件已写完、第二个尚未写入时断电，两个文件就对应两个不同的时刻。

模块的做法是不覆盖旧文件，而是写入新的文件名（代号加一）；全部写完后，再修改 `ctx.state.files` 中的文件名，并用一次 `ctx:save_state()` 保存。`save_state` 本身的写入也是完整的，因此它起到「提交」的作用：

| 出错的步骤 | 下次打开时读到的内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 写入新文件时断电或出错 | 目录仍指向旧文件，全部是旧数据 |
| 新文件均已写好，`save_state` 之前断电或出错 | 同上，多出的新文件由 `cleanup` 删除 |
| `save_state` 之后、删除旧文件之前 | 全部是新数据，旧文件由 `cleanup` 删除 |

因此：

- 只有在 `save_state` 成功之后才删除旧文件。
- 一次 `flush` 写入的几种数据必定对应同一时刻。需要始终保持一致的几项数据，应放入同一种，或在修改后一起 `flush`。
- 在 `on_load` 中调用 `cleanup`，每次只删除几个文件，不占用打开应用的时间。锁屏会话不自动保存，锁屏脚本中不要调用 `touch`、`flush`、`cleanup`，只用 `get` 读取。

## 日志、事件这类只增不减的：分块

日志这类数据只在末尾追加。如果整份放在一个文件中，每追加一条都要重写全部内容，游玩时间越长写入越慢。按每 100 条分为一块：只有最后一块会被修改，写满后开启新块；块数过多时丢弃最旧的一块。

```lua
-- log.lua：日志每 100 条一块，只有最后一块会改；最多留 20 块
local store = require("store")
local M = {}
local PER_CHUNK, MAX_CHUNKS = 100, 20
local function empty() return {} end

local function range(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.log = s.log or { first = 1, last = 1 }
  return s.log
end

function M.push(ctx, entry)
  local r = range(ctx)
  local chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. r.last, empty)
  if #chunk >= PER_CHUNK then              -- 这一块满了，开新的一块
    store.forget("log" .. r.last)
    r.last = r.last + 1
    chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. r.last, empty)
    if r.last - r.first >= MAX_CHUNKS then  -- 太多了，丢掉最老的一块
      store.drop(ctx, "log" .. r.first)
      r.first = r.first + 1
    end
  end
  chunk[#chunk + 1] = entry
  store.touch(ctx, "log" .. r.last)
end

-- 最近的 n 条，最新的在前
function M.recent(ctx, n)
  local r, out = range(ctx), {}
  for i = r.last, r.first, -1 do
    local chunk = store.get(ctx, "log" .. i, empty)
    for j = #chunk, 1, -1 do
      if #out == n then break end
      out[#out + 1] = chunk[j]
    end
    if i < r.last then store.forget("log" .. i) end  -- 老的块看完就放掉
    if #out == n then break end
  end
  return out
end

return M
```

- 每块 100 条小记录约 4 KB，在 X4 Pro 上写入一次约需 120 ms。记录较大时，减少每块的条数。
- 连续追加多条记录时，修改先暂存，300 ms 后一并写入，因此一次追加几百条也只写入几次。写满的块写入后不再修改。
- 最多保留 20 块，即最近 2000 条。如需全部保留，可以不设上限，但要计算文件数：512 个文件中还需为其他种类留出余量。
- 翻看更早的记录时逐块读取，看完后用 `store.forget` 释放，不要一次全部读入内存。

## 读：用到才读，读完放掉

- `on_load` 中只读取首屏需要绘制的几种数据。背包、图鉴这类数据，在打开对应页面时再调用 `store.get`。
- 在 X4 Pro 上解码一个 64 KB 的文件约需 100 ms，另加读取文件的时间。打开应用时读取的数据合计应控制在几十 KB 以内，否则会超出 `on_load` 的 2000 ms。
- 只读不改的种类，用完后调用 `store.forget` 释放内存。已修改但尚未写入的种类不会被释放。
- 文件缺失或损坏时，`store.get` 返回默认值，游戏仍可正常运行。是否提示玩家由你决定。

## 发布前检查

- 已按游玩时间最长的玩家估算存档大小，`ctx.state` 中只保留目录和少量状态。
- 每帧调用的回调（`on_tick`、`on_draw`）中没有 `flush`、`ctx.storage:write`。
- 花钱、过关这类操作之后调用了 `flush`；失败时会在画面上显示。
- 每种数据都有格式版本号 `v`，读到比当前程序更新的版本时不写入这一种。
- 日志、事件设有条数或块数上限。
- 锁屏脚本只读不写。
- 在 X4 Pro 上用 `ctx.clock:millis()` 测量过一次 `flush` 的耗时，距 1000 ms 留有余量。

local M = {}
local PER_FLUSH = 2          -- 一次回调最多写几个文件；文件大时改成 1
local DELAY = 300            -- 改完多久开始写（毫秒）

local data = {}              -- 读进内存的：data[kind] = 表
local dirty = {}             -- 改过还没写的：dirty[kind] = true
local timer
M.error = nil                -- 最近一次写失败的错误名

local function index(ctx)
  local s = ctx.state
  s.files = s.files or {}    -- s.files.bag = { name = "bag.3.json", gen = 3 }
  return s.files
end

function M.get(ctx, kind, fresh)

function M.flush(ctx, limit)

-- 不再需要的种类：从目录里去掉，文件留给 cleanup 删

# XTApp Lua Author API

This page documents the frozen API 0.8. It is not the current API. Write new apps against the 2.x contract, not this page.

This is a reference for readers who already know how to program. It follows the order in which you encounter things while writing code: callbacks, input, drawing, and state, then the names you can call. The integer range and the names missing from the sandbox come last.

For a small program that draws one line of text on the screen, start with the project layout page.

## Lifecycle

An application does not write its own main loop. You declare the functions below, and the system calls each one at the corresponding moment:

```lua
function on_load(ctx) end
function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end
function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms) end
function on_input(ctx, ev) return false end
function on_draw(ctx, g) end
function on_leave(ctx) end
function on_unload(ctx) end
```

- `on_load`: when the application is loaded. Validate and do light initialization.
- `on_enter`: when the screen is entered. Usually follow it with `ctx:invalidate()` to request the first frame.
- `on_tick`: called at the cadence you set. The argument is the number of milliseconds since the previous call. Advance only a small amount of state.
- `on_input`: when a key press or touch arrives.
- `on_draw`: draw the current state onto the screen.
- `on_leave` and `on_unload`: when the application leaves or unloads.

Each of these functions should return promptly. Do not write a top-level endless loop, and do not busy-wait inside a callback. When a computation may exceed the limits below, extend the time only inside **the current callback**. Do not start another main loop. See the long-task section below.

Without a long task, exceeding the limit aborts that callback:

| Callback | Limit |
|---|---:|
| `on_load` | 200 ms |
| `on_enter` | 300 ms |
| `on_tick` | 60 ms |
| `on_input` | 400 ms |
| `on_draw` | 1500 ms |
| `on_leave` | 100 ms |
| `on_unload` | 200 ms |

If `on_load` is aborted, the device shows a white screen. The logged line number is the line of the inner loop that was hit; follow the call chain to find the owning callback. Do not put random search, image scans, or level generation in `on_load`. Put large images in `preload_assets`.

## Input Events

You can handle a directional key like this:

```lua
function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  if ev.key == "up" then
    ctx.state.n = (ctx.state.n or 0) + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

Return `true` when you handled the event, and `false` when you did not. After you change state that should be shown, call `ctx:invalidate()`.

Currently, the only reliable key event is `ev.state == "down"`. Do not wait for a matching `up`. `ev.key` is always one of `up/down/left/right/ok/back`. `ev.time_ms` is the monotonic time in milliseconds when the event was delivered. The device does not provide `repeat_count`, `duration_ms`, or `ctx.color`.

X4 Classic and X4 Pro both provide these six remappable semantic keys. Code depends on the key names, not on physical key numbers or positions. Classic has no touch, so core operations must be completable with the directional keys, `ok`, and `back`. Pro also has touch events with `ev.type == "touch"`, coordinates `ev.x` and `ev.y`, and the gestures `tap`, `double_tap`, `long`, `swipe_left`, `swipe_right`, `swipe_up`, and `swipe_down`.

Power is a separate physical key. It is not delivered to the application as a `power` event. Do not write `ev.key == "power"`, and do not treat `ctx.input:has_key("power")` as an interactive capability.

## Screen and Device Profile

Lay out the screen based on its current size. Do not hard-code the width and height of one device.

Use `ctx.screen.width`, `ctx.screen.height`, `ctx.screen.orientation`, `ctx.screen.is_landscape`, `ctx.screen.is_portrait`, `ctx.screen.short_side`, and `ctx.screen.long_side`.

- X4 Classic: portrait `480×800`, landscape `800×480`, no touch. Core interaction uses the directional keys, confirm, and back.
- X4 Pro: portrait `480×800`, landscape `800×480`. It supports touch, a gyroscope, Bluetooth, and PSRAM.

The front cover hides the edges of the panel. `ctx.screen` keeps the full size, and those pixels are still drawn but are not visible. The occlusion is recorded for portrait orientation, with the origin at the top left: 9px on the top, and 2px each on the left, right, and bottom. The portrait visible area starts at `(2, 9)`. Its width is `width - 4` and its height is `height - 11`. On `480×800` that is `476×789`. Put text, strokes, focus, and touch targets inside this area. A full-bleed background can extend into the hidden pixels.

In landscape, the cover stays fixed to the chassis. The 9px strip is the physical edge that faces up when the device is held upright, not the logical top after rotation. The four landscape edges have not been remeasured with the same method. Do not reuse the portrait top inset of 9px as the landscape `y` origin.

## g Drawing API

Draw inside `on_draw`. Clear the screen, then draw text:

```lua
function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 40, "Hello", { color = 15 })
end
```

Colors range from `0` (white) to `15` (black). On the device, `0–7` is drawn white and `8–15` is drawn black. Use `0` and `15` in the interface. These 16 values are not 16 gray levels, and the values in between do not draw gray. The panel hardware supports four gray levels, but this API draws only black and white.

The available calls are:

- `g:clear(color)`
- `g:line(x1, y1, x2, y2, color)`
- `g:rect(x, y, width, height, "fill"|"stroke", color)`
- `g:circle(x, y, radius, "fill"|"stroke", color)`
- `g:text(x, y, text, { color = 15 })`
- `g:image(key_or_handle, x, y, opts)`
- `g:layer(layer, x, y)`
- `g:size()`

`g:text` supports only `color`. There is no `align`, `font`, or arbitrary font size. The application positions centered text or large digits itself from known character widths, or composes seven-segment digits from rectangles. `g:image` accepts `invert` and `color`. The real device does not scale images: if the `width/height` you pass differ from the original XIC size, the device records one diagnosable warning and still draws at the source size. Do not treat this as scaling. Every coordinate must fall inside the current screen or offscreen layer.

`g:rect` draws right angles only. There is no native `round_rect`, path, or clipping. The interface can still use rounded corners: a solid rounded corner is composed of two rectangles and four circles, and an outlined one is an outer solid block covered by a smaller inner block in the background color. A pill sets the radius to half the height, and a switch adds one more circle. Search boxes, chips, switches, primary buttons, and a few emphasized cards suit rounded corners. Tables, charts, progress bars, checkboxes, and console sections usually keep right angles. The device UI page describes the complete composition and the control bounds.

When composing rounded corners, draw the container before the text and icons. The background color of the inner outline must match the solid background at that location. Make complex static textures or illustrations into XIC files. Keep drawing changing values and interactive states with these basic calls. One rounded fill takes about six drawing commands. When you use many of them, monitor `ctx.perf:info().cmd_count` and the per-frame command budget.

## Persistent State

Store data that should persist after the application leaves in `ctx.state`. It is a serializable table. Store only strings, booleans, finite numbers, and plain tables:

```lua
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.counter then ctx.state.counter = 0 end
  return ctx.state
end
```

Leaving the application saves `ctx.state`. `ctx:save()` is not currently a reliable capability. Do not call it.

## Project Structure

The project layout page describes the file structure in full, including a minimal program. At run time, these paths are recognized:

```text
manifest.json
index.lua             # default entry
lockscreen.lua        # optional, used only when manifest.lockscreen explicitly enables it
data/*.tsv            # optional, read-only data
lang/*.tsv            # optional, multi-language text
raw/*                 # optional, source images, managed by Studio
assets/*.xic          # optional, created by the Studio asset tools; do not write binaries by hand
dist/*.xtapp          # packaging output
```

This page documents the frozen `"0.8"`. New projects use 2.x. Existing `"0.5"`, `"0.6"`, and `"0.7"` projects run as they are; their manifest and Lua are not rewritten automatically. The device runs only the entry declared in the manifest. `require`, `package`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, and dynamic code are unavailable at run time. In Studio, you can keep the source in several files; at run time they are combined into that one entry. Independent features such as the lock screen exist only when the manifest explicitly declares an extra entry point.

## Top-Level ctx Methods

After you change state that should be shown, call `ctx:invalidate()` to request a redraw. The other top-level calls are:

- `ctx:invalidate()`: requests a redraw
- `ctx:set_tick_rate(mode)`: sets the `on_tick` cadence. The fixed levels are `realtime/high/normal/low/idle`, about once every `33/50/100/500/2000ms` respectively
- `ctx:quit()`: requests exit
- `ctx:request_refresh()`: requests a refresh. This expresses only an intent; the system still chooses the waveform. In Studio, refresh calls do not produce the device waveform

## Time

Measure intervals with monotonic milliseconds: `ctx.sys:millis()` and `ctx.sys:uptime_ms()`. These count milliseconds since boot, not wall-clock time.

For a clock face, call `ctx.sys:clock()`. It requires no permission, and both the main entry and the lock screen can read it. Call it, then read the fields of the returned table. Both `ctx.sys:clock()` and `ctx.sys.clock()` work; the colon form is recommended.

Multiple calls in the same callback return the same snapshot, taken at the start of that callback. The time advances at the next `on_tick`, `on_draw`, or `on_input`. The returned table is read-only, and assigning to `hour` raises an error. Unknown fields are `nil`.

Check `valid` first. When the clock has not been set, or the source is empty, `valid` is false and the hour, minute, and date are `nil`. Show `--:--` in that case. Do not treat `nil` as midnight.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `valid` | whether the clock can be used |
| `hour` | local hour, 0–23. Noon is 12, midnight is 0, 1 PM is 13 |
| `minute` | 0–59 |
| `second` | 0–59 |
| `year` | local Gregorian year |
| `month` | 1–12 |
| `day` | 1–31 |
| `weekday` | 0 is Sunday, 6 is Saturday |
| `offset_minutes` | offset from UTC in minutes. China Standard Time is 480 |
| `hour12` | whether the user set the system display to 12-hour format. It does not change `hour` |
| `epoch_sec` | UTC Unix seconds |
| `local_sec` | local seconds with the time-zone offset already applied |

This is the wall clock in the device's current time zone, the same local time the status bar uses. It is not UTC, and it is not fixed to one city. When the time zone changes, `offset_minutes` changes with it. If the status bar shows 5:01 PM, the values here are still `hour == 17` and `minute == 1`. To distinguish morning from afternoon, read `hour12`, then treat `hour < 12` as morning.

`ctx.sys:epoch_sec()` and `ctx.sys:local_sec()` return the same pair of second counts, or `nil` when the clock is invalid. Do not convert them to hours and minutes with the float division `/`. Single precision rounds a value near 1.79 billion to steps of 128 seconds, so the minute always lands on an even number. Read `hour` and `minute` directly for a clock face. These second counts exceed the 32-bit integer range after 2038-01-19. `hour` and `minute` are not affected by this limit.

`source` is `hardware_rtc`, `sntp`, `manual`, or `none`. `trust` is `plausible`, `verified`, or `invalid`. `source_stale` indicates whether this sample is stale relative to the clock source. `revision`, `timezone_revision`, and `format_revision` are the versions of the clock, the time zone, and the 12/24-hour setting respectively. Each number changes when the corresponding setting changes.

Do not accumulate `dt_ms` to derive the hour and minute yourself.

```lua
local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
if clock.valid then
  -- clock.hour, clock.minute
end
```

For logging, use `ctx.log:info(...)`, `ctx.log:warn(...)`, and `ctx.log:error(...)`. Do not use `print`.

## Long Tasks

If a computation inside one callback may exceed the limits in the lifecycle section, call `ctx.longtask:start()` once before the computation. The first call gives the current callback 11 seconds. Calling it again in the same callback still returns `true` and does not restart the timer.

`ctx.longtask:feed()` returns `true` on success and extends the deadline to 11 seconds after the call. It returns `nil, "inactive"` if `start()` has not been called.

Use `ctx.longtask:stop()` only when the user explicitly cancels and leaves. It clears the long task and requests exit. When the computation finishes normally, return directly. Do not call `stop()`.

A long task also needs its own wall-clock budget. A single synchronous `on_tick` should stay under 10 seconds, and a routine search is usually limited to 0.5–2 seconds. The loop can check the budget often, but actual `feed()` calls should be coalesced by wall clock to about once every 1–2 seconds. When the budget runs out, return the best legal result found so far. Split work longer than 10 seconds across multiple callbacks. Cover every call site with `start()` / `feed()`, including startup and a rematch. These limits are fixed.

`pcall` / `xpcall` can catch a timeout. When the error text contains `watchdog` or `time budget`, re-raise it unchanged. Do not catch it and then call `feed()` to continue. Write search results to local variables first, and write them to `ctx.state` once after a successful return, so that an error cannot leave half-updated state.

Split a turn-based game into these steps: the user moves, one partial refresh, `ctx.longtask:start()` followed by synchronous thinking with `ctx.longtask:feed()` as needed in the loop, the AI moves, one partial refresh. Do not compute several moves in the same callback.

In Studio, `ctx.longtask:start()` and `ctx.longtask:feed()` return `true`, but the 11 second deadline is not enforced. `ctx.longtask:stop()` requests exit and does not raise the Lua error that the device raises.

## Networking

For how to organize a request, see the ScriptNet routing page. This section covers the calls themselves.

After the manifest declares `"permissions": ["net.http"]`, asynchronous HTTP GET and POST are available. Only `http://` is supported. Start the request from a lifecycle callback and poll it in a later `on_tick`. Do not block while waiting for the result.

- `ctx.net:get(url)` and `ctx.net:post(url, body[, headers])`: return a task ID on success, and `nil, err` on failure
- `ctx.net:poll(task_id)`: returns a result containing `done/ok/status/body/err/bytes`
- `ctx.net:cancel(task_id)`: cancels a task you no longer need

## Other Namespaces

Look up the remaining calls by name. To test whether a method exists, use a dot, for example `if ctx.i18n and ctx.i18n.t then`. To call it, use a colon.

- `ctx.display:full_refresh()`, `ctx.display:defer_auto_full(ms)`
- `ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()`
- `ctx.i18n.locale` and `ctx.i18n:t(key)`
- `ctx.perf:info()`: returns `tick_us/draw_us/cmd_count/image_count/asset_hit/asset_miss/draw_frame`. Studio guarantees only that these fields exist; the values do not reflect the real device
- `ctx.gc:count()`, `ctx.gc:collect()`
- `ctx.input.caps`, `ctx.input:has_key(key)`, `ctx.input:has_bt_keyboard()`, `ctx.input:has_bt_gamepad()`. The last two currently always return `false`
- `ctx.lock:flush_once(mode)`, `ctx.lock:set_interval(seconds)`. `ctx.lock` also exposes `reason/base_page/elapsed_sec/interval_sec/clear_background`
- `ctx.assets:evict(key)`, `ctx.assets:info(key)`, `ctx.assets:handle(key)`. `handle()` returns `handle/asset_key/width/height`, and `info()` returns `used/limit/count`
- `ctx.data:exists(name)`, `ctx.data:size(name)`, `ctx.data:read_text(name)`, `ctx.data:open_text(name)`. `open_text()` supports `max_bytes/max_line_bytes`. The reader provides `read_line()`, `seek()`, `tell()`, and `close()`. Failure codes include `invalid_name/not_found/read_failed/line_too_long`
- `ctx.layers:create(width, height)`

## Offscreen Layers

Graphics that rarely change can be drawn into a buffer first, then copied onto the screen in `on_draw`:

```lua
local layer

function on_load(ctx)
  layer = ctx.layers:create(160, 80)
  layer:draw_with(function(g)
    g:rect(0, 0, 160, 80, "stroke", 15)
  end)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:layer(layer, 20, 20)
end
```

The layer width and height must be positive and must not exceed the public contract limit. Do not nest `draw_with`. Call `layer:dispose()` on a layer you no longer use. Offscreen layers cache static geometry or images. They do not enlarge text, and `g:text` cannot be called inside `layer:draw_with`.

## data and i18n

Keep read-only tables and translated text in files, not in Lua.

Data files must be listed in the manifest `data_files`. `ctx.data` accepts a file name, not a path. The first line of a TSV can serve as the header.

Translated text goes in `lang/<locale>.tsv`, with one `key<TAB>value` per line. When a translation is missing, the application keeps its own readable fallback.

## Lock Screen

The lock screen is a separate entry that runs apart from the normal application. It draws one frame at a time, runs the entry again each time, and does not receive the normal application's key presses or touches. Put data that must persist across frames in `ctx.state`, and call `ctx.lock:flush_once("partial"|"full")` once. Do not treat the lock screen `on_input` as a reliable way to interact, and do not rely on module globals, `on_leave`, or `on_unload` to save lock screen state.

## The Language

The language is Lua 5.5. You can use `global` declarations, variable attributes (`<const>` / `<close>`), and named variadic parameters. The range of integers and floats is described in the next section.

In Studio, you can use `require("project.module")` to split this project into several files. The argument must be a literal module name. On the device, those files have already been combined into the entry, and `require` does not exist. You cannot assign `require` to another name and call it, and you cannot build a module name at run time.

## Numbers

Write counters, indexes, and loop variables as ordinary integers. Read the rest of this section when you approach a boundary.

Integers are signed 32-bit values, and `math.maxinteger` is `2147483647`. Floats are single precision. A literal that fits in a 32-bit integer stays an integer, such as `1111111109`. A larger numeral becomes a float, so `tostring(20000000000)` is `2e+10`. Floats represent consecutive integers exactly only up to `2^24` (`16777216`). Integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication wrap around in two's complement beyond 32 bits and remain integers. Division `/` and exponentiation `^` produce floats and lose low-order bits beyond `2^24`. Bitwise operators and integer division `//` stay exact as long as the result fits in a 32-bit integer. Do not use Lua floats for dynamic truncation or for the modulo of a large timestamp. For a clock face, read `hour` and `minute` from `ctx.sys:clock()`. Keep counters and digests in integers or byte strings.

## Security Restrictions

An application can use the public `ctx` and `g`. These names do not exist: `io`, `os`, `package`, `debug`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `load`, `require`, `collectgarbage`, `print`. The string metatable cannot be replaced. For logging, garbage collection, or networking, use `ctx.log`, `ctx.gc`, and `ctx.net`.

Files split with `require("project.module")` in Studio are combined into the entry before running. On the device, there is still no `require`, and there is no arbitrary file access.

entries.content:
# XTApp Lua 作者 API

本页记录的是已冻结的 API 0.8，不是现行接口。新应用应按 2.x 契约编写，不要参照本页。

本页是接口参考，面向已有编程经验的读者。内容按编写代码时遇到的顺序排列：先是回调、输入、绘图和状态，然后是可调用的名字。整数范围和沙箱中不存在的名字放在最后。

如需先查看一个能在屏幕上绘制一行文字的小程序，请从「XTApp 标准工程格式」开始阅读。

## 生命周期

应用不自行编写主循环。你声明下面这些函数，系统在对应的时刻调用它们：

```lua
function on_load(ctx) end
function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end
function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms) end
function on_input(ctx, ev) return false end
function on_draw(ctx, g) end
function on_leave(ctx) end
function on_unload(ctx) end
```

- `on_load`：应用加载时。执行校验和轻量初始化。
- `on_enter`：进入画面时。通常随后调用 `ctx:invalidate()`，请求绘制第一帧。
- `on_tick`：按你设置的节奏被调用，参数是距上次调用的毫秒数。只推进少量状态。
- `on_input`：有按键或触摸时。
- `on_draw`：把当前状态绘制到屏幕上。
- `on_leave` 与 `on_unload`：离开或卸载时。

这些函数都应尽快返回。不要编写顶层死循环，也不要在回调中空等。计算可能超出下列时限时，只能在**当前这次回调**中用长任务延长时限，不能另起主循环。写法见后文「长任务」。

未开启长任务时，超时会中止这次回调：

| 回调 | 上限 |
|---|---:|
| `on_load` | 200 ms |
| `on_enter` | 300 ms |
| `on_tick` | 60 ms |
| `on_input` | 400 ms |
| `on_draw` | 1500 ms |
| `on_leave` | 100 ms |
| `on_unload` | 200 ms |

`on_load` 被中止时，真机显示白屏。日志中的行号是内层循环被命中的那一行，需沿调用链找到所属的回调。随机搜索、扫描图像、生成关卡不要放在 `on_load` 中；大图放入 `preload_assets`。

## 输入事件

方向键可以按如下方式处理：

```lua
function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  if ev.key == "up" then
    ctx.state.n = (ctx.state.n or 0) + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

处理了事件返回 `true`，未处理返回 `false`。修改了需要显示的状态后，调用 `ctx:invalidate()`。

目前可靠的按键事件只有 `ev.state == "down"`，不要等待与之配对的 `up`。`ev.key` 只会是 `up/down/left/right/ok/back`。`ev.time_ms` 是事件投递时的单调毫秒数。设备上没有 `repeat_count`、`duration_ms` 或 `ctx.color`。

X4 Classic 与 X4 Pro 都提供这六个可重映射的语义键。代码依据键名，不依据物理键的编号或位置。Classic 没有触摸，核心操作必须能用方向键、`ok` 和 `back` 完成。Pro 另有触摸事件 `ev.type == "touch"`，坐标为 `ev.x`、`ev.y`，手势为 `tap`、`double_tap`、`long`、`swipe_left`、`swipe_right`、`swipe_up`、`swipe_down`。

Power 是单独的物理键，不会作为 `power` 事件传递给应用。不要编写 `ev.key == "power"`，也不要把 `ctx.input:has_key("power")` 当作可交互的能力。

## 屏幕与设备画像

按当前屏幕尺寸布局，不要写死某一台设备的宽高。

使用 `ctx.screen.width`、`ctx.screen.height`、`ctx.screen.orientation`、`ctx.screen.is_landscape`、`ctx.screen.is_portrait`、`ctx.screen.short_side` 和 `ctx.screen.long_side`。

- X4 Classic：竖屏 `480×800`，横屏 `800×480`，无触摸。核心交互使用方向键、确认键和返回键。
- X4 Pro：竖屏 `480×800`，横屏 `800×480`，支持触摸、陀螺仪、蓝牙和 PSRAM。

前盖板会遮挡面板边缘。`ctx.screen` 的宽高不变，这些像素仍会绘制，只是不可见。遮挡范围按竖屏、原点在左上角记录：上边 9px，左边、右边、下边各 2px。竖屏可见区域从 `(2, 9)` 开始，宽为 `width - 4`，高为 `height - 11`。在 `480×800` 上为 `476×789`。文字、描边、焦点和触摸命中区应放在此区域内。铺满的背景可以绘制到被遮挡的像素中。

横屏时盖板固定在机身上。9px 的那一边是机身竖持时朝上的物理边，不是旋转后的逻辑上边。横屏四边尚未按同一方法重新测量，不要把竖屏上边的 9px 套用为横屏的 `y` 起点。

## g 绘图 API

在 `on_draw` 中绘制。先清屏，再绘制文字：

```lua
function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 40, "Hello", { color = 15 })
end
```

颜色取值从 `0`（白）到 `15`（黑）。设备上 `0–7` 绘制为白色，`8–15` 绘制为黑色。界面使用 `0` 和 `15`。这 16 个数值不是 16 级灰度，中间值也不会绘制出灰色。面板硬件支持四阶灰度，但此 API 只绘制黑白。

可调用的函数如下：

- `g:clear(color)`
- `g:line(x1, y1, x2, y2, color)`
- `g:rect(x, y, width, height, "fill"|"stroke", color)`
- `g:circle(x, y, radius, "fill"|"stroke", color)`
- `g:text(x, y, text, { color = 15 })`
- `g:image(key_or_handle, x, y, opts)`
- `g:layer(layer, x, y)`
- `g:size()`

`g:text` 只支持 `color`，没有 `align`、`font` 或任意字号。居中文字或大号数字由应用根据已知字符宽度自行计算坐标，或用矩形组成七段数字。`g:image` 可以传入 `invert` 和 `color`。当前真机不支持缩放：传入的 `width/height` 与原 XIC 尺寸不一致时，设备记录一条可诊断的警告，仍按源尺寸绘制，不要把它当作缩放功能。所有坐标都必须位于当前屏幕或离屏图层范围内。

`g:rect` 只绘制直角，没有原生的 `round_rect`、路径或裁剪。界面仍然可以使用圆角：实心圆角由 2 个矩形和 4 个圆拼成；描边圆角先绘制外层实心块，再用背景色覆盖缩小的内层。胶囊形将半径设为高度的一半，开关再叠加一个圆。搜索框、Chip、开关、主按钮和少量重点卡片适合使用圆角；表格、图表、进度条、复选框和控制台分区通常保持直角。完整的拼法和控件边界见「XTApp 设备 UI 组合能力」。

拼接圆角时，先绘制容器，再绘制文字和图标。描边内层的背景色必须与该区域的纯色背景一致。复杂的静态纹理或插画制作成 XIC；会变化的数值和交互状态继续用这些基础调用绘制。一个圆角填充约占 6 条绘图命令，大量使用时应关注 `ctx.perf:info().cmd_count` 和单帧命令预算。

## 持久状态

离开应用后仍需保留的数据，放在 `ctx.state` 中。它是一张可序列化的表，只能存放字符串、布尔值、有限数字和普通 table：

```lua
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.counter then ctx.state.counter = 0 end
  return ctx.state
end
```

离开应用时会保存 `ctx.state`。`ctx:save()` 目前不是可靠的能力，不要调用。

## 工程结构

文件的组织方式在「XTApp 标准工程格式」中有更完整的说明，其中也包含一个最小程序。运行时识别以下路径：

```text
manifest.json
index.lua             # 默认入口
lockscreen.lua        # 可选，manifest.lockscreen 明确启用时使用
data/*.tsv            # 可选，只读数据
lang/*.tsv            # 可选，多语言文本
raw/*                 # 可选，素材原图，由 Studio 管理
assets/*.xic          # 可选，由 Studio 素材工具创建，不手写二进制
dist/*.xtapp          # 打包输出
```

本页记录的是已冻结的 `"0.8"`。新工程使用 2.x。已有的 `"0.5"`、`"0.6"` 与 `"0.7"` 工程按原样运行，manifest 和 Lua 不会被自动改写。设备只运行 manifest 声明的入口。`require`、`package`、`dofile`、`loadfile` 与动态代码在运行时均不可用。在 Studio 中可以分文件编写，运行时会合并为这一个入口。锁屏等独立功能只有在 manifest 明确声明额外入口时才存在。

## ctx 顶层方法

修改需要显示的状态后，用 `ctx:invalidate()` 请求重绘。顶层还提供以下调用：

- `ctx:invalidate()`：请求重绘
- `ctx:set_tick_rate(mode)`：设置 `on_tick` 的节奏。固定档位为 `realtime/high/normal/low/idle`，分别约每 `33/50/100/500/2000ms` 一次
- `ctx:quit()`：请求退出
- `ctx:request_refresh()`：请求刷新。这只表达意图，最终波形仍由系统决定。在 Studio 中，刷新调用不会产生设备上的波形

## 时间

计时使用单调毫秒：`ctx.sys:millis()`、`ctx.sys:uptime_ms()`。二者是开机后经过的毫秒数，不是墙钟时间。

钟面调用 `ctx.sys:clock()`。它不需要权限，主入口和锁屏都可以读取。先调用，再读取返回表中的字段。`ctx.sys:clock()` 和 `ctx.sys.clock()` 都可以使用，推荐使用冒号。

在同一次回调中多次调用，得到的都是本次回调开始时的同一份时间，到下一次 `on_tick`、`on_draw` 或 `on_input` 时才会更新。返回的表是只读的，给 `hour` 赋值会报错。未知字段为 `nil`。

先检查 `valid`。尚未校时或时间来源为空时，`valid` 为 false，此时小时、分钟和日期为 `nil`。界面应显示 `--:--`，不要把 `nil` 当作 0 点。

| 字段 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `valid` | 时钟是否可用 |
| `hour` | 本地小时，0–23。中午为 12，午夜为 0，下午 1 点为 13 |
| `minute` | 0–59 |
| `second` | 0–59 |
| `year` | 本地公历年 |
| `month` | 1–12 |
| `day` | 1–31 |
| `weekday` | 0 为星期日，6 为星期六 |
| `offset_minutes` | 相对 UTC 的偏移分钟数。中国标准时间为 480 |
| `hour12` | 用户是否将系统显示设为 12 小时制。不影响 `hour` |
| `epoch_sec` | UTC Unix 秒 |
| `local_sec` | 已加上时区偏移的本地秒 |

这是设备当前时区的墙钟，与状态栏使用同一套本地时间，不是 UTC，也不固定于某个城市。时区改变时，`offset_minutes` 随之变化。状态栏开启 12 小时制时，显示的文字可能是下午 5:01，此处仍为 `hour == 17`、`minute == 1`。如需区分上午和下午，读取 `hour12`，再用 `hour < 12` 判断上午。

`ctx.sys:epoch_sec()` 和 `ctx.sys:local_sec()` 返回同一对秒数，无效时为 `nil`。不要用浮点除法 `/` 把它们换算成时和分：单精度浮点会把约 17.9 亿的秒数舍入为 128 秒一档，分钟会落在偶数上。钟面应直接读取 `hour` 和 `minute`。这两个秒数在 2038-01-19 之后会超出 32 位整数范围，`hour` 和 `minute` 不受此限制。

`source` 为 `hardware_rtc`、`sntp`、`manual` 或 `none`。`trust` 为 `plausible`、`verified` 或 `invalid`。`source_stale` 表示本次采样相对时钟源是否过旧。`revision`、`timezone_revision`、`format_revision` 分别是时钟、时区和 12/24 小时制设置的版本号，对应设置改变时，该数值随之改变。

不要通过累加 `dt_ms` 自行推算小时和分钟。

```lua
local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
if clock.valid then
  -- clock.hour, clock.minute
end
```

日志使用 `ctx.log:info(...)`、`ctx.log:warn(...)`、`ctx.log:error(...)`。不要使用 `print`。

## 长任务

如果一次回调中的计算可能超出「生命周期」中的时限，在计算前调用一次 `ctx.longtask:start()`。首次调用为当前回调开放 11 秒。在同一次回调中再次调用仍返回 `true`，不会重新计时。

`ctx.longtask:feed()` 成功时返回 `true`，把截止时间延长到调用后的 11 秒。尚未调用 `start()` 时返回 `nil, "inactive"`。

`ctx.longtask:stop()` 只在用户明确取消并离开应用时使用。它会清除长任务并请求退出。正常计算完成后直接返回，不要调用 `stop()`。

长任务还需自行设定墙钟预算：单次同步 `on_tick` 建议不超过 10 秒，常规搜索通常限制在 0.5～2 秒。循环中可以频繁检查预算，但实际的 `feed()` 调用应按墙钟合并为约每 1～2 秒一次。预算用完时，返回目前最优的合法结果。超过 10 秒的工作应拆分到多次回调中。每个调用点都要调用 `start()` / `feed()`，包括启动和再来一局。这些时限是固定的。

`pcall` / `xpcall` 可以捕获超时错误。错误文本中含有 `watchdog` 或 `time budget` 时，必须原样重新抛出。不要在捕获后调用 `feed()` 继续计算。搜索结果先写入局部变量，成功返回后再一次性写入 `ctx.state`，以免出错时留下写了一半的状态。

交替落子的对弈按以下步骤拆分：用户落子，一次局部刷，`ctx.longtask:start()` 之后同步思考，并在循环中按需调用 `ctx.longtask:feed()`，AI 落子，再一次局部刷。不要在同一次回调中连续计算多步。

在 Studio 中，`ctx.longtask:start()` 和 `ctx.longtask:feed()` 返回 `true`，但不执行 11 秒的截止限制。`ctx.longtask:stop()` 会请求退出，不会抛出设备上的那种 Lua 错误。

## 联网

如何组织一次请求，见「XTApp ScriptNet 联网路由」。本节介绍调用本身。

Manifest 声明 `"permissions": ["net.http"]` 之后，可以使用异步的 HTTP GET 和 POST，只支持 `http://`。请求从生命周期回调中发出，并在之后的 `on_tick` 中轮询，不要阻塞等待结果。

- `ctx.net:get(url)` 与 `ctx.net:post(url, body[, headers])`：成功时返回任务 ID，失败时返回 `nil, err`
- `ctx.net:poll(task_id)`：返回包含 `done/ok/status/body/err/bytes` 的结果
- `ctx.net:cancel(task_id)`：取消不再需要的任务

## 其它命名空间

其余调用按名字查阅。判断某个方法是否存在时使用点号，例如 `if ctx.i18n and ctx.i18n.t then`；实际调用时使用冒号。

- `ctx.display:full_refresh()`、`ctx.display:defer_auto_full(ms)`
- `ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()`
- `ctx.i18n.locale` 与 `ctx.i18n:t(key)`
- `ctx.perf:info()`：返回 `tick_us/draw_us/cmd_count/image_count/asset_hit/asset_miss/draw_frame`。Studio 只保证这些字段存在，其数值不代表真机
- `ctx.gc:count()`、`ctx.gc:collect()`
- `ctx.input.caps`、`ctx.input:has_key(key)`、`ctx.input:has_bt_keyboard()`、`ctx.input:has_bt_gamepad()`。后两项目前固定返回 `false`
- `ctx.lock:flush_once(mode)`、`ctx.lock:set_interval(seconds)`。`ctx.lock` 还公开 `reason/base_page/elapsed_sec/interval_sec/clear_background`
- `ctx.assets:evict(key)`、`ctx.assets:info(key)`、`ctx.assets:handle(key)`。`handle()` 返回 `handle/asset_key/width/height`，`info()` 返回 `used/limit/count`
- `ctx.data:exists(name)`、`ctx.data:size(name)`、`ctx.data:read_text(name)`、`ctx.data:open_text(name)`。`open_text()` 支持 `max_bytes/max_line_bytes`，reader 提供 `read_line()`、`seek()`、`tell()`、`close()`。失败码包括 `invalid_name/not_found/read_failed/line_too_long`
- `ctx.layers:create(width, height)`

## 离屏图层

不常变化的图形可以先绘制到一块缓冲区上，再在 `on_draw` 中贴到屏幕上：

```lua
local layer

function on_load(ctx)
  layer = ctx.layers:create(160, 80)
  layer:draw_with(function(g)
    g:rect(0, 0, 160, 80, "stroke", 15)
  end)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:layer(layer, 20, 20)
end
```

图层的宽高必须是正数，并且不得超过公开契约的限制。不要嵌套 `draw_with`。不再使用的图层应调用 `layer:dispose()`。离屏图层用于缓存静态几何图形或图片，不会放大文字，`layer:draw_with` 中也不能调用 `g:text`。

## data 与 i18n

只读表格和多语言文本放在文件中，不写入 Lua。

数据文件必须列在 manifest 的 `data_files` 中。`ctx.data` 只接受文件名，不接受路径。TSV 的第一行可以作为表头。

多语言文本放在 `lang/<locale>.tsv` 中，每行为 `key<TAB>value`。缺少某条翻译时，应用应自行保留一句可读的 fallback。

## 锁屏

锁屏是另一个入口，与普通应用分开运行。它每次只绘制一帧，并重新执行入口，收不到普通应用的按键或触摸。需要跨帧保留的数据放在 `ctx.state` 中，并且必须调用一次 `ctx.lock:flush_once("partial"|"full")`。不要把锁屏的 `on_input` 当作可靠的交互入口，也不要依靠模块级全局变量、`on_leave` 或 `on_unload` 保存锁屏状态。

## 语言

使用的语言是 Lua 5.5。可以使用 `global` 声明、变量属性（`<const>` / `<close>`）和具名可变参数。整数和浮点数的范围见下一节。

在 Studio 中可以用 `require("project.module")` 把本工程拆分为多个文件，参数必须是字面模块名。运行到设备上时，这些文件已合并进入口，不存在 `require`。不能把 `require` 赋给其他名字再调用，也不能在运行时拼接模块名。

## 数字

计数、下标和循环变量写成普通整数即可。接近边界时，再参考以下内容。

整数是 32 位有符号整数，`math.maxinteger` 为 `2147483647`。浮点数是单精度。能放入 32 位整数的字面量保持为整数，例如 `1111111109`。更大的数会变成浮点数，`tostring(20000000000)` 为 `2e+10`。浮点数只能精确表示 `2^24`（`16777216`）以内的连续整数。整数加、减、乘超出 32 位时按二进制补码环绕，结果仍是整数。除法 `/` 和乘方 `^` 的结果是浮点数，超过 `2^24` 后会丢失低位。位运算和整数除法 `//` 在结果仍能放入 32 位整数时保持精确。不要用 Lua 浮点数做动态截断，也不要对很大的时间戳取模。钟面读取 `ctx.sys:clock()` 的 `hour` 和 `minute`。计数器和校验值保存为整数或字节串。

## 安全限制

应用可以使用的是公开的 `ctx` 和 `g`。以下名字不存在：`io`、`os`、`package`、`debug`、`dofile`、`loadfile`、`load`、`require`、`collectgarbage`、`print`。字符串的元表不能替换。需要日志、垃圾回收或联网时，使用 `ctx.log`、`ctx.gc` 和 `ctx.net`。

在 Studio 中用 `require("project.module")` 拆分的文件，会在运行前合并进入口。设备上仍然没有 `require`，也不能任意访问文件。
entries.example:
function on_load(ctx) end
function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end
function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms) end
function on_input(ctx, ev) return false end

# `app_id` and store issuance

`app_id` is the install identity of an application on the device. The name users see comes from `display_name`. Since 2.5, you can add per-language names in `display_names` (keys are `ctx.i18n.locale` values, e.g. `{ "en": "Focus Timer", "de": "Fokus-Timer" }`), and the device selects one based on its system language. Before you package or submit, check that the project's `app_id` follows the rules on this page.

## Format

The format is `<lowercase-prefix>-<8 lowercase hex digits>`, for example `u-3f9a0c21`.

The last 8 digits are random, not a content fingerprint. Editing code, validating, and packaging never change them.

## When it is created and issued

| Situation | `app_id` |
| --- | --- |
| New project | Generated by Studio |
| Remix from the store, copy a template | Replaced with a new `u-xxxxxxxx`; the source id is not kept |
| First submission | Issued by the platform as `u-xxxxxxxx` and written back to the project; authors cannot choose it |
| Later submissions of the same product | Unchanged |

If you set a custom value such as `once_again-…` locally, the first submission replaces it with the issued `u-…`. This is expected behavior.

## After release

- **Do not change `app_id`.** A different `app_id` is a different application; existing private files on the device are not carried over.
- **Ship new content by changing only `version`.** Installing the same `app_id` again is an upgrade and keeps private files.

# `app_id` 与商店签发

`app_id` 是应用在设备上的安装身份；用户看到的名称由 `display_name` 决定。自 2.5 起，可以在 `display_names` 中按语言分别填写名称（键为 `ctx.i18n.locale` 的取值，如 `{ "zh": "专注计时", "en": "Focus Timer" }`），设备按系统语言选取。打包或送审之前，请确认工程中的 `app_id` 符合本页规则。

## 格式

格式为 `<小写前缀>-<8 位小写十六进制>`，例如 `u-3f9a0c21`。

后 8 位是随机值，不是内容指纹。修改代码、校验、打包都不会改变它。

## 何时生成与签发

| 场景 | `app_id` |
| --- | --- |
| 新建工程 | 由 Studio 生成 |
| 从商店 Remix、复制模板 | 替换为新的 `u-xxxxxxxx`，不沿用来源的值 |
| 首次送审 | 由平台签发 `u-xxxxxxxx` 并写回工程，作者不能指定 |
| 同一商品再次送审 | 保持不变 |

在本地改为 `once_again-…` 这类自定义值后，首次送审时会被平台签发的 `u-…` 覆盖。这是正常行为。

## 发布之后

- **不要修改 `app_id`。** 更换 `app_id` 即成为另一个应用，设备上原有的私有文件不会迁移。
- **发布新内容只修改 `version`。** 以同一 `app_id` 再次安装即为升级，私有文件保留。

entries.content:
# Online games (WebSocket)

This guide shows how to build online games with the API 2.6 WebSocket, using online gomoku as the example: the server decides and pushes the whole state on every change; the app reconnects after a few seconds and keeps the seat token in `ctx.state`; the game supports both touch and keys; the Studio preview connects only to `wss://`.

## Choose the connection first

Choose by the pace of the game:

| Game | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn-based, slow-paced (chess, gomoku, crosswords, daily puzzle) | `ctx.net:request`, polling every few seconds while waiting; or WebSocket | One request per move is enough; since 2.6, consecutive requests reuse the connection |
| Must see the other player's action immediately (card games, draw-and-guess, quizzes, chat) | `ctx.net:websocket` | The server pushes each message as soon as it exists, with no polling |
| Fast action (shooters, racing, fighting) | Not suitable | An e-ink refresh takes hundreds of milliseconds, so players cannot see changes that fast |

WebSocket is available since API 2.6; put `"api": "2.6"` in the manifest. The device supports only HTTP(S) and WebSocket, not raw TCP or UDP. Write the server to the standard WebSocket protocol; any server a browser can reach, the device can reach too.

Only one WebSocket connection can exist at a time: opening another while the old one has not ended (including while it is closing) returns `nil, "busy"`. `request` keeps working while the connection is open. For the full rules, see contract section 14, "WebSocket".

## The server decides: designing the messages

The device sends only "what I want to do" (create a room, place a stone, play again); the server decides and pushes the result to everyone in the room. Disconnects, cheating, and two players acting at once are all handled in one place on the server; the device never changes the board on its own.

The simplest approach is to **push the whole room state on every change**; the device replaces everything and redraws. States arrive in order on one connection, so the last one is the newest. Messages need a sequence number, so that old ones can be dropped, only when you push deltas.

In the online gomoku example, every message is short JSON, and `t` is its kind:

| Direction | Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| device → server | `{t="list"}` | Request the lobby's room list |
| | `{t="create"}` / `{t="join", id="4821"}` | Create / join a room |
| | `{t="resume", token=...}` | Return to the same seat after a disconnect |
| | `{t="move", x=7, y=7}` | Place a stone |
| | `{t="again"}` / `{t="leave"}` | Play again / leave the room |
| server → device | `{t="rooms", rooms={{id, host, n}, ...}}` | Lobby list, pushed whenever it changes |
| | `{t="state", id, token, you, opp, opp_online, phase, board, next, winner, line, last}` | The whole room state; `board` is a 225-character string, with `.` for empty, `b` for black, and `w` for white |
| | `{t="error", code="not_your_turn"}` | The action was refused; sent only to the player who attempted it |

Practical guidelines:

- Encode bulky data such as the board as one string. It is smaller than nested arrays, and Lua reads it with `board:sub(i, i)`.
- Use fixed short English error codes and convert them into hints (`toast`) on the device; the server does not handle UI text.
- The server gives each seat a random token. The device stores it and uses it to reclaim the seat after reconnecting.
- Keep messages small: a sent message is at most 65536 bytes and a received message at most 131072 bytes; beyond that, the host closes the connection with 1009.

## Connecting, disconnects and reconnecting

Disconnects will happen: leaving Wi-Fi range, a server restart, or 45 seconds without any data from the other side (which the host reports as `timeout`) all end the connection. The host does not reconnect automatically. It calls `on_close`, and the app decides when to connect again.

```lua
local URL = "wss://game.example.com/gomoku/ws"
local conn            -- the WebSocket while connected
local retry_ms = 2000
local room            -- room state pushed by the server; nil in the lobby

local connect

local function on_message(ctx, ws, data)
  local msg = ctx.json:decode(data)
  if type(msg) ~= "table" then return end
  for k, v in pairs(msg) do         -- JSON null decodes to ctx.json.null
    if v == ctx.json.null then msg[k] = nil end
  end
  if msg.t == "state" then
    room = msg
    ctx.state.token = msg.token     -- keep the seat token
  elseif msg.t == "rooms" then
    room = nil
    ctx.state.token = nil
  elseif msg.t == "error" and msg.code == "no_seat" then
    ctx.state.token = nil           -- the seat expired: back to the lobby
    room = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

connect = function(ctx)
  local ws = ctx.net:websocket({ url = URL }, {
    on_open = function(c, w)
      retry_ms = 2000
      if c.state.token then         -- was in a room last time: reclaim the seat
        w:send(c.json:encode({ t = "resume", token = c.state.token }))
      end
    end,
    on_message = on_message,
    on_close = function(c, w, code, reason, err)
      conn = nil
      c:after(retry_ms, connect)    -- reconnect later, doubling the wait after each failure
      retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
      c:invalidate()
    end,
  })
  if ws then
    conn = ws
  else                              -- busy and the like: try again later
    ctx:after(retry_ms, connect)
    retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
  end
end

function on_load(ctx)
  connect(ctx)
end
```

Key points:

- `on_close` is called exactly once per connection, and you can open a new connection immediately. Start the retry interval at 2 seconds, double it after each failure, and cap it at 30–60 seconds; reset it in `on_open`.
- After reconnecting, do not assume that nothing happened while disconnected: on `resume`, the server sends the full state again. The server keeps a dropped seat for a period of time (60 seconds in the gomoku example) and answers `no_seat` after that, and the device returns to the lobby.
- Keep the seat token in `ctx.state` (saved automatically since API 2.2; see contract section 28). After the user leaves the app or locks the screen and then reopens the app, the `resume` in `on_open` returns to the same game.
- When the app exits, the screen locks, or the device powers off, the host closes the connection with 1001 and does **not** call `on_close`; the next launch reconnects from `on_load`.
- When the app calls `ws:close()` itself, `on_close` receives `err` as nil and the code the app passed. This ending is deliberate, so do not reconnect.
- `ctx.json:decode` decodes JSON `null` as `ctx.json.null`, not nil. For fields the server may send as `null`, replace the value with nil first, then test with `if msg.winner then`.
- The host handles the heartbeat (a ping after 20 seconds of idle time). The app does not need to implement one, and the server does not need to send extra heartbeats for the device.

## Lobby and room: screens and input

An online game usually has two screens: the **lobby** lists rooms waiting for a player plus a "Create room" button; the **room** draws the board and a status line. The server's latest message decides which screen is shown (a `state` enters the room, and a `rooms` returns to the lobby); the device never switches on its own.

The status line turns the server's state into one sentence so that players know what to do: "Waiting for an opponent", "Your turn (black)", "Waiting for the opponent…", "Opponent disconnected, waiting…", "You won!". Show a lost connection as well ("Disconnected, reconnecting…").

**A failed send does not change local state.** While the app is not yet connected or is reconnecting, `ws:send` returns nil:

```lua
local function send(ctx, msg)
  if conn and conn:send(ctx.json:encode(msg)) then return true end
  ctx.dialog:toast("Not connected yet, please wait")
  return false
end
```

Placing a stone also only calls `send(ctx, { t = "move", x = x, y = y })`; the stone is drawn when the server's `state` arrives.

**Support both touch and keys** (x4_pro has touch, and x4_classic has keys only):

- Touch: the first tap on a point selects it and draws a cursor; a second tap on the same point places the stone, so that an accidental touch does not play a move. When the user taps the same point twice quickly, the second tap has the `gesture` `double_tap` (the first already arrived as `tap`); treat it as the second tap on the board.
- Keys: the arrow keys move the cursor, and `ok` places a stone. In the lobby, up and down move the focus, and `ok` enters the room.
- Use `ctx.input.pointer` to check whether touch is available. Without touch, always draw the cursor and the focus frame, and show a key hint at the bottom.
- In the room, the back key first asks with `ctx.dialog:confirm` ("Leave the room?") and sends `leave` on confirmation; in the lobby, return `false` and let the host exit.

**Redraw only when the state changes.** Call `ctx:invalidate()` only when `on_message` receives a message; several consecutive messages still produce a single draw.

## Power and ending a game

While the connection is open, Wi-Fi stays on, and the host may also turn off Wi-Fi power saving for lower latency, so power consumption is higher than usual.

- When the game ends or nobody has acted for a long time, call `ws:close()` (close code 1000; do not reconnect in `on_close`).
- In phases that are not time-critical, such as the lobby or waiting for a match, you can use `request` every few seconds instead, and open the WebSocket once the player is in a room.
- While the app is paused (contract section 2), the connection stays open and messages are queued; they are delivered in order after `on_resume`. If the queued messages exceed 262144 bytes, the host closes the connection with 1009, and `err` is `limit_exceeded`.

## Testing in the preview and on a device

The Studio preview uses the browser's WebSocket, which differs from the device in the following ways:

| | Device | Studio preview |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws://` | Connects | Does not connect: ends with 1006 `io_error` and writes one log line (Studio is an https page, and the browser does not allow `ws://`) |
| `wss://` | Connects, verified against built-in root certificates | Connects |
| `headers` | Sent | Logged and ignored: put authentication in a URL query parameter or the first message |
| Heartbeat | Ping at 20 seconds, disconnect after 45 | Handled by the browser |

Therefore:

- To test a server in the preview, give it a domain name and a TLS certificate, and use `wss://`.
- Test LAN servers and IP-only `ws://` servers on a device: the preview shows only "disconnected" and that log line.
- Do not rely on `headers` alone for authentication. Put it in the URL or in the first message after connecting, which works both in the preview and on the device.
- Test reconnection on a device: switch off the router or restart the server while connected, and check that the status line and `resume` bring the player back to the same game.

# 联机游戏（WebSocket）

说明如何用 API 2.6 的 WebSocket 实现联机对战，以联机五子棋为例：由服务器判定，每次推送完整状态；断线后间隔几秒重连，座位 token 保存在 `ctx.state` 中；同时支持触摸和按键操作；Studio 预览只能连接 `wss://`。

## 先选连接方式

根据游戏节奏选择：

| 游戏 | 使用的接口 | 原因 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 回合制、慢节奏（象棋、五子棋、填字、每日一题） | `ctx.net:request`，等待对方时每隔几秒查询一次；或 WebSocket | 每一步发送一个请求即可；自 2.6 起，连续请求复用同一连接 |
| 需要立即得知对方动作（斗地主、你画我猜、多人答题、聊天） | `ctx.net:websocket` | 服务器有消息时立即推送，无需轮询 |
| 高速动作（射击、赛车、格斗） | 不适合 | 墨水屏刷新需要几百毫秒，玩家无法看到如此快速的变化 |

自 API 2.6 起提供 WebSocket，在 manifest 中写入 `"api": "2.6"`。设备只支持 HTTP(S) 和 WebSocket，不支持裸 TCP 和 UDP。服务器按通用 WebSocket 协议实现即可；浏览器能连接的服务器，设备也能连接。

同一时间只能有一条 WebSocket 连接。旧连接尚未结束（包括正在关闭）时再次建立连接，返回 `nil, "busy"`；连接打开期间，`request` 仍可正常使用。接口的完整规则见契约第 14 节「WebSocket」。

## 服务器说了算：怎样定消息

设备只发送「我想做什么」（建房、落子、再来一局），服务器判定后把结果推送给房间里的每个人。断线、作弊和两人同时操作都集中在服务器处理，设备不自行修改棋盘。

最简单的做法是：**每次变化都推送完整的房间状态**，设备收到后整体替换并重绘。在同一条连接上，状态按顺序到达，后到达的就是最新状态；只有推送增量时，才需要给每条消息加序号并丢弃过时的消息。

以联机五子棋为例，所有消息都是短 JSON，`t` 表示消息种类：

| 方向 | 消息 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 设备 → 服务器 | `{t="list"}` | 请求大厅的房间列表 |
| | `{t="create"}` / `{t="join", id="4821"}` | 建房 / 进房 |
| | `{t="resume", token=...}` | 断线后回到原来的座位 |
| | `{t="move", x=7, y=7}` | 落子 |
| | `{t="again"}` / `{t="leave"}` | 再来一局 / 离开房间 |
| 服务器 → 设备 | `{t="rooms", rooms={{id, host, n}, ...}}` | 大厅列表，有变化时推送 |
| | `{t="state", id, token, you, opp, opp_online, phase, board, next, winner, line, last}` | 完整的房间状态；`board` 是 225 个字符的字符串，`.` 表示空、`b` 表示黑、`w` 表示白 |
| | `{t="error", code="not_your_turn"}` | 操作被拒绝，只发给执行该操作的玩家 |

实践要点：

- 将棋盘这类大块数据编码为一个字符串，体积比嵌套数组小，在 Lua 中用 `board:sub(i, i)` 读取。
- 错误码使用固定的英文短词，由设备转换为提示（`toast`）；服务器不处理界面文字。
- 服务器为每个座位分配一个随机 token，设备保存该 token，断线重连时用它认领原座位。
- 消息应尽量小：发送的单条消息最多 65536 字节，接收的单条消息最多 131072 字节，超出时宿主以 1009 关闭连接。

## 连接、断线与重连

断线必然会发生：离开 Wi-Fi 范围、服务器重启、对方 45 秒内没有任何数据（宿主判定为 `timeout`），都会导致连接断开。宿主不会自动重连；连接断开时宿主调用 `on_close`，由应用决定何时重新连接。

```lua
local URL = "wss://game.example.com/gomoku/ws"
local conn            -- 连着时的 WebSocket
local retry_ms = 2000
local room            -- 服务器推来的房间状态；nil 时在大厅

local connect

local function on_message(ctx, ws, data)
  local msg = ctx.json:decode(data)
  if type(msg) ~= "table" then return end
  for k, v in pairs(msg) do         -- JSON 的 null 解出来是 ctx.json.null
    if v == ctx.json.null then msg[k] = nil end
  end
  if msg.t == "state" then
    room = msg
    ctx.state.token = msg.token     -- 座位 token 存起来
  elseif msg.t == "rooms" then
    room = nil
    ctx.state.token = nil
  elseif msg.t == "error" and msg.code == "no_seat" then
    ctx.state.token = nil           -- 座位过期：回大厅
    room = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

connect = function(ctx)
  local ws = ctx.net:websocket({ url = URL }, {
    on_open = function(c, w)
      retry_ms = 2000
      if c.state.token then         -- 上次在房间里：认回座位
        w:send(c.json:encode({ t = "resume", token = c.state.token }))
      end
    end,
    on_message = on_message,
    on_close = function(c, w, code, reason, err)
      conn = nil
      c:after(retry_ms, connect)    -- 隔一会儿重连，失败一次间隔加倍
      retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
      c:invalidate()
    end,
  })
  if ws then
    conn = ws
  else                              -- busy 等情况：过一会儿再试
    ctx:after(retry_ms, connect)
    retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
  end
end

function on_load(ctx)
  connect(ctx)
end
```

要点：

- 每条连接恰好调用一次 `on_close`，之后可以立即建立新连接。重连间隔从 2 秒开始，每失败一次加倍，上限为 30–60 秒；连接成功后在 `on_open` 中重置间隔。
- 重连后不要假设断线期间没有发生任何变化：服务器收到 `resume` 后会重新发送完整状态。服务器会为掉线的座位保留一段时间（五子棋示例中为 60 秒），超时后回复 `no_seat`，设备随之回到大厅。
- 座位 token 保存在 `ctx.state` 中（自 API 2.2 起自动存档，见契约第 28 节）。退出应用或锁屏后再次打开，`on_open` 中的 `resume` 即可回到原来的对局。
- 退出应用、进入锁屏或关机时，宿主以 1001 关闭连接，**不调用** `on_close`；下次打开时从 `on_load` 重新连接。
- 应用主动调用 `ws:close()` 时，`on_close` 的 `err` 为 nil，`code` 为传入的关闭码。这种结束是有意为之，不要重连。
- `ctx.json:decode` 把 JSON 的 `null` 解码为 `ctx.json.null`，而不是 nil。对于服务器可能发送 `null` 的字段，先替换为 nil，再用 `if msg.winner then` 判断。
- 心跳由宿主处理（空闲 20 秒后发送 ping），应用无需自行实现；服务器也无需为设备额外发送心跳。

## 大厅与房间：界面与操作

联机游戏通常有两个画面：**大厅**列出等待玩家加入的房间和一个「创建房间」按钮；**房间**绘制棋盘和状态行。显示哪个画面由服务器最近推送的消息决定（收到 `state` 时进入房间，收到 `rooms` 时回到大厅），设备不自行切换。

状态行把服务器的状态转换成一句话，让玩家立即知道下一步该做什么：「等对手进来」「轮到你（黑）」「等对手落子…」「对手掉线了，等他回来…」「你赢了！」。连接断开时也应显示出来（「连接断了，正在重连…」）。

**发送失败时不修改本地状态。** 尚未连接或正在重连时，`ws:send` 返回 nil：

```lua
local function send(ctx, msg)
  if conn and conn:send(ctx.json:encode(msg)) then return true end
  ctx.dialog:toast("还没连上服务器，稍等")
  return false
end
```

落子同样只调用 `send(ctx, { t = "move", x = x, y = y })`，等服务器返回 `state` 后再绘制棋子。

**同时支持触摸和按键操作**（x4_pro 有触摸屏，x4_classic 只有按键）：

- 触摸：第一次点击交叉点时选中该点并绘制光标，再次点击同一点时才落子，以免手指误触。快速连续点击同一点两次时，第二次的 `gesture` 为 `double_tap`（第一次已作为 `tap` 送达），在棋盘上按第二次点击处理。
- 按键：方向键移动光标，`ok` 落子。在大厅中，上下键移动焦点，`ok` 进入房间。
- 用 `ctx.input.pointer` 判断是否支持触摸：不支持时始终绘制光标和焦点框，并在底部显示操作提示。
- 在房间中按返回键时，先用 `ctx.dialog:confirm` 询问「离开房间？」，确认后发送 `leave`；在大厅中返回 `false`，由宿主退出应用。

**只在状态变化时重绘。** 仅在 `on_message` 收到消息时调用 `ctx:invalidate()`；连续收到多条消息也只绘制一次。

## 耗电与结束

连接打开期间 Wi-Fi 始终保持开启，宿主还可能关闭 Wi-Fi 省电模式以换取低延迟，因此耗电高于平时。

- 对局结束或长时间无人操作时，调用 `ws:close()`（关闭码 1000，`on_close` 中不再重连）。
- 在大厅、等待匹配等对实时性要求不高的阶段，也可以只用 `request` 每隔几秒查询一次，进入房间后再打开 WebSocket。
- 应用暂停期间（契约第 2 节），连接保持打开，消息进入队列，在 `on_resume` 之后依次交给应用；队列中的消息超过 262144 字节时，宿主以 1009 关闭连接，`err` 为 `limit_exceeded`。

## 在预览和设备上测试

Studio 预览使用浏览器的 WebSocket，与设备有以下几处不同：

| | 设备 | Studio 预览 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws://` | 可以连接 | 不连接：以 1006 `io_error` 结束，并写入一行日志（Studio 是 https 页面，浏览器不允许连接 `ws://`） |
| `wss://` | 可以连接，按内置根证书校验 | 可以连接 |
| `headers` | 发送 | 写入日志后忽略：鉴权信息放在 url 查询参数或第一条消息中 |
| 心跳 | 20 秒发送 ping，45 秒判定断线 | 由浏览器管理 |

因此：

- 如果要在预览中测试服务器，为它配置域名和 TLS 证书，并使用 `wss://`。
- 局域网服务器和只有 IP 的 `ws://` 服务器需要在设备上测试：在预览中只会看到「连接断了」和日志中的那一行。
- 鉴权不要只依赖 `headers`，应放在 url 或连接后的第一条消息中，这样预览和设备都能使用。
- 断线重连需要在设备上测试：在连接期间关闭路由器或重启服务器，检查状态行和 `resume` 能否让玩家回到原来的对局。
entries.example:
local URL = "wss://game.example.com/gomoku/ws"
local conn            -- 连着时的 WebSocket
local retry_ms = 2000
local room            -- 服务器推来的房间状态；nil 时在大厅

local connect

local function on_message(ctx, ws, data)
  local msg = ctx.json:decode(data)
  if type(msg) ~= "table" then return end
  for k, v in pairs(msg) do         -- JSON 的 null 解出来是 ctx.json.null
    if v == ctx.json.null then msg[k] = nil end
  end
  if msg.t == "state" then
    room = msg
    ctx.state.token = msg.token     -- 座位 token 存起来
  elseif msg.t == "rooms" then
    room = nil
    ctx.state.token = nil
  elseif msg.t == "error" and msg.code == "no_seat" then
    ctx.state.token = nil           -- 座位过期：回大厅
    room = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

connect = function(ctx)
  local ws = ctx.net:websocket({ url = URL }, {
    on_open = function(c, w)
      retry_ms = 2000
      if c.state.token then         -- 上次在房间里：认回座位
        w:send(c.json:encode({ t = "resume", token = c.state.token }))
      end
    end,
    on_message = on_message,
    on_close = function(c, w, code, reason, err)
      conn = nil
      c:after(retry_ms, connect)    -- 隔一会儿重连，失败一次间隔加倍
      retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
      c:invalidate()
    end,
  })
  if ws then
    conn = ws
  else                              -- busy 等情况：过一会儿再试
    ctx:after(retry_ms, connect)
    retry_ms = math.min(retry_ms * 2, 30000)
  end
end

function on_load(ctx)
  connect(ctx)
end

# Changing what the X4 Pro Home key does

A tap on the Home key below the X4 Pro screen (a key built into the touchscreen) reaches the app as `back` by default. You do not need a new function: perform your own action in the `up` event of `back` and return `true`, and a Home tap turns the page, refreshes, or opens a menu. Double tap and long press are controlled by system settings, and the app cannot intercept them; always leave a way to exit.

## What you can and cannot change

The system first handles the Home key according to Settings → Buttons → Bottom touch area. An app can take over only the tap:

| Action | Default | Can the app take it over? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tap | Back: the app receives `down` and `up` for `back` | Yes. Return `true` in `up`; the app stays open and performs its own action |
| Double tap | No action | No. When an action is set, the system performs it and the app receives nothing |
| Long press (500 ms by default) | Home: the session ends and `on_leave` is called | No |

- No interface reads or changes these system settings. The app sees only `back` and cannot tell whether it came from the Home key or from the back gesture at the screen edge.
- When the user sets the tap to Refresh or No action, or turns the Home key off, the app does not receive the tap.
- When the user sets an action for double tap, a tap arrives only after Tap delay (100 ms by default) confirms that it is not a double tap.
- On `x4_classic`, `back` is the physical Back key: you can take over a short press the same way, and holding the key for 1000 ms forces the app to exit, which the app cannot intercept.

For the full rules, see contract section 4, "Back".

## Example: a Home tap turns to the next page

The whole app treats a Home tap as "next page". Do this only on `x4_pro`; put an Exit control on the screen and let touch turn the page as well.

```lua
local page, pages = 1, 12
local is_pro = false
local W, H = 480, 800
local QUIT = { x = 0, y = 0, w = 120, h = 64 }   -- "Exit" in the top-left corner

function on_load(ctx)
  is_pro = ctx.device.model == "x4_pro"
end

local function next_page(ctx)
  page = page % pages + 1
  ctx:invalidate()
end

local function in_quit(x, y)
  return x >= QUIT.x and x < QUIT.x + QUIT.w and y >= QUIT.y and y < QUIT.y + QUIT.h
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "back" and is_pro then
    if ev.phase == "up" then next_page(ctx) end
    return true                -- consume back: the app stays open
  end
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.phase == "up" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    if in_quit(ev.x, ev.y) then
      ctx:quit()               -- the on-screen way out
    else
      next_page(ctx)           -- touch turns the page too, not only Home
    end
    return true
  end
  return false                 -- back on other devices ends up here: exits as usual
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  W, H = g:size()
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(QUIT.x + 8, QUIT.y + 8, QUIT.w - 16, QUIT.h - 16, { radius = 8 })
  g:text(QUIT.x + QUIT.w // 2, QUIT.y + 20, "Exit", { font = ctx.fonts.medium, align = "center" })
  g:text(W // 2, H // 2, page .. " / " .. pages, { font = ctx.fonts.large, align = "center" })
  if is_pro then
    g:text(W // 2, H - 60, "Home key or tap: next page", { align = "center" })
  end
end
```

- Act only in `up`. The return value of `down` has no effect; returning `true` for both only keeps the code short.
- If every `back` returns `true`, the user can leave the app only in other ways: the on-screen Exit calls `ctx:quit()`, or the user long-presses Home to go to the home screen. The user may set long press to No action, so do not remove the Exit control.
- Restrict this to `x4_pro` with `ctx.device.model`. On `x4_classic`, `back` is the physical Back key, and pressing it means the user wants to exit; do not change its meaning.
- The screen can say "Home key: next page", but do not ask the user to change system settings.

## Example: a Home tap opens and closes a menu

Games and reading apps often use Home as a menu key: a tap opens the menu, and another tap closes it. Put Exit inside the menu.

```lua
local menu_open = false

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "back" then
    if ev.phase ~= "up" then return true end
    if menu_open then
      menu_open = false        -- Home tap: close the menu
    else
      menu_open = true         -- Home tap: open the menu
    end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  -- put an "Exit" button in the menu that calls ctx:quit()
  return false
end
```

To go back level by level (close the menu if it is open, and exit at the outermost level), return `false` at the outermost level; see contract section 4, "Using Back as a function key". A Home tap can then still exit the app when the user has set long press to No action.

## Testing in the preview and on a device

- In the Studio preview, choose X4 Pro: the Back button below the preview, or the Backspace key, acts as a Home tap with default settings. Holding it for 1 second forces an exit, which is the physical Back key rule. On a device, a Home long press goes to the home screen after 500 ms by default, and the app does not receive it either.
- The preview cannot simulate the system Home settings. To test a tap set to Refresh or No action, the Home key turned off, or long press set to No action, change these settings on a device under Settings → Buttons → Bottom touch area.

Check the following:

1. A tap performs your function, and the app does not exit.
2. The same function is also available by touch.
3. The app can be exited without a Home long press: through an on-screen Exit, or by returning `false` at the outermost level.
4. After a Home long press goes to the home screen, reopening the app shows the correct state. `on_leave` is called when the session ends; keep everything that must be saved in `ctx.state`.
