## 整页示例：商店页

```lua widget=page_shop
-- 状态（文件顶层）
local goods = {
  { "面包", 12 }, { "药水", 40 }, { "绳索", 8 }, { "油灯", 25 },
  { "地图", 60 }, { "干粮", 15 }, { "火把", 6 }, { "斗篷", 90 },
  { "铁锅", 30 }, { "钓竿", 45 }, { "毛毯", 35 }, { "指南针", 70 },
}
local tab, page, pick, qty, money = 1, 1, 2, 1, 120

local function draw_good(g, r, item, st)
  local ink = 15
  if st.selected then g:rect(r.x, r.y + 4, r.w, r.h - 8, { fill = true, radius = 8 }) ink = 0
  elseif st.focused then g:rect(r.x, r.y + 4, r.w, r.h - 8, { radius = 8, line_width = 2 }) end
  g:text(r.x + 16, r.y + r.h // 2, item[1], { font = F.body, color = ink, valign = "middle" })
  g:text(r.x + r.w - 16, r.y + r.h // 2, item[2] .. "G", { font = F.body, color = ink, align = "right", valign = "middle", tabular = true })
end

-- on_draw 里，ui:begin_frame(g) 与 ui:end_frame() 之间
local price = goods[pick][2] * qty
ui:column("shop", { x = 0, y = 0, w = 480, h = 800, padding = 16, gap = 12, children = {
  { kind = "row", align_items = "center", children = {
    { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "杂货铺", font = F.title, bold = true, grow = 1 },
    { kind = "label", id = "money", text = money .. "G", font = F.body, w = "fit", tabular = true },
  } },
  { kind = "tabs", id = "cat", h = 52, items = { "全部", "食物", "工具" }, value = tab, gap = 4, radius = 8 },
  { kind = "list", id = "goods", grow = 1, row_h = 64, count = #goods, page = page, selected = pick,
    draw = function(g, r, i, st) draw_good(g, r, goods[i], st) end },
  { kind = "row", h = 52, gap = 12, align_items = "center", children = {
    { kind = "stepper", id = "qty", w = 180, value = qty, min = 1, max = 9 },
    { kind = "spacer" },
    { kind = "pager", id = "pg", w = 104, page = page, pages = 2, text = "" },
  } },
  { kind = "button", id = "buy", h = 64, radius = 8, emphasis = true, enabled = money >= price,
    text = "买入 · " .. price .. "G" },
} })

-- on_input 里，local id, action, v = ui:handle_event(ev) 之后
if action == "change" then
  if id == "cat" then tab, page = v, 1
  elseif id == "qty" then qty = v
  else page = v end
elseif action == "activate" then
  if id == "goods" then pick = v
  elseif id == "buy" then money = money - goods[pick][2] * qty end
end
```

页签 + 分页列表 + 步进器 + 翻页器 + 主按钮。列表设为 `grow = 1`，占满中间的高度；金额不足时，买入按钮设为 `enabled = false`。所有数值都保存在脚本中，每帧传入。

## 自己画：尺寸与配方

界面库未提供的样式用 `g` 绘制。以下各节列出设备系统界面所用的尺寸和绘制方法，坐标按 480 宽的竖屏给出，实际宽高通过 `g:size()` 获取。字号统一通过 `ctx.fonts:size(px)` 获取。

## 自己画：画布

| 项 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| 竖屏 | `480×800`（X4 Pro、X4 Classic） |
| 横屏 | `800×480` |
| 尺寸 | 下面的坐标按竖屏 `480` 宽给出。实际宽高通过 `g:size()` 获取，横屏时据此重新排布 |
| 边距 | `20` |
| 图标槽 | `36×36` |

local function edge_hint(g, x, text, font)

local function key_hints(ctx, g, labels)
  if ctx.input.pointer then return end
  local k, font = ctx.input.keys, ctx.fonts.medium
  local w, h = g:size()
  key_tab(g, 40, h, font, labels.back, k.ok and labels.ok or "")
  if k.left or k.right then
    key_tab(g, w - 224, h, font, k.left and labels.left or "", k.right and labels.right or "")
  end
  if k.up then edge_hint(g, 0, labels.up, font) end
  if k.down then edge_hint(g, w - 24, labels.down, font) end
end

## 自己画：蓝牙键盘（2.10）

用户在系统设置中连接的蓝牙键盘，无需应用做任何处理即可使用：方向键、PageUp、PageDown、Enter、Esc、Backspace 作为普通按键投递（`up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back`）；停靠键盘或文字输入打开时，可以直接打字。应用收不到其余的键。

如需获取每一个键（快捷键、打字游戏、终端），调用 `ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })`。每次打开应用时都处于未监听状态；键盘未连接时也可以调用，连接后生效。

```lua
local line = ""

function on_start(ctx)
  ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.source == "keyboard" then
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.text then line = line .. ev.text end
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.code == "Backspace" then line = line:sub(1, -2) end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

| 字段 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | `"keyboard"`。设备按键、翻页器的事件没有这个字段 |
| `key` | 方向键、PageUp/PageDown、Enter、Esc 仍为 `up` … `back`；其余键为 `"other"`，Backspace 也是如此 |
| `code` | 键位名，与浏览器的 `KeyboardEvent.code` 相同，例如 `KeyA`、`Digit1`、`Backspace` |
| `text` | 按美式布局和 Shift 状态输入的字符；只在 `down`、`repeat` 上提供，按住 Ctrl、Alt、Meta 时不提供 |
| `mods` | `{ shift, ctrl, alt, meta }` |
| `phase` | `down`、`repeat`（按住时连续投递）、`up` |

开始监听后，Backspace 不再作为返回键；`back` 仍可通过 Esc 或设备的返回键触发。由于大多数用户手边没有键盘，界面上应写明哪些键有作用：键盘只是额外的操作方式，仅用方向键和触摸也必须能完成整个应用的操作。

## 设计规范：墨水屏上的界面

| 规则 | 做法 |
| --- | --- |
| 只有黑白 | 普通帧只有纸色 0 和墨色 15。容器 `background` 用网点表示：0–2 为纸色；3–7 为浅网点，上面可以放黑字；8–12 为深网点，只用作色块，不放文字；13–15 为墨色 |
| 层级由字号和粗细区分 | 用 `ctx.fonts:size(px)` 拉开字号差距（如 40 / 30 / 24 / 20），标题设置 `bold = true`；不要依靠灰色文字 |
| 数字不跳动 | 时钟、分数、倒计时使用 `tabular = true`；`w = "fit"` 中的数字加 `reserve`，按最宽的取值预留宽度 |
| 只有一个主操作 | 每屏只有一个 `emphasis` 按钮，其余按钮使用描边样式 |
| 当前项 | 菜单、宫格中的当前项使用 `selected`（反白）；顶部页签使用视觉更轻的 `selected_style = "underline"` |
| 换页全刷 | 打开新的一屏、切换页签、列表翻页时使用 `ctx:invalidate("full")`；同一页内的焦点、开关、计数变化使用 `ctx:invalidate()` |
| 不做动画 | 一帧约需 0.5 秒：不绘制按下状态，不做过渡效果；点按的反馈就是下一帧 |
| 热区 | 可点击的元素至少为 44×44，翻页箭头为 78×78 |
| 键盘区 | 在有输入框的页面上，底部 `ctx.input.keyboard_h` 像素留给系统键盘 |
| 两种设备 | 同一屏既要能只用方向键 + `ok` 完成全部操作（X4 Classic），也要能直接点击操作（X4 Pro）。不要按机型分支，而是按 `ctx.input.pointer` 判断 |
| 文字宽度 | 字体由用户选择，宽度一律实测（`font:measure`），不按字数估算；放不下时使用 `font_min` 或省略号 |

entries.content:
# XTApp usage ladder

The sections are ordered by the dependencies between structures. Each section covers one structure and points to a single-file example. The examples include no image pack, and the request host is not a live service.

An information app needs only the structures up to the screen state machine. Read the later sections when you need rule checks, frame-by-frame presentation, or a node table.

## Persistent state

Store values that must persist after the app is reopened in `ctx.state`. It accepts only strings, booleans, finite numbers, and plain tables. Call `ctx:invalidate()` after each change. Keep each counter in a single field.

Example: `state-counter.lua`. `up` and `down` change the value, and `ok` resets it.

## Key stepper

Each `ev.key` changes one field and then calls `ctx:invalidate()`. Return `false` for keys you do not handle. Draw the result and the step in separate rectangles.

Example: `calculator.lua`. `up` and `down` add or subtract the step, `left` and `right` change the step, and `ok` clears the result. The file demonstrates a stepper and does not implement arithmetic.

## Line reads from data_files

Store entries in text files declared in `manifest.data_files`, and read them line by line with `ctx.data:open_text`. Store progress, favorites, and the current index in `ctx.state`. Do not copy the whole file into state.

For a small file, see `data-i18n.lua`. Split a large file into fixed-size chunks, and open only the chunk that contains the current index on each read:

```lua
local CHUNK = 200

local function line_at(ctx, card_index)
  local shard = math.floor((card_index - 1) / CHUNK) + 1
  local row = (card_index - 1) % CHUNK + 1
  local name = string.format("words_%03d.tsv", shard)
  local reader = ctx.data:open_text(name, { max_bytes = 131072, max_line_bytes = 1024 })
  if not reader then return nil end
  local line
  for _ = 1, row do
    line = reader:read_line()
    if not line then break end
  end
  reader:close()
  return line
end
```

Use the declared file name, without a directory. State records only the indexes that have been read.

## Seven-segment digits and an offscreen layer

`g:text` has no font size. Build large digits as seven-segment figures with `g:rect`. Draw a panel that does not change over time into an offscreen layer, and stamp it with `g:layer` each frame.

Example: `layer-clock.lua`. For the lock-screen entry, see "App entry and lock-screen entry".

## Focus rectangles and hit testing

Key input and touch input must hit the same region. Write the position function once, and use its return value in both `on_draw` and hit testing. Show focus by filling the card and inverting its text. Do not change only a label.

Example: `focus-cards.lua`, with four cards. The directional keys move the focus, and `ok` or a tap opens the current card.

## Frame states after input

If an input only increments a counter, the next frame looks the same as the previous one. Drive several poses from one countdown, for example raised, struck, and resting. Store the session count and the total in separate fields. Do not record a streak of days when no calendar API is available.

Example: `tap-frames.lua`. `ok` or a tap on the figure starts a countdown, and `up` and `down` change the goal.

## Screen state machine

A list, a reading view, and a line-by-line reveal are three values of a single `screen` field, not three separate paint functions. Draw each hidden line with `g:line`. `back` returns to the previous screen based on the current value and does not exit immediately.

Example: `screen-modes.lua`.

## App entry and lock-screen entry

The main entry can call `ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()`. The lock screen is a separate entry: it calls the same draw function with the control flag set to false, then `ctx.lock:flush_once("partial")`. The lock screen does not receive the app's key input. Store data that must persist across frames in `ctx.state`.

```lua
local function draw_clock(ctx, g, show_controls)
  local h = ctx.screen.height
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, math.floor(h * 0.4), "12:00", { color = 15 })
  if show_controls then
    g:text(24, h - 48, "Set lock screen", { color = 15 })
  end
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" and ev.key == "ok" then
    ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  draw_clock(ctx, g, true)
end
```

The lock-screen entry keeps the time display and submits the frame:

```lua
function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  ctx.lock:set_interval(60)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  draw_clock(ctx, g, false)
  ctx.lock:flush_once("partial")
end
```

See `layer-clock.lua` for seven-segment digits. Both entries share this draw function.

## Legal action set

Rebuild the buttons from the current rules on every frame. Do not draw a primary action that the current rules reject. The view passed to another seat contains your own cards and the other seats' remaining card counts, but not their cards.

Example: `legal-actions.lua`. When the selected number cannot beat the target, PASS is the only button.

## Resolve, then draw in frames

For a swap or a play, write the final board first, then show the difference over a few frames: the original cells, a blank, and the settled board. Advance frames by accumulating `dt_ms` in `on_tick`. Do not move cells pixel by pixel.

Example: `discrete-waves.lua`.

## longtask time slice

Before a search inside one callback, call `ctx.longtask:start()`. The loop checks the wall-clock budget with `ctx.sys:millis()` and calls `ctx.longtask:feed()` about once every one or two seconds. When the budget runs out, return the best result found so far. When the search finishes normally, return directly. Do not call `ctx.longtask:stop()`. Use `stop()` only when the user explicitly cancels and leaves the app.

Example: `longtask-slice.lua`.

## HTTP get and poll

After the manifest declares `net.http`, call `ctx.net:get` in a lifecycle callback, `ctx.net:poll` in a later `on_tick`, and `ctx.net:cancel` when the app leaves. Do not block inside a callback. The sample host only illustrates the call shape.

Example: `net-poll.lua` requests `http://example.test/status`.

## Branching node table

Store nodes, body text, and choices in one table. `on_draw` reads only the current node. A single function computes the choice rectangles, and drawing and hit testing share its result. To change the content, replace the table. Do not write branches inside the paint function.

Example: `story-choice.lua`. A directional key or a tap writes the next node.

# XTApp 用法阶梯

各节按状态与绘制之间的依赖关系排序。每节介绍一种结构，并给出一份单文件示例。示例不含素材包，其中的请求地址也不是可用的主机。

信息类应用实现到屏幕状态机即可。需要规则判定、分帧结算或分支节点时，再阅读后面各节。

## 持久状态

应用关闭后再次打开时仍需保留的值放在 `ctx.state` 中。它只接受字符串、布尔值、有限数字和普通 table。修改后调用 `ctx:invalidate()`。同一个计数只放在一个字段中。

示例：`state-counter.lua`。`up` / `down` 修改数值，`ok` 将其归零。

## 按键步进

每个 `ev.key` 只修改一个字段，然后调用 `ctx:invalidate()`。未处理的按键返回 `false`。结果和步长分别绘制在两个矩形中。

示例：`calculator.lua`。`up` / `down` 按步长加减，`left` / `right` 修改步长，`ok` 将结果清零。该文件演示的是步进，不包含四则运算。

## data_files 行读取

词条放在 `manifest.data_files` 中声明的文本文件里，用 `ctx.data:open_text` 逐行读取。进度、收藏和当前下标保存在 `ctx.state` 中。不要把整份文件复制到状态中。

小文件的用法见 `data-i18n.lua`。大文件按固定行数切分为分片，每次只打开当前下标所在的分片：

```lua
local CHUNK = 200

local function line_at(ctx, card_index)
  local shard = math.floor((card_index - 1) / CHUNK) + 1
  local row = (card_index - 1) % CHUNK + 1
  local name = string.format("words_%03d.tsv", shard)
  local reader = ctx.data:open_text(name, { max_bytes = 131072, max_line_bytes = 1024 })
  if not reader then return nil end
  local line
  for _ = 1, row do
    line = reader:read_line()
    if not line then break end
  end
  reader:close()
  return line
end
```

文件名使用声明时的名称，不带目录。状态中只记录已读的下标。

## 七段数字与离屏层

`g:text` 没有字号参数。需要放大显示的数字用 `g:rect` 拼成七段数码。不随时间变化的底板绘制到离屏层中，每帧用 `g:layer` 贴上。

示例：`layer-clock.lua`。锁屏入口见「主入口与锁屏入口」。

## 焦点矩形与命中测试

方向键和触摸必须命中同一块区域。位置函数只写一次，`on_draw` 和命中测试共用它的返回值。当前焦点用填充和文字反相表示，不要只修改一行标签。

示例：`focus-cards.lua`。共四张卡片。方向键移动焦点，`ok` 或点击打开当前卡片。

## 输入后的多帧状态

如果一次输入只让计数加一，下一帧的画面与上一帧相同。用一个倒计时驱动几帧外形变化，例如抬起、落下、待机。本次计数和累计总数保存在不同的字段中。没有日历接口时，不要写入连续天数。

示例：`tap-frames.lua`。`ok` 或点击图形开始一次倒计时，`up` / `down` 修改目标值。

## 屏幕状态机

列表、阅读和逐行揭开是同一个 `screen` 字段的三个取值，而不是三个独立的绘制函数。尚未揭开的行用 `g:line` 绘制为一条线。按 `back` 时根据当前画面返回上一屏，不直接退出。

示例：`screen-modes.lua`。

## 主入口与锁屏入口

主入口可以调用 `ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()`。锁屏是另一个入口：调用同一个绘制函数，将控件参数设为 false，然后执行 `ctx.lock:flush_once("partial")`。锁屏不接收普通应用的按键。跨帧数据保存在 `ctx.state` 中。

```lua
local function draw_clock(ctx, g, show_controls)
  local h = ctx.screen.height
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, math.floor(h * 0.4), "12:00", { color = 15 })
  if show_controls then
    g:text(24, h - 48, "Set lock screen", { color = 15 })
  end
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" and ev.key == "ok" then
    ctx.system:set_as_lockscreen_app()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  draw_clock(ctx, g, true)
end
```

锁屏入口只保留时间显示和提交：

```lua
function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  ctx.lock:set_interval(60)
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  draw_clock(ctx, g, false)
  ctx.lock:flush_once("partial")
end
```

七段数字见 `layer-clock.lua`。两个入口共用这一套绘制。

## 合法操作集合

每帧都按当前规则重新计算按钮。当前规则不允许的主动作不要绘制。交给其他座位的视图只包含自己的牌和对方的剩余张数，不包含对方的牌。

示例：`legal-actions.lua`。所选数字不大于目标时，只显示 PASS 按钮。

## 结算后分帧绘制

交换或出牌时，先写入最终盘面，再把差异分几帧呈现：原样、空白、落定。在 `on_tick` 中累加 `dt_ms` 来切换帧。不要按像素逐步绘制下落。

示例：`discrete-waves.lua`。

## longtask 时间片

在一次回调内执行搜索前，先调用 `ctx.longtask:start()`。循环中用 `ctx.sys:millis()` 检查墙钟预算，大约每 1 到 2 秒调用一次 `ctx.longtask:feed()`。预算用完时返回当前的最优结果。正常结束时直接返回，不调用 `ctx.longtask:stop()`。`stop()` 只用于用户明确取消并离开的情况。

示例：`longtask-slice.lua`。

## HTTP 请求与 poll

在 manifest 中声明 `net.http` 后，在生命周期回调中调用 `ctx.net:get`，在之后的 `on_tick` 中调用 `ctx.net:poll`，离开时调用 `ctx.net:cancel`。不要在回调中阻塞等待。示例主机仅用于说明调用方式。

示例：`net-poll.lua`，请求 `http://example.test/status`。

## 分支节点表

节点、正文和选项放在同一张表中。`on_draw` 只读取当前节点。选项矩形由同一个函数计算，绘制和命中测试共用其结果。更换内容时替换这张表，不要把分支写进绘制函数。

示例：`story-choice.lua`。方向键或点击会写入下一个节点。

-- Example: a stepper. Up and down change the value. Left and right change the step. OK clears the value.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.calc then
    ctx.state.calc = { value = 0, step = 1 }
  end
  return ctx.state.calc
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then s.value = s.value + s.step
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.value = s.value - s.step
  elseif ev.key == "left" then s.step = math.max(1, math.floor(s.step / 10))
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.step = math.min(1000, s.step * 10)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.value = 0
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  local result_h = math.floor(h * 0.42)
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, result_h, "fill", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 0 })
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + math.floor(result_h * 0.45), tostring(s.value), { color = 0 })
  g:rect(margin, margin + result_h + 16, w - margin * 2, 72, "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + result_h + 40, "STEP " .. tostring(s.step), { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: read lines from a file declared in manifest.data_files. Progress stays in ctx.state.
local FILE = "items.tsv"

local function tr(ctx, key)
  if ctx.i18n and ctx.i18n.t then return ctx.i18n:t(key) end
  return key
end

function on_load(ctx)
  ctx.items = {}
  local reader = ctx.data:open_text(FILE)
  if not reader then return end
  reader:read_line()
  while true do
    local line = reader:read_line()
    if not line then break end
    local label, value = line:match("([^\t]+)\t([^\t]+)")
    if label then ctx.items[#ctx.items + 1] = { label = label, value = value } end
  end
  reader:close()
  if not ctx.state.index then ctx.state.index = 1 end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" or #ctx.items == 0 then return false end
  if ev.key == "down" or ev.key == "ok" then ctx.state.index = ctx.state.index % #ctx.items + 1
  elseif ev.key == "up" then ctx.state.index = (ctx.state.index - 2) % #ctx.items + 1
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, tr(ctx, "title"), { color = 15 })
  local item = ctx.items[ctx.state.index or 1]
  if item then
    g:text(24, 90, item.label, { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 130, item.value, { color = 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: the swap writes the final board immediately. on_tick only advances original, blank, and settled.
local PHASE_MS = { original = 400, blank = 500, settled = 400 }

local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.grid then
    ctx.state.grid = {
      board = { 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 },
      cursor = 3,
      animation = nil,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.grid
end

local function clone(board)
  local copy = {}
  for index = 1, 9 do copy[index] = board[index] end
  return copy
end

local function full_row(board)
  for row = 0, 2 do
    local a = row * 3 + 1
    if board[a] == 1 and board[a + 1] == 1 and board[a + 2] == 1 then
      return { a, a + 1, a + 2 }
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function adjacent(a, b)
  local ar, ac = math.floor((a - 1) / 3), (a - 1) % 3
  local br, bc = math.floor((b - 1) / 3), (b - 1) % 3
  return math.abs(ar - br) + math.abs(ac - bc) == 1
end

local function resolve_swap(board, a, b)
  if not adjacent(a, b) then return nil end
  local before = clone(board)
  before[a], before[b] = before[b], before[a]
  local cells = full_row(before)
  if not cells then return nil end
  local after = clone(before)
  for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do after[cell] = 0 end
  return { before = before, cells = cells, after = after, phase = "original", remaining = PHASE_MS.original }
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local animation = s.animation
  if not animation then return end
  animation.remaining = animation.remaining - (dt_ms or 0)
  if animation.remaining > 0 then return end
  if animation.phase == "original" then
    animation.phase = "blank"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.blank
  elseif animation.phase == "blank" then
    animation.phase = "settled"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.settled
    s.board = animation.after
  else
    s.animation = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.animation then return false end
  if ev.key == "left" then s.cursor = s.cursor - ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 0 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.cursor = s.cursor + ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 2 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "up" then s.cursor = math.max(1, s.cursor - 3)
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.cursor = math.min(9, s.cursor + 3)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then
    local partner = s.cursor < 9 and s.cursor + 1 or s.cursor - 1
    s.animation = resolve_swap(s.board, s.cursor, partner)
    if not s.animation then return false end
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local board = s.board
  local hidden = {}
  if s.animation and s.animation.phase == "blank" then
    board = s.animation.before
    for _, cell in ipairs(s.animation.cells) do hidden[cell] = true end
  elseif s.animation and s.animation.phase == "original" then
    board = s.animation.before
  end
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, "SWAP WITH RIGHT", { color = 15 })
  local origin_x, origin_y, cell = 24, 70, 72
  for index = 1, 9 do
    local column = (index - 1) % 3
    local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 3)
    local x = origin_x + column * (cell + 8)
    local y = origin_y + row * (cell + 8)
    local selected = index == s.cursor
    g:rect(x, y, cell, cell, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    if not hidden[index] and board[index] == 1 then
      g:circle(x + 36, y + 36, 16, "fill", selected and 0 or 15)
    end
  end
end

-- Example: one rectangle function for drawing and hit testing. The focused card is inverted.
local LABELS = { "NOW", "NEXT", "LATER", "NOTES" }

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.cards = ctx.state.cards or { selected = 1, opened = 0 }
  return ctx.state.cards
end

local function layout(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(20, math.floor(w * 0.05))
  local gap = 12
  local card_w = math.floor((w - margin * 2 - gap) / 2)
  local card_h = math.floor((h - margin * 2 - gap) * 0.42)
  return { margin = margin, gap = gap, card_w = card_w, card_h = card_h, cards_y = margin + 36 }
end

local function card_position(l, index)
  local column = (index - 1) % 2
  local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 2)
  local x = l.margin + column * (l.card_w + l.gap)
  local y = l.cards_y + row * (l.card_h + l.gap)
  return x, y
end

local function hit_card(l, x, y)
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local left, top = card_position(l, index)
    if x >= left and x <= left + l.card_w and y >= top and y <= top + l.card_h then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = s.selected - ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 0 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = s.selected + ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 1 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 2)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.selected = math.min(4, s.selected + 2)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.opened = s.selected
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_card(layout(ctx), ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index then return false end
    s.selected = index
    s.opened = index
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local l = layout(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(l.margin, 24, s.opened > 0 and ("OPEN " .. LABELS[s.opened]) or "PICK A CARD", { color = 15 })
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local x, y = card_position(l, index)
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, y, l.card_w, l.card_h, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 28, LABELS[index], { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: seven-segment digits from g:rect, with a static panel on an offscreen layer.
local panel

local DIGIT_SEGMENTS = {
  ["0"] = "abcdef", ["1"] = "bc", ["2"] = "abdeg", ["3"] = "abcdg",
  ["4"] = "bcfg", ["5"] = "acdfg", ["6"] = "acdefg", ["7"] = "abc",
  ["8"] = "abcdefg", ["9"] = "abcdfg",
}

local function has_segment(segments, name)
  return segments and string.find(segments, name, 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function draw_digit(g, x, y, digit, scale, color)
  local segments = DIGIT_SEGMENTS[digit]
  local t, w, h = 8 * scale, 46 * scale, 80 * scale
  local half = math.floor(h / 2)
  local vertical_h = half - t
  if has_segment(segments, "a") then g:rect(x + t, y, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "b") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "c") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "d") then g:rect(x + t, y + h - t, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "e") then g:rect(x, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "f") then g:rect(x, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "g") then g:rect(x + t, y + half - math.floor(t / 2), w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
end

local function draw_colon(g, x, y, scale, color)
  local dot = 8 * scale
  g:rect(x, y + 20 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
  g:rect(x, y + 52 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
end

local function two_digits(value)
  if value < 10 then return "0" .. tostring(value) end
  return tostring(value)
end

function on_load(ctx)
  panel = ctx.layers:create(320, 160)
  panel:draw_with(function(g)
    g:rect(0, 0, 320, 160, "stroke", 15)
    g:line(20, 124, 300, 124, 15)
  end)
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local key = clock.valid and string.format("%02d%02d", clock.hour, clock.minute) or "unset"
  if key ~= ctx.state.shown_minute then
    ctx.state.shown_minute = key
    ctx:invalidate()
  end
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local time = clock.valid and (two_digits(clock.hour) .. two_digits(clock.minute)) or "----"
  local scale, digit_w, gap, colon_w = 1, 46, 8, 18
  local time_w = digit_w * 4 + gap * 3 + colon_w
  local x = math.floor((ctx.screen.width - time_w) / 2)
  local y = math.floor((ctx.screen.height - 160) / 2)

  g:clear(0)
  g:layer(panel, math.floor((ctx.screen.width - 320) / 2), y - 40)
  draw_digit(g, x, y, string.sub(time, 1, 1), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 2, 2), scale, 15)
  draw_colon(g, x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2, y, scale, 15)
  local right_x = x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2 + colon_w
  draw_digit(g, right_x, y, string.sub(time, 3, 3), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, right_x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 4, 4), scale, 15)
end

function on_unload(ctx)
  if panel then panel:dispose() end
end

-- Example: buttons are rebuilt from the current rule. The public view omits other seats' cards.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.hand then
    ctx.state.hand = {
      mine = { 3, 9, 12 },
      remain = { 3, 5, 4 },
      target = 8,
      selected = 1,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.hand
end

local function public_view(s)
  return { own = s.mine, remain = s.remain, target = s.target }
end

local function actions(s)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local card = view.own[s.selected]
  if not card or card <= view.target then
    return { { id = "pass", label = "PASS" } }
  end
  return {
    { id = "play", label = "PLAY" },
    { id = "pass", label = "PASS" },
  }
end

local function apply(s, id)
  local row = actions(s)
  local allowed = false
  for _, action in ipairs(row) do
    if action.id == id then allowed = true end
  end
  if not allowed then return end
  if id == "play" then
    table.remove(s.mine, s.selected)
    s.selected = math.max(1, math.min(s.selected, #s.mine))
    s.remain[1] = #s.mine
    s.target = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  local row = actions(s)
  if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = math.min(#s.mine, s.selected + 1)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then apply(s, row[1] and row[1].id or "pass")
  elseif ev.key == "back" and row[2] then apply(s, row[2].id)
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 28, "TARGET " .. tostring(view.target), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, 64, "OTHERS " .. table.concat(view.remain, " "), { color = 15 })
  local x = 24
  for index, card in ipairs(view.own) do
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, 110, 64, 88, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 18, 146, tostring(card), { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
    x = x + 76
  end
  local row = actions(s)
  local button_w = math.floor((w - 24 * 2 - 12 * (#row - 1)) / math.max(1, #row))
  for index, action in ipairs(row) do
    local left = 24 + (index - 1) * (button_w + 12)
    g:rect(left, 230, button_w, 56, index == 1 and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(left + 16, 250, action.label, { color = index == 1 and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: ctx.longtask:start, then ctx.longtask:feed on a wall-clock budget. Return without stop().
local BUDGET_MS = 2000
local FEED_EVERY_MS = 1000

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.search = ctx.state.search or { best = 0, done = false }
  return ctx.state.search
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.done then return end
  local started_ok, start_err = ctx.longtask:start()
  if started_ok ~= true then
    s.best = 0
    s.done = true
    s.err = tostring(start_err or "inactive")
    ctx:invalidate()
    return
  end
  local started = ctx.sys:millis() or 0
  local fed_at = started
  local best = 0
  for step = 1, 40 do
    local now = ctx.sys:millis() or started
    if now - started >= BUDGET_MS then break end
    best = step
    if now - fed_at >= FEED_EVERY_MS then
      local fed_ok, feed_err = ctx.longtask:feed()
      if fed_ok ~= true then
        error("watchdog feed failed: " .. tostring(feed_err or "inactive"), 0)
      end
      fed_at = now
    end
  end
  s.best = best
  s.done = true
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, s.done and ("BEST " .. tostring(s.best)) or "SEARCH", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: start one GET, poll it from on_tick, and cancel it on leave.
-- The manifest must declare net.http. example.test is only a shape, not a live service.
local URL = "http://example.test/status"
local task_id

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.net = ctx.state.net or { status = "idle", body = "" }
  return ctx.state.net
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.status == "idle" and not task_id then
    local id, err = ctx.net:get(URL)
    if id then
      task_id = id
      s.status = "loading"
    else
      s.status = "error"
      s.body = tostring(err or "request failed")
    end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  if not task_id then return end
  local result = ctx.net:poll(task_id)
  if not result or not result.done then return end
  local s = state(ctx)
  task_id = nil
  if result.ok then
    s.status = "ready"
    s.body = tostring(result.body or "")
  else
    s.status = "error"
    s.body = tostring(result.err or result.status or "failed")
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  if task_id then ctx.net:cancel(task_id) end
  task_id = nil
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 40, s.status, { color = 15 })
  if s.body ~= "" then g:text(24, 88, s.body, { color = 15 }) end
end

-- Example: list, read, and reveal are three values of screen.
local LINES = {
  "The river is wide.",
  "A lamp marks the pier.",
  "You can still turn back.",
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.pages = ctx.state.pages or { screen = "list", recite = 0 }
  return ctx.state.pages
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then s.screen = "read"; s.recite = 0
    else return false end
  elseif s.screen == "read" then
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then s.screen = "recite"; s.recite = 0
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.screen = "list"
    else return false end
  else
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then
      s.recite = math.min(#LINES, s.recite + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then
      s.recite = math.max(0, s.recite - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then
      s.screen = "read"
    else return false end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    g:text(24, 48, "ONE POEM", { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 96, "OK TO OPEN", { color = 15 })
    return
  end
  g:text(24, 36, s.screen == "recite" and "REVEAL" or "READ", { color = 15 })
  for index, line in ipairs(LINES) do
    local y = 80 + (index - 1) * 48
    if s.screen == "recite" and index > s.recite then
      g:line(24, y + 16, math.min(w - 24, 24 + #line * 12), y + 16, 15)
    else
      g:text(24, y, line, { color = 15 })
    end
  end
end

-- Example: a counter stored in ctx.state. Up and down change it. OK resets it.
local function app_state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.counter then ctx.state.counter = 0 end
  return ctx.state
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then state.counter = state.counter + 1 end
  if ev.key == "down" then state.counter = math.max(0, state.counter - 1) end
  if ev.key == "ok" then state.counter = 0 end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, math.floor(h * 0.55), "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, math.floor(h * 0.38), tostring(state.counter), { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, h - margin - 28, "UP +  DOWN -  OK RESET", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: nodes and choices live in one table. Drawing and hit testing share choice rectangles.
local STORY = {
  start = {
    text = "A light is on at the end of the pier.",
    choices = {
      { label = "Walk closer", next = "pier" },
      { label = "Stay here", next = "stay" },
    },
  },
  pier = { text = "The lamp is warm. The path ends here.", choices = {} },
  stay = { text = "You wait. The light does not move.", choices = {} },
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.story = ctx.state.story or { node = "start", focus = 1 }
  return ctx.state.story
end

local function choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = 24
  local slot_h = 64
  local y = h - margin - (count - index + 1) * slot_h
  return margin, y, w - margin * 2, slot_h - 8
end

local function hit_choice(ctx, count, x, y)
  for index = 1, count do
    local left, top, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
    if x >= left and x <= left + width and y >= top and y <= top + height then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function choose(s, index)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choice = node and node.choices and node.choices[index]
  if not choice then return false end
  s.node = choice.next
  s.focus = 1
  return true
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local choices = (STORY[s.node] and STORY[s.node].choices) or {}
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "up" then s.focus = math.max(1, s.focus - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.focus = math.min(math.max(1, #choices), s.focus + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then
      if not choose(s, s.focus) then return false end
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_choice(ctx, #choices, ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index or not choose(s, index) then return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choices = node.choices or {}
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, node.text, { color = 15 })
  for index, choice in ipairs(choices) do
    local x, y, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, #choices)
    local selected = index == s.focus
    g:rect(x, y, width, height, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 22, choice.label, { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: one input starts a countdown across three poses. Session count and total stay in separate fields.
local RAISE_MS = 180
local HIT_MS = 220
local REST_MS = 200
local STRIKE_MS = RAISE_MS + HIT_MS + REST_MS

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.tap = ctx.state.tap or { session = 0, total = 0, goal = 8, strike_ms = 0 }
  return ctx.state.tap
end

local function pose(s)
  if s.strike_ms > HIT_MS + REST_MS then return "raise" end
  if s.strike_ms > REST_MS then return "hit" end
  return "rest"
end

local function strike(s)
  s.total = s.total + 1
  s.session = s.session + 1
  s.strike_ms = STRIKE_MS
  if s.session >= s.goal then
    s.session = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("high")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.strike_ms <= 0 then return end
  s.strike_ms = math.max(0, s.strike_ms - (dt_ms or 0))
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then strike(s)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.goal = math.min(36, s.goal + 4)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.goal = math.max(4, s.goal - 4)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.session = 0
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    strike(s)
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local cx, cy = math.floor(w / 2), math.floor(h * 0.46)
  local which = pose(s)
  local bob = which == "raise" and -36 or (which == "hit" and 18 or 0)
  g:clear(0)
  g:circle(cx, cy, 70, "stroke", 15)
  g:rect(cx - 10, cy - 110 + bob, 20, 70, "fill", 15)
  g:circle(cx, cy - 120 + bob, 16, "fill", 15)
  g:text(24, 28, "ROUND " .. tostring(s.session) .. "/" .. tostring(s.goal), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, h - 48, "TOTAL " .. tostring(s.total), { color = 15 })
end

# 0. General rules, an example, and Manifest

This directory is the author contract for API 2.x. The current minor version is 2.18. In `manifest.json`, set `"api": "2.0"`, `"2.1"`, `"2.2"`, `"2.3"`, `"2.4"`, `"2.5"`, `"2.6"`, `"2.7"`, `"2.8"`, `"2.9"`, `"2.10"`, `"2.11"`, `"2.12"`, `"2.13"`, `"2.14"`, `"2.15"`, `"2.16"`, `"2.17"`, or `"2.18"`. Anything marked 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.10, 2.11, 2.12, 2.13, 2.14, 2.15, 2.16, 2.17, or 2.18 exists only on hosts that implement that minor version; see section 19. The text is split into sections `00`–`30` and appendices A–C. “This document” refers to the whole set.

1. Every call you write has a defined result. An optional capability is either a function or nil (section 17).
2. One name does one thing. Each operation has only one spelling.
3. Passing a parameter of the wrong type (a number where a table is required, or nil where a string is required) raises a Lua error. Passing the right type with a value outside the stated range returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Device, file, quota, and network failures return `nil, err`.
4. Predicates (`exists`, `is_*`) return only booleans. A successful command returns nothing, a successful write or release returns true, and a query returns the requested value.
5. The host must implement everything except the optional capabilities listed in section 17.
6. Every rule has a conformance test (section 20). A host conforms when it passes those tests.

Error codes form a closed set; see section 18.

## Numeric parameters

A parameter described as an integer accepts integers directly. A float that equals an integer exactly (for example, `240.0` from `w / 2`) is accepted as that integer. Any other float, NaN, or infinity returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

Coordinates and sizes range over `-32768..32767`, unless a narrower range is specified elsewhere. Anything drawn outside the canvas is clipped; this is not an error.

A color is an integer in `0..15` that represents an amount of ink: `0` is paper (white), and `15` is the darkest ink (black).

You can omit an options table; omitting it is equivalent to passing an empty table. Unrecognized fields in an options table are ignored.

## A complete example

```lua
local F, count

function on_load(ctx)
  F = ctx.fonts
  local saved = ctx.storage:read("state.json")
  count = saved and ctx.json:decode(saved).count or 0
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear()
  g:text(w // 2, 40, ctx.i18n:t("title"), { font = F.large, align = "center" })
  g:rect(40, 120, w - 80, 80, { radius = 12 })
  g:text(w // 2, 160, tostring(count), { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.gesture == "tap"
     or ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "down" and ev.phase == "down" then
    count = count + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false            -- including back: hand control back; (2.7) the app exits after the user confirms
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  ctx.storage:write("state.json", ctx.json:encode({ count = count }))
end
```

## Manifest

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | `"2.<minor>"`. If the minor version is newer than the host supports, the install is refused. See section 19 |
| `app_id` | Application ID. 1–63 bytes, character set `[a-z0-9._-]`. Required |
| `display_name` | Display name. A non-empty string. Required |
| `display_names` | 2.5: display names per language. An object whose keys are the `locale` values from section 8 and whose values are non-empty strings. Optional. The host uses the first value present among `display_names[locale]`, `display_names.zh` (for `zh-TW`), `display_names.en` (for languages other than `zh` and `zh-TW`), and `display_name`. When the system language changes, the app list shows the new name the next time it is displayed. The packager rejects unknown keys and empty values; the host ignores them |
| `version` | The app's own version string. Required |
| `author` `description` | Strings. Optional |
| `app_icon_s` `app_icon_l` `splash` | Image keys in the package. Optional. See appendix A for suggested sizes |
| `entry` | Main script. Defaults to `index.lua` |
| `display.orientation` | `system`, `portrait`, or `landscape`. Defaults to `system`. It only sets the orientation at open; (2.18) during a session, `ctx.screen:set_orientation` can change it (section 3) |
| `requires` | An array of strings; see below. If the device does not meet any one of them, the app does not open (opening it reports `not_supported`; a host that can check at install time refuses the install) |
| `permissions` | An array of strings: `net` (section 14), `reader` (2.1, section 22). An unknown name causes the install to be refused |
| `preload_assets` | An array of image keys. A key that is not in the package causes the install to be refused. The images are decoded before `on_load`. A single failure does not block startup; `ctx.package:image` retries it later |
| `data_files` | Data files that `ctx.package` can read. An array of `{ name, format, max_bytes }`: `format` is `txt`, `tsv`, or `json`, the extension of `name` matches it, the file is stored under the package's `data/` directory, and its size does not exceed `max_bytes`. Otherwise, both packaging and installation fail |
| `ttf_reserve_kb` | An integer, 512–4096. (2.17) Hosts that implement 2.17 still accept it but ignore it; the host reserves TTF memory itself (section 7). New apps do not set it. On hosts of 2.16 and earlier, it determines how much TTF memory is reserved when the session starts |
| `lockscreen.entry` | Lock-screen script. Required when a `lockscreen` object is present. If the script is missing from the package, the install is refused |
| `lockscreen.interval_sec` | Integer. Defaults to 60. Clamped to 30–3600 at install |

Names that `requires` accepts:

| Name | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `pointer` | The device has a touchscreen |
| `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` | The device has this key built in (Bluetooth peripherals do not count) |
| `pattern` `image_transform` `ttf` `ui` | Optional capabilities from section 17. (2.17) On hosts that implement 2.17, `ttf` is never satisfied, and packages that list it do not open |
| `reader` `dialog` `frontlight` `image_decode` | 2.1 optional capabilities from section 17 |
| `nn` | 2.18, native inference from section 30; checked for the normal session |
| `lockscreen_timer` | The device can wake on a timer to refresh the lock screen |

An unknown name causes the install to be refused. Every device has `back`, so do not list it. The app's core flow uses only the inputs that `requires` guarantees, plus `back`.

entries.content:
# 1. Language and the sandbox

Lua 5.5, with 32-bit numbers: integers are signed 32-bit integers, and floats are single precision (`float`). The device processor has single-precision floating-point hardware only; 64-bit integers and double-precision arithmetic are emulated in software.

- `math.maxinteger` is `2147483647`, and `math.mininteger` is `-2147483648`. Integer addition, subtraction, and multiplication wrap around in two's complement when the result is out of range.
- Integer operations (`+ - * // %` and bitwise operations) produce integers. `/` and `^` produce floats.
- Single precision has about 7 significant digits, and the largest contiguous integer it represents exactly is `16777216`. Use integers and `//` for coordinates, counts, and amounts of money.

Available standard libraries: `base`, `table`, `string`, `math`, `utf8`, `coroutine`. `math.random` is seeded differently at the start of each session.

The following globals do not exist: `io`, `os`, `package`, `debug`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `load`, `print`, `collectgarbage`. `getmetatable("")` returns false; string methods work as usual.

`require(name)` loads only scripts in this package: it replaces `.` in the name with `/` and appends `.lua`. A module runs at most once per session; later calls return the cached result. If the module is not found, or the name contains `..` or starts with `/`, it raises the Lua error `module 'name' not found`.

## Memory

The script heap is at least 2 MB (not counting TTF memory). The actual size depends on the device's free memory. When the script's own allocation (creating a table, concatenating strings, and so on) fails, a Lua error (`not enough memory`) is raised, which `pcall` can catch. When a host function fails to allocate its result in the script heap (for example, the string returned by `ctx.zlib:decompress`), the same error is raised; functions whose error codes list `out_of_memory` instead return `nil, "out_of_memory"` as each section describes. When a result table the host delivers to a callback does not fit, it is handed to the app as each section specifies (for example, `err = "out_of_memory"` in section 14). Running out of memory only ends the current session; it does not restart the device. For garbage collection, see `ctx.gc` in section 12.

## Errors

If an error raised in a callback is not caught, or a callback runs out of time, the session ends: the host calls no further callbacks (including `on_leave`), shows an error screen, and then returns to the system. Files written before that point are kept.

# 2. Lifecycle

A session starts when it is loaded and ends when it leaves. When the session ends, the virtual machine is destroyed, and the next open starts a new session. State carries over only through the files in section 9 and (2.2) `ctx.state` in section 28.

Load order: `on_load`, then the host draws the first frame (it calls `on_draw`). During load, the screen keeps showing the picture from before the app opened; there is no splash image. When load takes longer than about 0.8 seconds, the host first shows the system opening page (this app's icon card and "Opening...", see appendix A, "Icons"). A lock-screen session (section 15) shows no opening page; the screen stays as it was before the lock. To show the first picture sooner, do only what the first frame needs in `on_load` and move the rest to later callbacks.

If a function is not defined, the host skips it.

| Function | When | Limit |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `on_load(ctx)` | The session loads | 2000 ms |
| `on_draw(ctx, g)` | A frame needs to be drawn. `g` is the canvas for this frame (section 6) | 1500 ms |
| `on_input(ctx, ev)` | A key press or pointer event (section 4). Return `true` to indicate that it was handled | 1000 ms |
| `on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)` | Called on the period set by `set_tick` | 1000 ms |
| `on_pause(ctx)` | A system screen covers the app (text input, a dialog, (2.7) the exit confirmation, and so on) | 1000 ms |
| `on_resume(ctx)` | The cover is dismissed. The host then redraws one frame | 1000 ms |
| `on_leave(ctx)` | The last callback before the session ends | 1000 ms |

The timer function of `ctx:after`, the completion functions of `ctx.net:request` and `ctx.input:text`, (2.1) the completion function of `ctx.dialog`, (2.6) the WebSocket `on_open`, `on_message`, and `on_close`, (2.9) the docked-input `on_change` and `on_end`, and (2.18) the completion function of native inference are also callbacks, with a limit of 1000 ms.

While the app is paused (from `on_pause` until `on_resume`), the host does not call `on_input`, `on_tick`, timer functions, completion functions, or (2.6) WebSocket callbacks. After `on_resume` returns, the host first redraws one frame, then calls, in order, the timer functions and completion functions that came due during the pause and the queued WebSocket callbacks.

Any callback can call the interfaces in this document (the canvas is valid only in `on_draw` and `layer:draw`), including starting a network request or setting a timer in `on_load`.

## Time budget

The limit is measured in wall-clock time from the start of the callback. The host checks it between Lua instructions. A slow host function (decoding an image, opening a font, reading or writing a file) is not interrupted; the check happens at the next instruction after the function returns. Exceeding the limit aborts the callback, and the error text contains `time budget`. After `pcall` catches it, the host raises it again at the next instruction. Running out of time ends the session just like an uncaught error (section 1, "Errors"): `on_leave` is not called, and (2.2) `ctx.state` is not saved automatically. The user sees the app quit unexpectedly.

```lua
local ok, err = ctx.budget:extend()
```

Moves the deadline of the current callback to 11000 ms after the call and returns true. The deadline is never later than 30000 ms after the callback started. When called from `on_leave`, in a lock-screen session (section 15), or outside a callback, it returns `nil, "inactive"`.

The following reference values were measured on the Gancao X4 Pro / X4 Classic (2026-10-16 firmware) and are not guarantees: one virtual machine instruction takes about 0.45 µs, and newly allocated memory takes about 0.2 µs per byte. Library calls such as `string.format` and string concatenation are similarly costly. For JSON and private file timings, see sections 10 and 9.

### When to call `extend`

When the work in a callback takes an unpredictable amount of time and may approach the limit, call `ctx.budget:extend()` once before you start it. The call itself takes almost no time and always returns true when it is available; calling it when it is not needed does no harm. Typical cases:

- AI thinking: search in board and card games, Monte Carlo simulation (for example, poker win probability), and pathfinding.
- Batch calculations done in a single pass: offline settlement in an idle game (section 28), generating a level or map, and simulating a whole game after shuffling.
- Large data: parsing or generating large JSON (section 10), paginating long text, and reading or writing private files in bulk (section 9).
- Setup in `on_load` and the first frame: opening TTFs at several new sizes at once (`ctx.fonts:size`, section 7) and decoding a large image (section 27). These run to completion inside a single host function, and their duration varies with the card and the font file, so they are the hardest to estimate in advance.

The call must come before the time-consuming code, and in the callback that actually runs that code: calling it in `on_input` does not extend a later `on_draw`. Do not call it repeatedly inside a loop. For a single computation longer than 11 seconds, call it again every few seconds of wall-clock time inside the loop; the total time still must not exceed 30 seconds after the callback started.

```lua
local function think(ctx, game)
  ctx.budget:extend()
  local stop = ctx.clock:millis() + 1500     -- its own budget: think for 1.5 seconds
  local best = first_legal_move(game)
  for depth = 1, 8 do
    local move = search(game, depth, stop)   -- returns nil when stop is reached
    if not move then break end
    best = move
  end
  return best                                -- when time is up, still return the best so far
end
```

### What to watch out for after extending

- While a callback runs, the screen does not update and input is not handled. Extending only prevents the callback from being aborted; it does not keep the display and keys responsive. Set a duration for the computation that the user can tolerate (1.5 seconds in the example above), and return the best result so far when it expires. If you need longer, draw a "thinking" indicator before computing, or use `ctx:after` to split the work into parts, one callback per part, so that the display and input work normally between parts.
- Do not put computation in `on_draw`. `on_draw` only draws the current state. Compute the result in `on_input`, `on_tick`, or a timer callback, store it, and draw it after `ctx:invalidate()`.
- `on_leave` and lock-screen sessions cannot be extended, so the work there must already fit within the limit: `on_leave` only writes data that is already prepared, and a lock screen only draws one frame.
- 30 seconds is the hard limit for a single callback. Longer work can only be split across several callbacks, with the progress kept in `ctx.state` or a private file.

## Tick and timers

```lua
ctx:set_tick(ms)
local timer = ctx:after(ms, function(ctx) end)
timer:cancel()
```

`set_tick` sets the `on_tick` period. `ms` is an integer from 33 to 60000, or 0 to stop. The period is 0 when the session starts, so `on_tick` is not called. The period is the target interval between the starts of two `on_tick` calls. If the previous callback has not finished, the next one is delayed, and missed ticks are not made up. `dt_ms` is the number of milliseconds since the previous `on_tick` (or since `set_tick`, for the first call).

Presenting a frame on an e-ink panel takes a few hundred milliseconds. Frames requested while a present is in progress are combined into one frame. The host may call `on_draw` for that frame while the previous frame is still refreshing; it draws the state at that moment, and the frame is shown after the previous refresh finishes. The panel's frame rate is therefore determined by presenting: on the Gancao X4 Pro and X4 Classic, a partial refresh takes about 650 ms per frame (about 75 ms to render and about 570 ms to refresh), which is under 1.5 frames per second, so the displacement between two adjacent frames is speed × 0.65 seconds. The frame on which the system performs its automatic full refresh takes about 1.5 seconds (section 5). Whether `on_tick` keeps running during a present depends on the device. On the X4 Pro, it is called on its period as usual. On the X4 Classic, once the next frame is taken, no callback runs until that frame is shown, so while frames are requested continuously there is one `on_tick` per frame and `dt_ms` is about 650. Gancao firmware before 2026-10-16 behaves the same way. Animate based on time: advance continuous motion by speed × `dt_ms`. Do not move a fixed step per `on_tick` or `on_draw`, and do not cap `dt_ms` or the displacement per step; otherwise, the speed differs several times over between devices. When the jump between two frames is too large to look continuous, use discrete motion by cell or by step, or draw only the start and end positions.

The `set_tick` period is rounded to the device's system tick. Gancao firmware ticks every 10 ms, so `set_tick(33)` runs about every 40 ms.

`after` calls the function once after `ms` milliseconds. `ms` is an integer from 1 to 2147483647. At most 32 timers can be pending at once; the 33rd returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. It returns the timer object. `cancel` stops a pending timer from firing and returns nothing. It has no effect on a timer that has already fired or been cancelled.

Wake only when needed to save power: align a clock face to the next minute with `ctx:after`, and use `set_tick` only for animation.

## How a session ends

Each of the following calls `on_leave` (unless the session has already ended because of an error) and then destroys the virtual machine:

| Cause | When |
| --- | --- |
| The app leaves | The script calls `ctx:quit()`, after the current callback returns |
| A system page opens | The script calls `ctx.system:open` (2.1, section 25), after the current callback returns |
| Back was not handled | `on_input` for `back` did not return `true`; (2.7) after the user chooses to exit in the exit confirmation (section 4) |
| Forced exit | A long press of Back (section 4) |
| Back to Home | A system key returns to the home screen, for example a long press of the `x4_pro` Home key (section 4) |
| The lock screen starts | The system decides to lock (section 15) |
| Power off | The user powers off the device, or it powers off on low battery |

When `on_leave` starts, unfinished network exchanges, text input, (2.9) docked input, dialogs, (2.18) native inference, and pending timers are cancelled, and their functions are not called. Files written in `on_leave` are flushed before the virtual machine is destroyed; at least 256 KB of writes can complete within 1000 ms. (2.2) After `on_leave` returns, the host saves `ctx.state` (section 28); this does not count against the `on_leave` limit.

`ctx:quit()` returns nothing.

If a finger is still down when a system screen covers the app, the host first delivers a pointer `cancel`, then calls `on_pause`.

# 3. Screen and device

```lua
ctx.screen.width
ctx.screen.height
ctx.screen.orientation    -- "portrait" | "landscape"
ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)   -- 2.18: o is "portrait" | "landscape" | "default"
ctx.screen.occlusion      -- { top, right, bottom, left }, pixels hidden by the bezel
ctx.screen.gray_levels    -- gray levels the app's drawing actually shows
ctx.screen.gray_still     -- 2.11: gray levels a gray frame shows, 4 or 2
ctx.device.model          -- device profile name, see the table below
ctx.device.lock_timer     -- whether a timer can wake the lock screen (the "timer wake" column), boolean
ctx.device.name           -- 2.1: the name the user gave the device
ctx.device.firmware       -- 2.1: firmware version string
ctx.device.id_for_app     -- 2.1: a device id that differs per app
```

`id_for_app` is a string of 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. On a given device, the same `app_id` always gets the same value; a different app or a different device gets a different value. You can use it as an online account or a leaderboard identity. It is not the device serial number, and the serial number cannot be derived from it. It does not change when the app is uninstalled and reinstalled.

The screen is in landscape when its width is greater than its height. When `display.orientation` is `portrait` or `landscape`, these fields do not change during the session. When it is `system`, rotation happens only between callbacks: the next callback sees the new width, height, orientation, and `occlusion`, and a redraw is already scheduled. The origin is at the top left of the logical screen; x increases to the right, and y increases downward. Pointer coordinates are already converted for the rotation.

## In-app orientation change (2.18)

```lua
local ok, err = ctx.screen:set_orientation("landscape")
```

`display.orientation` only sets the orientation at open. During a session, the app can call `set_orientation(o)` to change it: `"portrait"` is portrait, following the system's portrait setting (upright or upside down); `"landscape"` is landscape, the same as opening with `landscape` in the manifest; `"default"` returns to the orientation this session opened with according to `display.orientation`.

- It takes effect after the current callback returns: the fields of `ctx.screen` do not change during this callback; the next callback gets the new `width`, `height`, `orientation` and `occlusion`, and the host has scheduled one redraw, which is a full refresh. If it is called several times in one callback, the last call wins. When the target orientation equals the current one, it returns `true` and does not redraw.
- When called in `on_load`, the first frame is already drawn in the new orientation. To remember the user's choice, save it in `ctx.state` (section 28), read it in `on_load`, and call it there.
- It only applies to this session and does not change the system setting. When the session ends, the host restores the orientation from before the app was opened; the next open starts from `display.orientation` again.
- Pointer coordinates are converted for the new orientation; semantic keys do not change with orientation. Offscreen layers (section 11) keep their size after rotation, but their content is not guaranteed to survive it, so the app should redraw them.
- On success it returns `true`. A value other than the three above returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`; a non-string raises a Lua error. While docked input (section 4 `ctx.input:edit`, section 16 `ui:field`) is open it returns `nil, "busy"`. In a lock-screen session it returns `nil, "inactive"`.

The app should read `ctx.screen.width` and `height` for layout in every `on_draw` instead of caching them in `on_load`.

Pixels inside `occlusion` are drawn as usual but are not visible. Place text, strokes, focus, and hit targets in the visible area.

## Gray levels

The host maps each color onto `gray_levels` steps. The step is `(color * gray_levels) // 16`, and step 0 is the lightest.

An e-ink panel can show intermediate gray only with a dedicated grayscale waveform and a full refresh (the whole screen flashes). App frames use the fast refresh, which is black and white only, so every current profile has a `gray_levels` of 2, regardless of how many gray steps the panel itself can show.

- When `gray_levels` is 2, `0..7` is drawn as paper and `8..15` as ink. Use `g:pattern` for midtones (section 6).
- Antialiasing on TTF text edges can use more of the panel's steps; this limit does not apply to it.

Use `0` and `15` for body text and controls; the result is the same on every device.

### Gray frames (2.11)

A still picture (a photo album, a cover, a map) can show intermediate gray by using the grayscale waveform. If any `g:image` call in a frame sets `gray = true` (section 6), that frame is a gray frame:

- The whole frame is drawn in `gray_still` steps. The step is `(color * gray_still) // 16`, for rectangles, lines, text, and images alike. A 4-level image keeps its own 4 levels, and a black-and-white image stays black and white.
- The frame uses a full refresh with the grayscale waveform. The whole screen flashes once, and the refresh is slower than a normal full refresh, so gray frames are not suitable for animation. The first normal frame after a gray frame also uses a full refresh to clear the intermediate gray.
- `gray_levels` does not change; it is still the number of steps in a normal frame.

On a device whose `gray_still` is 2, `gray` is ignored and the frame stays black and white. `gray` also has no effect, and the frame is drawn as usual, inside a layer's `layer:draw` (layers are black and white, section 11) and in a lock-screen session (section 15). While a system input method, dialog, or similar screen covers the app, the host turns that frame into a normal full refresh.

`gray_still` depends on the device and the panel. Check its value; do not infer it from the device profile.

**4-level images in normal frames** (2.11): In a package whose manifest sets `"api": "2.11"` or later, a 4-level image (a 4-level image in the package, or an image that `ctx.image:decode` decodes with `gray = true`, section 27) is drawn in a normal frame as a 4×4 dot pattern fixed to the canvas. The four steps 0, 5, 10, and 15 come out as about 0, 6/16, 11/16, and all ink dots, and the dot patterns of neighboring images line up. A package for 2.10 or earlier still uses the threshold described above, so its picture does not change.

## Device profiles

| `model` | Portrait | Touch | Built-in keys | Gray levels | small / medium / large | Timer wake | Front light | Portrait occlusion top/right/bottom/left | Docked keyboard height (2.9) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x4_pro` | 480×800 | yes | `up` `down` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | yes, warmth is adjustable | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 340 |
| `x4_classic` | 480×800 | no | `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | no | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |

A type size is the line height in pixels. A new profile can only be added as a row in this table, and the row must fill in every column.

Every profile has a touchscreen or has all of `up`, `down`, and `ok`, so the UI library in section 16 can be operated on every profile. The largest system font is 40 px. Larger type (such as clock digits) uses TTF: (2.3) `ctx.fonts:size(px)` returns the preferred font directly, which is the font the user chose in system settings (2.17, section 7).
