- When focus is drawn, a 2-pixel frame is drawn 3 pixels outside the whole control, with corner radius `radius + 3` when `radius` is set. When the control is disabled, it is drawn and then covered with white dots.

A `note` that is not a string, or a `skin` that is not a registered skin name, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

```lua
ui:switch("autoflip", { x = 30, y = 220, w = 420, h = 70, radius = 12,
  text = "Auto flip", note = "Flip every 30 seconds", selected = s.autoflip })
```

### The button's `align` and badges

`button` accepts `align`: `"left"`, `"center"` (default), or `"right"`. The text is aligned accordingly within the text area.

`button` and `region` accept `badge`: a string. `""` or omitting it means no badge. The badge is drawn in the top-right corner using `ctx.fonts.small`. Its height is `line height + 4` and its width is `max(height, text width + 8)`; its right edge is 4 pixels from the control's right edge, and its top edge is 4 pixels from the control's top edge. A 2-pixel paper-colored (0) capsule is drawn first, then a capsule filled with color 15, with the text centered in color 0. The badge is drawn after the control (after `region`'s `draw`) and before the disabled white dots.

### `ui:skin`

```lua
local tc, tx, ty, tw, th = ui:skin(g, "iron", x, y, w, h, { focused = true, selected = false })
```

Draws a registered skin on any canvas (including a layer, and inside a `region`'s `draw`) by "How buttons are drawn": nine-slice, the derived reverse, the focus outer frame, no text. `st` is optional and may contain `focused`, `selected`, `enabled`, and `emphasis`, all booleans; `enabled` defaults to true and the rest to false. With `enabled = false`, the `disabled` variant is used only if it is set, and no white dots are drawn: because the dots must cover the text, the script draws its own `g:pattern` after it draws the text.

Returns the text color of this look and the text area `tx, ty, tw, th` after `pad` is applied. Returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` if `g` is not a canvas, the name is not registered, `x`, `y`, `w`, or `h` is not an integer, `w` or `h` is less than 1, or `st` is not a table.

## Layout (2.15)

Packages whose manifest declares 2.15 or later lay out `row` and `column` according to this section, and also get `ui:grid`, `ui:stack`, the `spacer` child, container appearance, and `ui:layout`. Packages for 2.0–2.14 still use the earlier rules above: the fields in this section are ignored, `kind = "spacer"`, `"grid"`, and `"stack"` are unknown controls, and `ui:grid`, `ui:stack`, and `ui:layout` return `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Field names and values follow CSS flexbox (`row`, `column`) and grid (`grid`), with `-` replaced by `_`. For where they differ from CSS, see "Differences from CSS".

```lua
ui:column("page", { x = 0, y = 0, w = 480, h = 800, padding = 24, gap = 16, children = {
  { kind = "row", align_items = "center", children = {
    { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "Reading settings", font = big, grow = 1 },
    { kind = "button", id = "close", text = "Close", w = "fit", h = "fit" },
  } },
  { kind = "column", border = true, radius = 16, divider = { inset = 16 }, children = {
    { kind = "switch", id = "flip", text = "Auto flip", note = "Flip every 30 seconds", h = 72, selected = s.flip },
    { kind = "switch", id = "ghost", text = "Clear ghosting", h = 72, selected = s.ghost, hidden = not s.flip },
  } },
  { kind = "grid", columns = { min = 140 }, auto_rows = 56, gap = 12, children = {
    { kind = "button", id = "f16", text = "16" }, { kind = "button", id = "f20", text = "20" },
    { kind = "button", id = "f24", text = "24" },
  } },
  { kind = "spacer" },
  { kind = "row", h = 64, gap = 16, children = {
    { kind = "button", id = "reset", text = "Restore defaults", grow = 1 },
    { kind = "button", id = "ok", text = "Done", grow = 1, emphasis = true },
  } },
} })
```

There are four container kinds: `row` and `column` are flexbox containers, `grid` is a grid, and `stack` overlays its children in the same region.

### Container fields

| Field | Value | Default | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `padding` | An integer 0..255, or 1–4 such integers in CSS order: `{ all }`, `{ top/bottom, left/right }`, `{ top, left/right, bottom }`, `{ top, right, bottom, left }` | 0 | all four |
| `gap` | An integer 0..255 | 0 | flexbox, `grid`: sets both fields below at once |
| `row_gap` `column_gap` | Integers 0..255 | equal to `gap` | flexbox, `grid`: `row_gap` is the spacing between vertically adjacent items, and `column_gap` the spacing between horizontally adjacent ones |
| `justify_content` | `"start"` `"center"` `"end"` `"space-between"` `"space-around"` `"space-evenly"` | `"start"` | flexbox: distributes leftover space on the main axis; `grid`: distributes leftover horizontal space |
| `align_items` | `"start"` `"center"` `"end"` `"stretch"` `"baseline"` | `"stretch"` | flexbox: placement of children on the cross axis; `grid`, `stack`: vertical placement within the region, `"baseline"` not allowed |
| `align_content` | Same as `justify_content`; flexbox also accepts `"stretch"` | flexbox `"stretch"`, `grid` `"start"` | flexbox: placement of lines on the cross axis when `wrap` is true; `grid`: distributes leftover vertical space |
| `wrap` | Boolean | false | flexbox: wraps to a new line when the current line does not fit |
| `divider` | `true`, or `{ line_width = 1..255, color = 0..15, inset = 0..255 }`, each field optional, defaulting to 1, 15, 0 | not set | flexbox with `wrap` false: see "Container appearance" |
| `justify_items` | `"start"` `"center"` `"end"` `"stretch"` | `"stretch"` | `grid`, `stack`: horizontal placement of children within the region |
| `columns` | An integer 1..64, `{ min = width }`, or an array of 1–64 tracks | required | `grid`, see "`ui:grid`" |
| `rows` | An array of 1–64 tracks | not set | `grid` |
| `auto_rows` | One track | `"fit"` | `grid`: rows beyond those in `rows` |
| `border` | Boolean | false | all four: draws a border |
| `line_width` | Integer 1..255 | 1 | all four: border stroke width |
| `border_color` | Integer 0..15 | 15 | all four: border color |
| `background` | Integer 0..15 | not set (no fill) | all four: fill color |
| `radius` | Integer 0..255 | 0 | all four: corner radius of the border and fill |
| `skin` | A skin name registered in `create` | not set | all four: draws the base with the skin |

Main axis: horizontal for `row`, vertical for `column`; the other direction is the cross axis. The inner box is the container's box minus `padding`. Setting a field on a container kind it does not apply to (such as `wrap` on `grid`, `columns` on `row`, or `gap` on `stack`), or setting `divider` together with `wrap = true`, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

The outermost containers (those called directly as `ui:row`, `ui:column`, `ui:grid`, `ui:stack`) must set `id`, `x`, and `y`; `w` and `h` are integers or `"fit"`, not percentages. A container nested in `children` may omit `id`. Every container counts toward the limit of 128 controls per frame, is not hittable, and is not in the focus order.

### Child fields

| Field | Value | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `w` `h` | An integer of at least 1, `"fit"`, `"N%"` (N an integer 1..100), or not set | see below |
| `min_w` `max_w` `min_h` `max_h` | Non-negative integers | `min` defaults to 1 (0 for `spacer`). When the `h` of a `label`, `button`, `switch`, or `tabs` in a `row` or `column` is not set or is `"fit"`, `min_h` is one line height of the font in use (at most `max_h`). `max` defaults to unlimited |
| `aspect_ratio` | A positive finite number: width ÷ height | not set |
| `align_self` | Same as `align_items` | inherits the container's `align_items` |
| `grow` | Integer 0..1000: leftover space is split in proportion to this value | 0 (for `spacer`, see below). Flexbox only |
| `shrink` | Integer 0..1000: when space is insufficient, children shrink in proportion to `shrink × inner base` | 1. Flexbox only |
| `justify_self` | Same as `justify_items` | inherits the container's `justify_items`. `grid` and `stack` only |
| `column_span` `row_span` | Integers 1..64: the number of columns and rows spanned | 1. `grid` only |
| `hidden` | Boolean | false |

A container child is never smaller in either direction than the sum of its own `padding` on both sides (like CSS `box-sizing: border-box`): when `min`, `max`, the set size, or the base is smaller than that sum, the sum is used instead.

A child's `x` and `y` are ignored. Setting `min` greater than `max`, setting a field used only by some container kinds on a child of another kind, or setting `column_span` greater than the number of columns returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

A child with `hidden = true` is treated as absent: it takes no space and no gap, and it is not drawn, not registered, and not in the focus order. Its other fields are still validated. A `false` in `children` is also skipped (so you can write `cond and { ... }` directly in the array); any other non-table value returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Below, "child" refers only to children that are not skipped, but "the n-th" still refers to the position in `children`.

A child whose computed width or height is 0 (possible only when `min_w = 0` or `min_h = 0` is set) still occupies its laid-out position, but it is not drawn, not registered, and not in the focus order. If it is a container, the same applies to its children. The result of `ui:layout` still includes its box as usual. The container's other children are still drawn, and the call does not fail.

`"fit"` is the size computed from the content (see "Content size"). Only `label`, `button`, `switch`, `tabs`, `image`, `spacer`, and the four container kinds support `fit` (a `grid` with `columns = { min = width }` cannot fit its width). Setting `"fit"` on any other control returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

`"N%"` is N% of the reference length, `reference length × N // 100`. In flexbox, the reference is the container's inner box in that direction; in `grid`, the cell region the child occupies; in `stack`, the inner box. When the reference length is not yet known (for example, while the container's own content size is being computed), the percentage is treated as not set, as in CSS.

`aspect_ratio`: width is always resolved first, then height. When width is not set but height is an integer or a percentage, width = `floor(height × ratio + 0.5)` (in `grid`, no width is derived when height is a percentage, because the row height is not yet known when column widths are resolved). When height is not set, height = `floor(width ÷ ratio + 0.5)`. A size derived this way counts as set and is not stretched. Setting `aspect_ratio` and `h = "fit"` without `w` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

### `spacer`

`{ kind = "spacer" }` only takes up space: it is not drawn, not hittable, not in the focus order, and does not count toward the 128 controls per frame. `id` is optional. Its content size is 0. In flexbox, when neither a main-axis size nor `grow` is set, `grow` is 1, so the spacer takes up the leftover space. In `grid`, it occupies one cell (`column_span` and `row_span` are allowed). A `spacer` cannot be at the outermost level.

### Flexbox: main axis

Each child is first assigned a base:

1. An integer is set: the base is that integer. A percentage is set: it is computed as described in "`\"N%\"`"; when the reference length is unknown, it is treated as not set.
2. `"fit"` is set: the content size.
3. Not set, but derivable from `aspect_ratio`: the derived size (in `row`, the width derived from the set height; in `column`, the height derived from the resolved width).
4. Not set, and `grow > 0`: 0 (like CSS `flex: 1`, so children with the same `grow` get the same size).
5. Not set, `grow` is 0, and the child can `fit`: the content size.
6. Otherwise, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

The base is clamped between `min` and `max` to get the hypothetical size; the base itself is not clamped (a container child's base is still no less than the sum of its `padding` on both sides). The base minus a container child's `padding` on both sides in this direction is the inner base (for a non-container child, the inner base equals the base). Main-axis gap: `row` uses `column_gap`, and `column` uses `row_gap`.

**Line breaking**: when `wrap` is false, all children are placed on one line. When it is true, children are placed into lines in declaration order: when a line already has children and `sum of existing hypothetical sizes + gap × existing count + the next hypothetical size > inner box main-axis length`, the next child starts a new line. When the inner box main-axis length is unknown (the main axis is `"fit"`), lines do not wrap.

**Per-line distribution** follows the CSS flexbox algorithm (CSS Flexbox 9.7). Let `avail = inner box main-axis length − gap × (this line's count − 1)`. When the sum of hypothetical sizes is less than `avail`, the line "grows", and the space is split by `grow`; otherwise it "shrinks", and the space is split by `shrink × inner base` (as in CSS).

1. Initial freeze: when growing, freeze children with `grow` 0 and children whose base is greater than their hypothetical size (clamped by `max`); when shrinking, freeze children with `shrink` 0 and children whose base is less than their hypothetical size (clamped by `min`). Frozen children take their hypothetical size.
2. `free = avail − sum of frozen children's sizes − sum of unfrozen children's bases`. Unfrozen children are taken in declaration order, with weight `grow` when growing and `shrink × inner base` when shrinking. The cumulative weight through the i-th child is `W_i`, and the total is `W`. When growing, the i-th child gets its base plus `floor(free × W_i / W) − floor(free × W_{i−1} / W)`; when shrinking, it gets its base minus `ceil(|free| × W_i / W) − ceil(|free| × W_{i−1} / W)` (not below 0), so in both cases the boundaries round down. When `W` is 0, every child equals its base.
3. Clamp these sizes between `min` and `max`, and sum `after clamp − before clamp` over the children: when the sum is 0, freeze all; when it is greater than 0, freeze those clamped by `min`; when it is less than 0, freeze those clamped by `max`. Frozen children take the clamped size.
4. If any children remain unfrozen, return to step 2; otherwise, finish.

If the children still do not fit after distribution, they are still drawn: they extend outside the container, are not clipped, and no error is raised.

**Position on the main axis**: the line's `free = avail − sum of child sizes` (which may be less than 0) is split by `justify_content` into `n + 1` slots: before the first child, between each adjacent pair, and after the last child. The weight of each slot:

| `justify_content` | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| `start` | only the last slot is 1 |
| `end` | only the first slot is 1 |
| `center` | the first and last slots are 1 each |
| `space-between` | the first and last are 0; each middle slot is 1 |
| `space-around` | the first and last are 1; each middle slot is 2 |
| `space-evenly` | all are 1 |

The split uses cumulative rounding: the cumulative weight through the i-th slot is `W_i`, the total is `W`, and the i-th slot gets `floor(free × W_i / W) − floor(free × W_{i−1} / W)`. When `free < 0`, `space-between`, `space-around`, and `space-evenly` all behave as `start` (like the CSS fallback; all overflow goes to the trailing side). When `W` is 0 (`space-between` with a single child), the container behaves as `start`.

### Flexbox: cross axis

`column` resolves each child's width (the cross axis) first and then computes the main axis; `row` computes the main axis first and then resolves the height. A child's cross size:

- An integer is set: that value. A percentage is set: it refers to the inner box cross length, and is treated as not set when that length is unknown.
- `"fit"` is set: the content size (in `row`, a `label`'s height is computed from its resolved width).
- Not set, but derivable from `aspect_ratio`: the derived size.
- Not set: the content size first (0 for a child that cannot `fit`), stretched later if the effective alignment is `stretch`. In `column` with `wrap` false and a known inner box width, a `stretch`ed child is given the inner box width directly, and its height is computed from that width.

All cross sizes are clamped between `min` and `max`.

**Line cross length**: when `wrap` is false and the inner box cross length is known, the line cross length is the inner box cross length. Otherwise, it is the maximum cross size among the line's children; children aligned by `baseline` together count as `max(baseline) + max(cross size − baseline)`.

**Multiple lines** (`wrap` is true, even if only one line results): `free = inner box cross length − Σ line cross lengths − cross-axis gap × (line count − 1)` (0 when the inner box cross length is unknown). When `align_content` is `stretch` and `free > 0`, `free` is added evenly to the lines in order (with cumulative rounding, the i-th line gets an extra `floor(free × i / line count) − floor(free × (i − 1) / line count)`), and the lines start from the beginning. Other values split `free` into the slots between lines by the weight table above.

**Position within a line**: for a child whose effective alignment is `stretch` and whose cross size is neither set nor derived from `aspect_ratio`, the cross size equals the line cross length (clamped between `min` and `max`). Offset: `start` and `stretch` are 0; `center` is `(line cross length − size) // 2`; `end` is `line cross length − size`; `baseline` is `max(baseline) − its own baseline`. In `column`, `baseline` behaves as `start`. A child whose cross size is not set and that cannot `fit` still behaves as `stretch` when its alignment is set to `baseline`, `start`, `center`, or `end`.

### Baseline

The baseline is the distance from the child's top edge to the baseline of its first line of text. The line box height of a single line is `font.line_height`, and the baseline is `font.ascent` below the top edge of the line box (section 7).

| Child | Baseline |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | The offset of the line block within the box + `ascent`: the offset is 0 when `valign` is `top`, `(h − block height) // 2` when `middle`, and `h − block height` when `bottom`. The block height is the line block height from `font:layout` |
| `button` | Text area top + `(text area height − line height) // 2 + ascent`. The text area is inset by the skin's `pad`, or is the whole button when there is no skin. With an image and no text, the baseline is `h` |
| `switch` | Without `note`: `(h − line height) // 2 + ascent`; with `note`: `h // 2 − 2 − line height + ascent` |
| `tabs` | Same as `button` (per cell) |
| container | The baseline of the first non-`spacer` child + its vertical offset in the container; `h` when there are no children |
| other | `h` (the bottom edge) |

### Content size

Text uses the control's `font` (`ctx.fonts.medium` when not set). The line height is `font.line_height`, and the text width is measured with `font:measure`.

| Control | Width | Height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | The width of the widest line after splitting by `\n` | Given the resolved width, the line block height returned by `font:layout(text, w, 32767)` |
| `button` | text width + 24 | line height + 16 |
| `switch` | `8 + max(text width, note width) + 12 + 64 + 8` | `max(34, h₁) + 16`, where `h₁` is `2 × max(line height, small line height) + 4` with `note`, and the line height otherwise |
| `tabs` | `n × (widest item + 24) + gap × (n − 1)` | line height + 16 |
| `image` | image width | image height |
| `spacer` | 0 | 0 |

With a skin, the skin's `pad` is added: `button` adds the left and right padding to its width and the top and bottom padding to its height; `tabs` adds the left and right padding to each cell's width (that is, `n × (widest item + 24 + left/right) + gap × (n − 1)`) and the top and bottom padding to its height. A `button` with `image` and no `text` uses the image's width and height. A container's skin does not affect its content size.

Flexbox content size:

- Main axis: `padding` on both sides + gap × `(n − 1)` + the sum of each child's contribution, regardless of `wrap` (computed as a single line). A child with an integer or `"fit"` set, or with a size derived from `aspect_ratio`, contributes that size; a percentage is treated as not set; an unset child that can `fit` contributes its content size, and one that cannot contributes 0. Children with `grow` set but no main-axis size together contribute `G × max(ceil(fit_i / grow_i))` (`G` is the sum of their `grow`, and `fit_i` is 0 for a child that cannot `fit`), so that after splitting, each is no smaller than its own content. All contributions are first clamped between `min` and `max`.
- Cross axis: for `row`, after the lines are laid out with the resolved width, `padding` top and bottom + the sum of the line cross lengths + `row_gap × (line count − 1)`; for `column`, `padding` left and right + the maximum child width (set, or the content size, 0 for a child that cannot `fit`), with `wrap` also computed as a single column.

### `ui:grid`

```lua
ui:grid("fonts", { x = 24, y = 300, w = 432, h = "fit", columns = { min = 140 }, gap = 12, children = { ... } })
ui:grid("shop", { x = 0, y = 0, w = 480, h = 800, padding = 16, gap = 12,
  columns = { 96, "1fr", "fit" }, rows = { 64, "1fr", 72 }, children = {
    { kind = "label", id = "title", text = "Shop", column_span = 3, align_self = "center" },
    { kind = "region", id = "list", column_span = 2, draw = draw_list },
    ...
} })
```

**Tracks**: a track is the width of a column or the height of a row, written as:

| Written as | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| an integer of at least 1 | fixed pixels |
| `"fit"` | sized by the content of children that occupy only this track |
| `"Nfr"` (N an integer 1..1000) | shares the leftover space in proportion to N |
| `"N%"` (N an integer 1..100) | N% of the grid inner box length in this direction, `inner box length × N // 100`; behaves as `"fit"` when the inner box length is unknown |

`columns = n` is equivalent to n tracks of `"1fr"`. `columns = { min = width }` (width an integer of at least 1) gives `max(1, (inner box width + column_gap) // (width + column_gap))` tracks of `"1fr"`. It requires a known inner box width, so such a grid with `w = "fit"` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`, and its width counts as 0 when an outer container computes its content size. `rows` define the 1st, 2nd, … rows in order; further rows use `auto_rows`.

**Placement**: children are placed automatically in declaration order, like CSS `grid-auto-flow: row`. Starting after the previous child's end and moving left to right, top to bottom, each child goes in the first unoccupied position that fits `column_span × row_span`. When rows run out, rows are added downward.

**Track sizing**: columns are computed first, then rows. Columns use the children's widths; rows use the children's heights computed from their final widths. A child's "contribution" in one direction: a set integer or a size derived from `aspect_ratio` contributes that size; `"fit"`, a percentage, or no setting contributes the content size (0 for a child that cannot `fit`). All contributions are clamped between `min` and `max`.

1. Integer and percentage tracks take their value.
2. A `"fit"` track is the maximum contribution of children that occupy only this track (0 when there are none).
3. Children spanning multiple tracks are processed in groups, from the smallest span to the largest. Children that cross an `fr` track are ignored. For the others, the part of the contribution that exceeds the total length of the crossed tracks plus the gaps between them is split evenly among the `"fit"` tracks they cross (with cumulative rounding); if they cross no `"fit"` track, it is not split. Within a group, each track takes the maximum of the amounts the children give it, and this amount is added to the track after the group is done.
4. When the length in this direction is known: `free = inner box length − sum of non-fr tracks − gap × (track count − 1)`. When it is greater than 0, it is split among the `fr` tracks in proportion to their ratios with cumulative rounding; otherwise, the `fr` tracks are 0.
5. When the length in this direction is unknown (`"fit"`, while computing the content size): `unit = max(ceil(m_t / fr_t))`, where `m_t` is the maximum contribution of children that occupy only this `fr` track. Each `fr` track is `fr_t × unit`.

Tracks are separated by `column_gap` and `row_gap`. When the grid inner box is longer than the tracks plus gaps, the leftover space is split horizontally by `justify_content` and vertically by `align_content` into the gaps between tracks (same weight table as "Position on the main axis", `n` is the track count); when it is shorter, the same rules apply, and the tracks may extend outside the grid.

**Position in a cell**: a child's cell region consists of the tracks it spans, the gaps between them, and the space that `justify_content` and `align_content` distribute into those gaps. Horizontal placement follows `justify_self`, and vertical placement follows `align_self`. When the effective alignment is `stretch` and the size is neither set nor derived from `aspect_ratio`, the size equals the region length (clamped between `min` and `max`); otherwise, the size is the set size (a percentage refers to the region) or the content size, placed by `start`, `center` (offset `(region length − size) // 2`), or `end`. A child with no set size that cannot `fit` still behaves as `stretch`. Width is resolved first, then height from that width.

**Content size**: width is `padding` left and right + the sum of the columns (computed by step 5) + `column_gap × (column count − 1)`; height is the sum of the rows computed from these column widths + `row_gap × (row count − 1)` + `padding` top and bottom.

### `ui:stack`

```lua
ui:stack("cover", { x = 40, y = 120, w = 400, h = 300, border = true, radius = 16, padding = 12, children = {
  { kind = "image", id = "art", source = cover },
  { kind = "label", id = "tag", text = "New", w = "fit", h = "fit", justify_self = "end", align_self = "start" },
} })
```

All children are placed in the same region: the inner box. Each child is placed in the region as in `grid`'s "Position in a cell": by `justify_self` and `align_self`, with percentages referring to the inner box. The container accepts `padding`, `justify_items`, `align_items`, and the appearance fields. Children are drawn in declaration order, so later children cover earlier ones, and a tap on an overlapping spot hits the later child.

**Content size**: width is `padding` left and right + the maximum width contribution among the children (as in `grid`); height is `padding` top and bottom + the maximum child height, each computed from the child's own width. When the inner box length is unknown, the region is computed from the content size.

### Container appearance

The container is drawn before its children, so the children cover its appearance.

- With `skin`, the nine-slice is drawn in the skin's normal look (as in "How buttons are drawn", but without state variants or text), and `border`, `background`, and `radius` have no effect. The skin's `pad` is not applied to the container; use `padding` for spacing.
- Without `skin`: when `background` is set, the container's box is filled with that color using `radius`; with `border = true`, a border is then drawn along the inside of the box using `radius`, `line_width`, and `border_color`.
- `divider`: a divider line is drawn between each pair of adjacent children that are both not `spacer`. The line width `t` is the divider's `line_width`, and the line is drawn in the middle of the gap between the two children. In `row`, it is a vertical line whose left edge is at `p = previous right + (next left − previous right − t) // 2`; in `column`, it is a horizontal line whose top edge is computed the same way. The line spans the container's box on the cross axis, inset by `inset` at both ends. The divider takes no space; the gap comes from `gap`.

### Overflow

When a child's box extends outside the container's inner box (its left or top edge is less than the inner box's, or its right or bottom edge is greater), the container overflows. In the result of `ui:layout`, this container's table has `overflow`, which is the position in `children` of the first overflowing child; when there is no overflow, the field is absent. The same applies to the outermost container. The host's debugging tool can mark it.

### Differences from CSS

- `min_w` and `min_h` default to 1 (0 for `spacer`), not CSS `auto` (no smaller than the content): when space is insufficient, children shrink and truncate text with an ellipsis rather than pushing out of the container. The exception is the height of text controls in `row` and `column`: `label`, `button`, `switch`, and `tabs` without a numeric `h` keep at least one line of text. When the container cannot fit them, it overflows (`overflow`) rather than squeezing out the text.
- With `grow` set but no main-axis size, the base is 0, as with CSS `flex: 1`, not the content-based behavior of `flex-grow` alone.
- `fr` tracks have a minimum of 0 (in CSS it is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, which fits at least the content). A child crossing an `fr` track does not stretch the track.
- A size derived from `aspect_ratio` is not stretched.
- When wrapping, the content width of `column` is computed as a single column.
- `stack` is like a CSS grid with a single cell that all children are placed into.
- All sizes are integers, all proportional splits use cumulative rounding, and the remainder goes to the later items.
- There is no margin, absolute positioning, `order`, placement by grid lines, or right-to-left layout. Use `padding`, `gap`, and `spacer` for spacing, and `stack` for overlaying.

### `ui:layout`

```lua
local b = ui:layout({ x = 0, y = 0, w = 480, h = 800 }, { kind = "column", padding = 24, gap = 12, children = {
  { id = "head", h = 64 },
  { id = "body", grow = 1 },
  { kind = "row", h = 64, gap = 12, children = { { id = "a", grow = 1 }, { id = "b", grow = 1 } } },
} })
-- b = { x = 0, y = 0, w = 480, h = 800, ... }; b.body = { x = 24, y = 100, w = 432, h = 600 }
-- b.b = { x = 246, y = 712, w = 210, h = 64 }; b[3][2] is the same table as b.b
```

Computes rectangles only, following the rules in this section. It draws nothing, registers no controls, does not count toward the 128 controls per frame, and can be called inside or outside a frame. `rect`'s `x` and `y` are integers, and `w` and `h` are integers of at least 1 or `"fit"`. `spec` is a container (`kind` of `"row"`, `"column"`, `"grid"`, or `"stack"`) placed inside `rect`: when `w` and `h` are integers, it fills them; when they are `"fit"`, it uses its content size. Its own `padding` is kept inside the box, the `x`, `y`, `w`, and `h` set on it are ignored, and its appearance fields are validated but not drawn. A child's `kind` may be any control (its content size is computed by that control's rules, and the sizing fields `text`, `font`, `note`, `items`, `source`, `image`, and `skin` are validated by the control's rules), `"spacer"`, a container, or not set (a plain box that cannot `fit`). `id` is optional. When set, it cannot be repeated and cannot be `"x"`, `"y"`, `"w"`, `"h"`, or `"overflow"`.

Returns the box of `spec` as `{ x, y, w, h }`, with `overflow` when it overflows. `[1..n]` are the boxes of `spec`'s children (including `spacer`; a skipped child is `false`). When a child is a container, its table also has its own `[1..m]` and `overflow`. A child with an `id` is also stored at `[id]` in the returned table, as the same table as at its numbered position.

More than 16 levels of nesting or more than 1024 children returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. A `rect` or `spec` that violates the rules returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

## Text levels, halftone and stable layout (2.16)

This section applies only to packages whose manifest declares 2.16 or later. In packages for 2.0–2.15, these fields are ignored and the rendering is unchanged.

### Bold

`label`, `button`, `switch`, `tabs`, and `radio` accept `bold` (a boolean); the text is drawn as described in section 7, "Bold (2.16)". When it is not set:

- the `text` of `switch` is bold, and its `note` is not;
- the selected cell of `tabs` is bold and the other cells are not; with `bold = true`, every cell is bold, and with `bold = false`, none are;
- the other controls are not bold.

### Tabular digits

`label` and `button` accept `tabular` (a boolean, default `false`); the text is drawn as described in section 7 "Tabular digits (2.16)". The middle text of `stepper` and `pager` is tabular by default; setting `tabular = false` turns it off.

### Reserved width

`label` and `button` accept `reserve` (a string): with `w = "fit"`, the width is determined by the wider of `text` and `reserve` (using the same font, `bold`, and `tabular`, plus the usual padding). For a control whose digits change, set the widest form, for example `reserve = "00:00"` or `reserve = "999"`. When the text changes, the control keeps its width, and adjacent controls do not move. It has no effect when `w` is not `"fit"`. A `reserve` that is not a string returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

### Selected appearance

`tabs` accepts `selected_style`. Without a skin, the selected cell is drawn as follows:

| Value | How it is drawn |
| --- | --- |
| `"fill"` (default) | Fill 15, text 0, same as 2.14 |
| `"outline"` | No fill; stroke width 3 (drawn even when `border = false`); text 15 |
| `"underline"` | No fill; the stroke is drawn as usual (not drawn when `border = false`), and a horizontal bar 4 pixels high, filled with 15, is drawn along the cell's bottom edge, inset `min(8, w // 6)` on each side; text 15 |

With `outline` and `underline`, switching tabs changes only the selected cell's border and bar. No large black block moves with the selection, so there is less ghosting on an e-ink screen. With a skin, `selected_style` has no effect. An invalid value returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

`ctx.ui:create(opts)` accepts `focus_style`. `"fill"` (default) is the 2.13 rendering: when focus is drawn, a `button` and the buttons of `stepper` and `pager` are filled with 15, with text 0. With `"outline"`, they are not filled; instead, a 2-pixel frame is drawn 3 pixels outside the box (like the focus of a tab), so moving focus with the arrow keys changes only the two frames. Focus on the other controls is already drawn as an outer frame and is unaffected. An invalid value returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

### Halftone background

A normal frame has only black and white (section 3). The library's own color fills use halftone instead, so a light background does not become pure white or pure black. Halftone is used for a container's `background` and the `divider` color (2.15). Colors fall into four bands:

| Color | How it is drawn |
| --- | --- |
| 0–2 | Filled with the paper color (0) |
| 3–7 | Light halftone: a paper fill first, then a `dot` in color 15 with `density = 38` (about 6/16 of the dots are black) |
| 8–12 | Dark halftone: a paper fill first, then a `dot` in color 15 with `density = 69` (about 11/16) |
| 13–15 | Filled with the ink color (15) |

The halftone aligns to the canvas origin, as `g:pattern` does (section 6), so two adjacent blocks join without a visible seam. With `radius`, it follows the rounded corners: rows within the corner radius are drawn one at a time, one command per row, so a rounded halftone block takes at most `2 × radius + 2` commands.

Black text (15) can be placed on a light halftone. Do not put text on a dark halftone; it is only for color blocks, separators, and decoration. `border_color` and the text `color` are unchanged and are still drawn as described in section 3. On a device without the `pattern` capability (`ctx.capabilities.pattern` is false), the fill uses the threshold described in section 3.

### Full refresh on page turns

When the content of the whole page is replaced (turning a page or opening a new screen), request the frame with `ctx:invalidate("full")` (section 5) to clear the ghosting. Local changes within the same page (focus, switches, counts) use the usual partial refresh. The UI library does not make this decision for the app; this item is a recommendation.
entries.example:
local ui = ctx.ui:create()        -- create it once in on_load

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  ui:begin_frame(g)
  ui:label("title", { x = 20, y = 20, w = 440, h = 40, text = "Settings", font = ctx.fonts.large })
  ui:switch("wifi", { x = 20, y = 80, w = 440, h = 56, text = "Wi-Fi", selected = wifi })
  ui:button("save", { x = 20, y = 160, w = 200, h = 56, text = "Save", radius = 8 })
  ui:end_frame()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local id, action = ui:handle_event(ev)
  if action == "activate" then
    if id == "wifi" then wifi = not wifi end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if action then ctx:invalidate(); return true end
  return false
end

entries.content:
# 17. Optional capabilities

`ctx.capabilities` exists at the start of the session. Every field is a boolean and does not change during the session. The host may report any of the following as false.

| Field | Present when true | When false |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | `g:pattern` | `g.pattern` is nil |
| `image_transform` | Transform fields of `g:image` | Setting those fields returns `nil, "not_supported"` |
| `ttf` | `ctx.fonts:installed`, `ctx.fonts:open`. (2.17) Always false on hosts that implement 2.17, regardless of the version the package declares | Both functions are nil |
| `ui` | `ctx.ui` | `ctx.ui` is nil |
| `reader` (2.1) | `ctx.reader` (also requires the `reader` permission) | `ctx.reader` is nil |
| `dialog` (2.1) | `ctx.dialog` | `ctx.dialog` is nil |
| `frontlight` (2.1) | `ctx.frontlight` | `ctx.frontlight` is nil |
| `image_decode` (2.1) | `ctx.image:decode` | `ctx.image` is nil |

The name of an optional capability is the name of its namespace (except `image_decode`, whose namespace is `ctx.image`). On a 2.0 host, the 2.1 fields are absent (nil), so treat the capability as missing unless `ctx.capabilities.dialog` is true.

When a field is true, the corresponding calls behave as this document specifies and must not return `not_supported`. An app that cannot run without a capability lists it in the manifest's `requires`.

## Capability check for a required interface (2.18)

`ctx.capabilities.nn` must be true in a 2.18 normal session and is false on the lock screen; when true, `ctx.nn` exists, and when false it is nil (section 30). nn is a pure computation interface, not one of the optional capabilities in the table above that a host may leave out; the field exists for compatibility with older hosts and to tell sessions apart. On an older host without the field, treat it as unavailable.

# 18. Error codes

The second return value of a call is always one of these strings:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_argument` | The type is correct, but the value is outside the stated range |
| `not_found` | Nothing exists for that name |
| `io_error` | A storage, decode, or network read or write failed |
| `out_of_memory` | The host could not allocate memory for this call |
| `busy` | An operation of the same kind is already in progress |
| `invalid_handle` | The object has already been released or closed |
| `limit_exceeded` | A count, size, or (2.18 native inference) time limit stated in this document was exceeded |
| `inactive` | Not allowed at this time: the canvas has expired, `extend` was called outside a callback, or text input or a dialog was requested in a lock-screen session |
| `not_supported` | Returned only by `g:image` when `image_transform` is absent |

A network result's `err` can also be `no_network` or `timeout`. These appear only in the result table in section 14 and (2.6) in the WebSocket `on_close`.

The completion function of 2.18 native inference uses `invalid_argument` and `limit_exceeded`; an inference that runs past its deadline uses the latter, not the network-only `timeout`. Once the session has started ending, new inference is refused with `inactive`; a model that has already been closed still gets `invalid_handle` (section 30).

# 19. Versions

`ctx.api` is `{ major = 2, minor = <the minor the host implements> }`.

A 2.x minor version only adds: new calls, new optional capabilities, new device profiles, new `requires` names, new `locale` values, and new optional manifest fields. Parameters, return values, and error codes of existing calls do not change.

Suppose the host supports 2.m and the package writes `"api": "2.n"`. If `n <= m`, the package installs and runs; if `n > m`, installation is refused and the user is prompted to update the firmware. An incompatible change can only arrive in 3.0.

When the host also runs packages whose `api` is 0.x or 1.x, those packages follow their own older contracts. A 2.x package sees none of the names from those older contracts, except `ctx.state`, which 2.2 adds back in section 28.

**2.1** adds: sections 22–27; the manifest `permissions` name `reader`; the `requires` names `reader`, `dialog`, `frontlight`, and `image_decode`; `ctx.device.name`, `firmware`, and `id_for_app`; new fields of `battery()` and `radios()`; `align = "justify"`; runtime images (section 8). On a host that implements 2.1, `ctx.api.minor` is 1, and 2.0 packages can also see these new names. To keep a package installable on 2.0 devices, write `"2.0"` and check `ctx.api.minor >= 1` and `ctx.capabilities`.

**2.2** adds: section 28 (`ctx.state`, `ctx:save_state()`). On a host that implements 2.2, `ctx.api.minor` is 2, and 2.0 and 2.1 packages also have `ctx.state` and are saved automatically when a session ends.

**2.3** adds: `ctx.fonts:size(px, sample)` (section 7), which returns the preferred font at a given size without requiring you to choose a font, and falls back to a system font when there is no TTF; the preferred font is checked against the system language or `sample` (fixed in 2.3.1; 2.3.0 accepted only CJK fonts). On a host that implements 2.3, `ctx.api.minor` is 3, and 2.0–2.2 packages also have this function.

**2.4** adds: `ctx.net:keep_wifi(ms)` (section 14), which sets how long Wi-Fi that the host turned on for a request stays on after the last request ends. The default is 5 minutes, and -1 keeps it on for the whole session. On a host that implements 2.4, `ctx.api.minor` is 4, and 2.0–2.3 packages also have this function and also keep Wi-Fi on for the default 5 minutes.

**2.5** adds: `date_order` and `date_sep` in `ctx.clock:now()` (section 12), and `revision` also increments when the date format changes; the optional manifest field `display_names` (section 00); `toast` up to 95 bytes, wrapped to at most three lines (section 23); characters missing from a TTF are drawn with a system font (section 7). On a host that implements 2.5, `ctx.api.minor` is 5, and 2.0–2.4 packages also get these fields and behaviours.

**2.6** adds: `ctx.net:websocket(req, handlers)`, `ws:send`, and `ws:close` (section 14), a persistent two-way `ws://` or `wss://` connection; the host handles the heartbeat, and the connection does not reconnect automatically; and “How to build an online game” in section 14. Host behaviour: `request` reuses the connection to the same origin (“Connection reuse” in section 14), which also applies to 2.0–2.5 packages. On a host that implements 2.6, `ctx.api.minor` is 6, and 2.0–2.5 packages also have these functions.

**2.7** adds: `ui:focus(id)` and `ui:focused()` (section 16), so a script can set and read the UI library's focus, for example to return focus to the button that opened a screen when going back from it. Section 16 states that you can create several UI objects, each keeping its own focus (this has been true since 2.0). Host behaviour: when `back` is not handled, the host first shows an exit confirmation and exits only after the user confirms (“Exit confirmation” in section 4). On a host that implements 2.7, `ctx.api.minor` is 7, and 2.0–2.6 packages also have these two functions and get the exit confirmation.

**2.8** adds: `ctx.lockscreen:clear_default()`, `set_wallpaper(image)`, and `is_wallpaper()` (section 15), so an app can give the lock screen back, or set a picture (which may have transparency) as the lock-screen wallpaper drawn over the book page while reading (the cover; since 2.8.4, the user's original lock screen is shown when not reading); `ctx.reader:book_days(from, to)`, `ctx.reader:all_books()`, and `books_read` in `summary()` (section 22), which provide the reading time per book per day and every book ever read, all taken from the reading statistics; and the `image` and `border` fields of the UI library's `button` (section 16). On a host that implements 2.8, `ctx.api.minor` is 8, and 2.0–2.7 packages also have these functions and fields.

**2.9** adds: section 29 (`ctx.files`: `path`, `list`, `exists`, `size`, `read`, `write`, `append`, `remove`). `AppFiles/<app_id>/` on the storage card is this app's user-facing folder: the app can read files the user puts there from a computer or over phone transfer, the user can take away files the app writes, and neither uninstalling nor upgrading deletes them. It must be implemented, needs no permission, and the manifest does not change. Section 15 separates the lock screen from the cover: `set_default` and `set_wallpaper` can both be in effect without replacing each other, `clear_default` gives back only the lock screen, and the new `ctx.lockscreen:clear_wallpaper()` clears only the cover. On a host that implements 2.9, `ctx.api.minor` is 9, 2.0–2.8 packages also have `ctx.files` and `clear_wallpaper`, and the new lock-screen and cover rules apply to all packages. Section 4 docked input: `ctx.input:edit(opts)` with the edit object's `set_text`, `text`, and `close`, and `ctx.input.keyboard_h`. The system keyboard docks at the bottom of the app's screen to edit a piece of text in place, without changing pages or pausing the app, and `on_change` delivers the text as it is typed. Section 16 UI library text fields: `ui:field`, `ui:editing()`, and `ui:stop_edit()`. They must be implemented (`ui:field` is provided with the optional capability `ui`). A device without touch falls back to full-screen input, and the manifest does not change. 2.0–2.8 packages also have these functions.

**2.10** adds: section 4 "Physical keyboard" and `ctx.input:listen(opts)`. A Bluetooth keyboard that the user connects works without any change to the app: the arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Enter, Esc, and Backspace are delivered as ordinary keys, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, and `ok` in `ctx.input.keys` are true, and the user can type directly while docked input or full-page input (on a device with touch) is open. After the app calls `ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })`, it receives the full event for every key (`source`, `code`, `text`, `mods`, and `phase`, which may be `repeat`). It must be implemented. The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.10, `ctx.api.minor` is 10, 2.0–2.9 packages also have `listen`, and the keyboard's navigation keys and typing apply to all packages.

**2.11** adds: section 3 "Gray frames" and `ctx.screen.gray_still`. `gray = true` on `g:image` (section 6) makes the frame a full refresh with the grayscale waveform, showing `gray_still` gray steps. `gray = true` on `ctx.image:decode` (section 27) decodes a 4-level image. In a package whose manifest sets 2.11 or later, 4-level images are drawn in normal frames as a 4×4 dot pattern; 2.0–2.10 packages are still drawn with the threshold, so their output does not change. It must be implemented (`gray` is ignored on a device whose `gray_still` is 2). The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.11, `ctx.api.minor` is 11, and 2.0–2.10 packages also have `gray_still` and the `gray` option.

**2.12** adds: `ctx.device:display()` (section 13), which returns `{ dark }` to tell the app whether the system dark mode is on (when it is on, the host inverts the whole frame on screen). It must be implemented, needs no permission, the manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.12, `ctx.api.minor` is 12, and 2.0–2.11 packages can also call it.

**2.13** adds: UI library state, skins, custom areas, font shrinking, and position-based navigation (section 16): `ctx.ui:create(opts)` accepts `skins`; a control accepts `enabled`, `selected`, `emphasis`, `skin`, `font_min`, and `nav`; the new control `ui:region`. `g:image` adds `src`, which draws only part of the source image (section 6). It must be implemented (the UI library itself is still the optional capability `ui`). The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.13, `ctx.api.minor` is 13, and the new fields and `src` also work for 2.0–2.12 packages. Only position-based focus movement with the arrow keys depends on the manifest `api`: it takes effect when the manifest specifies 2.13 or later, and earlier packages still move focus in declaration order (skipping disabled controls).

**2.14** adds: UI library composite controls and badges (section 16): the new controls `ui:tabs`, `ui:radio`, `ui:stepper`, `ui:pager`, `ui:list`, and `ui:progress`; `button` accepts `align`, and `button` and `region` accept `badge`; `ui:skin` draws a skin on any canvas. `handle_event` gains one more return value: the item number of a composite control, or the new value for the new `change` action. `ui:focus` accepts an item, and `ui:focused` also returns the item. It must be implemented (the UI library itself is still the optional capability `ui`). The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.14, `ctx.api.minor` is 14, and the new controls and fields also work for 2.0–2.13 packages; when you do not use composite controls, the third return value of `handle_event` is nil and the behaviour does not change. Two drawing changes also affect old packages on new firmware: `switch` is drawn as a capsule instead of a square box (and accepts `note`, `skin`, and `radius`), and the `emphasis` button is filled instead of drawn with a border of line width 3; `tabs`, `stepper`, and `pager` accept `border = false`, and the stepper's minus and plus are drawn as a horizontal bar and a vertical bar.

**2.15** adds: UI library layout (section 16 "Layout (2.15)"). Field names and values follow CSS flexbox and grid: `row` and `column` accept `padding`, `row_gap`, `column_gap`, `justify_content`, `align_items` (including `baseline`), `wrap`, `align_content`, and `divider`, and children accept `grow`, `shrink`, `min_w`, `max_w`, `min_h`, `max_h`, `align_self`, `aspect_ratio`, and `hidden`; `w` and `h` accept `"fit"` or a percentage, or can be omitted; the new container `ui:grid` (tracks `columns`, `rows`, and `auto_rows` in pixels, `"fit"`, `fr`, or percentages, with row and column spanning and in-cell alignment); the stacking container `ui:stack`; container appearance `border`, `line_width`, `border_color`, `background`, `radius`, and `skin`; the child `spacer`; and `ui:layout`, which only computes rectangles (it can size by content and returns the overflow position `overflow`). It must be implemented (the UI library itself is still the optional capability `ui`). The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.15, `ctx.api.minor` is 15. The new layout depends only on the manifest `api`: it takes effect when the manifest specifies 2.15 or later. 2.0–2.14 packages still lay out by the old rules: the new fields are ignored, `ui:grid`, `ui:stack`, and `ui:layout` return `nil, "invalid_argument"`, and the output does not change.

**2.16** adds: `bold` and `tabular` for text (section 7 "Bold (2.16)" and "Tabular numerals (2.16)"), and `font:measure` accepts `opts`; line-start and line-end rules for `text_box` and `layout` (section 7 "Text box"); the UI library's bold default, tabular numerals, `reserve`, `selected_style` on `tabs`, `focus_style` on `ctx.ui:create`, and dot-pattern backgrounds (section 16 "Text hierarchy, dot patterns, and stable layout (2.16)"). It must be implemented (the UI library itself is still the optional capability `ui`). The manifest does not change, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added. On a host that implements 2.16, `ctx.api.minor` is 16. These changes depend only on the manifest `api`: they take effect when the manifest specifies 2.16 or later. In a 2.0–2.15 package, the new fields are ignored even if written, and wrapping, `layout`'s `consumed`, the switch and tab text, and the container's background colour stay the same as before.

**2.17** adds: the user chooses the font in system settings (section 7 "User-chosen font (2.17)"), in the toolbox ("More features" / "Ink App") under the top-right settings → font; when no font is chosen, the reader's body-text font is used. `ctx.fonts:size` tries the user-chosen font and then the reader's body-text font, and no longer tries MiSans or the other files in the font folder; the host allocates TTF memory and falls back to the system font when the font does not fit. On a host that implements 2.17, `ctx.api.minor` is 17, and the new font order also applies to 2.3–2.16 packages. The TTF font line box becomes ink-centred (section 7 "Line box and alignment"). Whatever version a package writes, `ctx.fonts.installed` and `ctx.fonts.open` are nil, `ctx.capabilities.ttf` is false, packages whose `requires` contains `ttf` cannot be opened, and the manifest's `ttf_reserve_kb` is still accepted but ignored. The manifest gains no fields, and no error codes, permissions, or capability names are added.

On a host at 2.16 or earlier, when `ctx.capabilities.ttf` is true, the host provides `ctx.fonts:installed()` (which lists the TTF names in the font folder) and `ctx.fonts:open(name, px)` (which opens a font by name; the 33rd combination returns `limit_exceeded`, a missing name returns `not_found`, a font that does not fit into `ttf_reserve_kb` returns `out_of_memory`, and a font that cannot be read returns `io_error`). TTF memory is allocated only when the package writes `ttf_reserve_kb` or its `requires` contains `ttf` (defaulting to 2048 KB when the package does not write it).

**2.18** adds: `ctx.device:keep_awake(ms)` (section 13 "Keep awake (2.18)"), which prevents idle auto power-off for `ms` milliseconds, up to 4 hours, and can be renewed; expiry, cancelling or the end of the session counts as a user action. It is required, needs no permission, and the manifest does not change; no new error codes, permissions or capability names. On a host that implements 2.18, `ctx.api.minor` is 18, and 2.0–2.17 packages can call it too.

**2.18** also extends `ctx.net:request` (section 14, proposal 0021): `method` adds `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `PROPFIND`, `PROPPATCH`, `MKCOL`, `COPY`, `MOVE` and `REPORT`, and every method except `GET` and `HEAD` may carry a `body`; `timeout_ms` takes 1000–60000, default 30000; `save` stores a 2xx body whole as a private file (up to 262144 bytes) or an app file (up to 8388608 bytes), and the result table adds `saved`. Hosts of 2.17 and earlier return `invalid_argument` for the new methods and ignore `timeout_ms` and `save`. It is required, and the manifest does not change; no new error codes, permissions or capability names.

**2.18** also adds `ctx.screen:set_orientation(o)` (section 3 "In-app orientation change (2.18)", proposal 0022): switches between portrait and landscape during a session; it takes effect after the current callback returns, and the next callback gets the new width and height with one full-refresh frame. It only applies to this session; when the session ends, the orientation from before the open is restored. It is required, needs no permission, and the manifest does not change (`display.orientation` still sets the orientation at open); no new error codes, permissions or capability names. 2.0–2.17 packages can call it too.

**2.18** also adds section 30, native inference (proposal 0025). It is required in the normal session and needs no permission. It adds the capability field `ctx.capabilities.nn`, the `requires` name `nn`, and the `ctx.nn:formats()` query, and supports FWNN v1/v2/v3 with F32LE data outside; v2 can use INT8/INT32 inside, and v3 adds compact I8 weights with F32 activations and accumulation. No new error codes and no separate hardware capability. In a lock-screen session, `ctx.nn` is nil and `ctx.capabilities.nn` is false.

# 20. Conformance tests

Each section has a corresponding set of test apps. The tests run on the host's simulator and on hardware, and the log prints `api2 <section> passed checks=<n>`. Drawing results are compared pixel by pixel against the golden image for each device profile.

A host that claims to support 2.m must pass every test except those in section 17, and must pass the tests for every optional capability it reports as true. A rule with no test cannot enter a release.

# 22. Reading data (2.1)

Requires the `reader` permission and the `reader` optional capability; otherwise `ctx.reader` is nil. Both the main program and lock-screen sessions can use it. It is read-only.

```lua
local books = ctx.reader:books()            -- recently read books, most recent first
local book  = ctx.reader:current()          -- the book being read, or the most recent; nil if there is none
local days  = ctx.reader:days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")
local sum   = ctx.reader:summary()
local cover, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id)
local rows  = ctx.reader:book_days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")   -- 2.8
local all   = ctx.reader:all_books()                              -- 2.8
```

**Books.** `books()` returns an array of at most 18 books, ordered by most recent reading. If there are no books, it returns an empty table. `current()` returns the book being read right now; otherwise it returns the most recently read book, or nil if no book has ever been read. Both return the same kind of table:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The book's id: an opaque string that is stable across sessions |
| `title` | Title |
| `author` | Author, or `""` when unknown |
| `format` | `"epub"`, `"txt"`, or `"xtc"`; more values may be added later |
| `percent` | Reading progress, an integer 0–100 |
| `page` `total_pages` | Page number and page count; nil before the book has been paginated |
| `finished` | Whether the book has been finished |
| `read_sec` | Total seconds spent reading this book |

**Time per day.** The dates of `days(from, to)` are `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings, inclusive at both ends, spanning at most 366 days. It returns an array with one item per day, `{ date, sec }`. Days with no reading are included, with `sec` 0. You can compute week, month, and year totals and bar charts from this array. A malformed date, a date that does not exist (such as 30 February), `from` later than `to`, or a range of more than 366 days returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

**Totals.** `summary()` returns:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `total_sec` | Total reading seconds |
| `today_sec` | Seconds read today; nil when the clock is not valid |
| `days_read` | Number of days on which something was read |
| `streak_days` `best_streak_days` | The current run of reading days, and the longest run |
| `books_finished` | Number of books finished |
| `books_read` | (2.8) Number of books read: books with a reading record in the reading statistics, including deleted ones |
| `first_date` | The date of the first reading record; nil when there is none |

**Cover.** `cover(id)` synchronously returns the cover already generated for this book (a runtime image, section 8) without opening the book file. The host chooses the size; scale it with the `w` and `h` of `g:image` when drawing. If `id` is unknown, or the book does not have a generated cover yet (it has never been shown on the shelf), it returns `nil, "not_found"`.

**Time per book per day (2.8).** The dates of `book_days(from, to)` follow the same rules as `days`. It returns an array of `{ date, id, title, sec }` items, each meaning that on `date` the book was read for `sec` seconds (greater than 0). Days without reading have no items. Items are ordered by date, earliest first; within a day, the book read longest comes first. `id` matches that book's `id` in `books()`, and `title` is the title recorded in the reading statistics. A malformed date returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Out of memory returns `nil, "out_of_memory"`.

**Every book read (2.8).** `all_books()` returns every book that has a reading record in the reading statistics, most recently read first, without the limit of 18 (the statistics keep at most 512 books). Each item:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` `title` | Same as in `book_days` |
| `sec` | Total reading seconds |
| `first_date` `last_date` | The first and last dates the book was read, `"YYYY-MM-DD"` |
| `finished` | Whether the book has been finished |

It reads only the statistics and does not scan the storage card, so it remains fast even with many books. Books whose files have been deleted are still listed. If there are no records, it returns an empty table. Out of memory returns `nil, "out_of_memory"`. The number of books equals `summary().books_read`.

A failed read returns `nil, "io_error"`.
entries.example:
local books = ctx.reader:books()            -- recently read books, most recent first
local book  = ctx.reader:current()          -- the book being read, or the most recent; nil if there is none
local days  = ctx.reader:days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")
local sum   = ctx.reader:summary()
local cover, err = ctx.reader:cover(book.id)
local rows  = ctx.reader:book_days("2026-10-05", "2026-10-11")   -- 2.8
local all   = ctx.reader:all_books()                              -- 2.8

# 23. System dialogs (2.1)

Optional capability `dialog`.

```lua
ctx.dialog:confirm({ title = "Delete the record", message = "This cannot be undone.", ok_text = "Delete" },
  function(ctx, ok) if ok then remove_record() end end)

ctx.dialog:choose({ title = "Sort", items = { "By time", "By name" }, selected = 1 },
  function(ctx, index) if index then sort_by = index; ctx:invalidate() end end)

ctx.dialog:toast("Saved")
```

`confirm` and `choose` behave like text input in section 4: after the current callback returns, the host opens the dialog and the app receives `on_pause`; after the user makes a choice, the app receives `on_resume`, and then the completion function is called once as a callback. While the dialog is open, the app receives no input events. Back acts as cancel.

| Call | Fields | Second argument of the completion function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `title` (≤ 95 bytes), `message` (≤ 191), `ok_text`, `cancel_text` (each ≤ 63; defaults to the system's Confirm and Cancel) | true on confirm, false on cancel |
| `choose` | `title`, `items` (1–7 strings, each ≤ 63 bytes, required), `selected` (1-based row, may be omitted) | the selected row (1-based), or nil on cancel |

`toast(text)` shows a message on the screen for about 2 seconds without interrupting the app, and returns nothing. `text` is at most 95 bytes (47 bytes in 2.4 and earlier). If it does not fit on one line the host wraps it to at most three lines, and ends it with "..." if it still does not fit. On a host that implements 2.5, 2.1–2.4 packages may also use up to 95 bytes; for the text to display on older hosts as well, stay within 47 bytes or check `ctx.api.minor >= 5`.

They return nothing. Text that is too long returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An empty `items`, or a `selected` outside the list, returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. If a dialog, a text input, or (2.9) a docked input has not finished, the call returns `nil, "busy"`. In a lock-screen session, the call returns `nil, "inactive"`. When the session ends, an unfinished dialog is cancelled and the completion function is not called.

# 24. Front light (2.1)

Optional capability `frontlight`: `ctx.frontlight` exists when the device has a front light; otherwise it is nil. It is nil in a lock-screen session.

```lua
local f = ctx.frontlight:get()                       -- { on, brightness, warmth }
ctx.frontlight:set({ on = true, brightness = 20 })   -- write only the fields to change
ctx.frontlight:reset()                               -- back to the user's settings
```

`brightness` and `warmth` are integers 0–100 (for `warmth`, 0 is the coolest and 100 the warmest). `set` lasts only for this session and does not change system settings. `get` returns the values the app set. When the session ends (including entering the lock screen), the host calls `reset` automatically. If the system's night mode is running, `reset` hands the front light back to night mode. On a device without a warm light, `warmth` is always 0, and values written to it are ignored.

`set` and `reset` return nothing. An out-of-range value returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

# 25. Opening a system page (2.1)

```lua
if not online and ctx.system:can_open("settings.wifi") then
  ctx.system:open("settings.wifi")
end
```

After the current callback returns, `open` ends this session (calling `on_leave`) and opens a system page. When the user comes back from that page, the app opens again as an entirely new session. To continue work after that, write it in `on_leave` to a file from section 9, or (2.2) keep it in `ctx.state` from section 28.

| Target | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `"settings.wifi"` | Wi-Fi settings |
| `"settings.bluetooth"` | Bluetooth settings |

Later minor versions only add targets. `can_open(target)` returns a boolean: it is false for an unknown target and in a lock-screen session, and in those cases `open` returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A successful `open` returns nothing.
entries.example:
if not online and ctx.system:can_open("settings.wifi") then
  ctx.system:open("settings.wifi")
end

# 26. Encoding, hashes, and random bytes (2.1)

Required. Arguments and results are byte strings.

```lua
ctx.base64:encode(s, opts)   ctx.base64:decode(s)
ctx.hex:encode(s)            ctx.hex:decode(s)
ctx.url:encode(s)            ctx.url:decode(s)
ctx.url:query(t)             -- { q = "eink", page = 2 } -> "page=2&q=eink"

ctx.hash:sha256(s)  ctx.hash:sha1(s)  ctx.hash:md5(s)
ctx.hash:hmac_sha256(key, s)
ctx.hash:crc32(s)

ctx.random:bytes(n)
ctx.random:uuid()
```

- **base64**: uses the RFC 4648 standard alphabet, padded with `=`. When `opts.url` is true, the `-` `_` alphabet is used without padding. `decode` accepts both alphabets, and padding may be omitted.
- **hex**: `encode` outputs lowercase. `decode` accepts either case, and the length must be even.
- **url**: `encode` writes every byte outside `A–Z a–z 0–9 - . _ ~` as `%XX` (a space becomes `%20`). `decode` only decodes `%XX`; `+` is left unchanged. The keys of `query(t)` must be strings, and the values strings, numbers, or booleans. Items are joined in the byte order of the keys, and both keys and values are encoded with `encode`. An empty table yields `""`. At most 64 items are allowed.
- **hash**: returns the raw digest bytes (32 bytes for SHA-256, 20 for SHA-1, 16 for MD5), the same as Python `hashlib` `digest()`. For hexadecimal output, write `ctx.hex:encode(ctx.hash:sha256(s))`. `hmac_sha256` follows RFC 2104. `crc32` matches zlib `crc32`, but it is returned as a signed 32-bit integer (values above `0x7FFFFFFF` are negative).
- **random**: `bytes(n)` returns `n` hardware-random bytes, where `n` is an integer 1–1024. `uuid()` returns a version-4 UUID string (lowercase, with `-`). These are suitable for tokens and random seeds; `math.random` is not.

Input is limited to 1048576 bytes; longer input returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An illegal character or an incorrect length during decoding returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Encryption and decryption are not provided.
entries.example:
ctx.base64:encode(s, opts)   ctx.base64:decode(s)
ctx.hex:encode(s)            ctx.hex:decode(s)
ctx.url:encode(s)            ctx.url:decode(s)
ctx.url:query(t)             -- { q = "eink", page = 2 } -> "page=2&q=eink"

ctx.hash:sha256(s)  ctx.hash:sha1(s)  ctx.hash:md5(s)
ctx.hash:hmac_sha256(key, s)
ctx.hash:crc32(s)

ctx.random:bytes(n)
ctx.random:uuid()

# 27. Decompression, QR codes, and image decode (2.1)

```lua
local text = ctx.zlib:decompress(res.body)                     -- recognizes gzip or zlib
local code = ctx.qr:encode("https://example.com/r/42", { size = 240 })
local img  = ctx.image:decode(res.body, { max_w = 96, max_h = 96 })   -- optional capability image_decode
```

**Decompression** (required). `opts.format` is `"auto"` (the default), `"gzip"`, `"zlib"`, or `"raw"` (raw deflate). For gzip, the CRC-32 and the length at the end are checked. The result is at most 1048576 bytes; longer output returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. Damaged data or the wrong format returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Decompression needs about 70 KB of work space plus the size of the result; when the script heap cannot hold it, `not enough memory` is raised as in section 1, which `pcall` can catch. Compression is not provided.

**QR codes** (required). Returns a black-and-white runtime image (section 8) with a white margin of 4 modules on every side. `opts.size` is the desired side length in pixels (21–4096, default 200). The host uses the largest whole-number module size that does not exceed it; the actual side length is `code.width`. `opts.ecc` is `"low"`, `"medium"` (the default), `"quartile"`, or `"high"`. The content is at most 1024 bytes and contains no `\0`. If the content does not fit (too much content, or `size` smaller than the module count plus the white margin), the call returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`.

**Image decode** (optional capability `image_decode`). Decodes PNG, JPEG, or BMP bytes into a runtime image, dithers it to the device's gray levels, and scales it proportionally to fit within `max_w × max_h` (1–4096, default the screen size). (2.18, a host fix that applies to packages of every version) When a PNG carries transparency (an alpha channel or `tRNS`), the decoded image has 1-bit transparency: after scaling, pixels less than 50% opaque are transparent and the rest are dithered by color without blending with the background, the same as PNG resources in the package (section 6, appendix A); `g:image`, layers, and `ctx.lockscreen:set_wallpaper` all honor it. A source image that is fully opaque carries no transparency; JPEG and BMP are always opaque. The transparency takes `ceil(w / 8)` bytes per row and counts toward the total runtime image bytes in section 8. (2.11) When `opts.gray` is true and `ctx.screen.gray_still` is 4, it decodes a 4-level image (colors 0, 5, 10, 15) for display in a gray frame; in a normal frame, the image is drawn as a dot pattern (section 3). When `gray_still` is 2, it still decodes to black and white. A `gray` value that is not a boolean returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. The call runs synchronously, and its time counts against the current callback. A source image whose width or height exceeds 1024 returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. An unrecognized format returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Insufficient memory returns `nil, "out_of_memory"`. When used with section 14: a response body keeps at most 131072 bytes, so the server must reduce larger pictures first.
entries.example:
local text = ctx.zlib:decompress(res.body)                     -- recognizes gzip or zlib
local code = ctx.qr:encode("https://example.com/r/42", { size = 240 })
local img  = ctx.image:decode(res.body, { max_w = 96, max_h = 96 })   -- optional capability image_decode
